title: Naiṣkarmyasiddhi — Complete Sanskrit Reader
author: Sureśvara
coverage: Complete Sanskrit source and original English translation for all 1178 reader units. All 100 numbered verses of Adhyāya 1 and verses 2.1–2.20, plus verses 3.114, 3.123, and 4.43, now show complete shlokas, transliteration, translation, and word-by-word glosses; the remaining 300 numbered verses and prose commentary still need separate gloss work.

sections.title: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self

source.edition: Sanskrit Wikisource text compiled and transliterated by the ERC-funded Intellexus project.
source.changes: Complete source body arranged as a local reader, preserving all four chapter boundaries. IAST is converted to Devanāgarī in the reader, and the source's final colophon is retained. Original English translations are included throughout. All 100 verses of Adhyāya 1 and verses 2.1–2.20 now have complete shloka text, IAST, meaning-aligned translations, and word-by-word glosses; four formerly split or missing entries (1.100, 3.114, 3.123, 4.43) have also been restored. Prose commentary passages still need separate lexical glosses. Verse 2.5 follows Alston's reading that the sentence does not conflict with the listed referents; verse 2.20 renders the four-bearer image.

units.label: Chapter heading
units.translation: Now begins the first chapter.

units.label: Text 2
units.deva: आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तैः सर्वप्राणिभिः सर्वप्रकारस्यापि दुःखस्य स्वरसत एव जिहासितत्वात्तन्निवृत्त्यर्था प्रवृत्तिरस्ति स्वरसत एव ।
units.iast: ābrahmastambaparyantaiḥ sarvaprāṇibhiḥ sarvaprakārasyāpi duḥkhasya svarasata eva jihāsitatvāttannivṛttyarthā pravṛttirasti svarasata eva |
units.translation: All living beings, from Brahmā to a clump of grass, naturally wish to abandon suffering of every kind. Their action is naturally for its cessation.

gloss.en: from Brahmā to a clump of grass

units.editionTranslation: All beings, from Brahmā down to a clump of grass, naturally wish to be rid of suffering of every kind; therefore they naturally act for its cessation.

units.label: Text 3
units.translation: Suffering does not cease: taking a body is its sole cause, and the body is rooted in merit and demerit accumulated before.

gloss.en: because taking a body is the sole cause
because rooted in merit and demerit

units.editionTranslation: Suffering has the body as its sole basis, and the body is rooted in merit and demerit accumulated previously; therefore suffering does not cease.

units.label: Text 4
units.translation: They do not cease because those two [merit and demerit] are rooted in prescribed and forbidden actions.
units.editionTranslation: Those two are rooted in prescribed and prohibited action, and so they do not cease.

units.label: Text 5
units.translation: Action rests on attachment and aversion; these arise from imagining things to be desirable or undesirable. That superimposition is grounded in an unexamined assumption of duality. All duality persists because the naturally evident, non-dual Self is not known—just as silver is imagined in a shell.

units.label: Text 6
units.deva: अतः सर्वानर्थहेतुरात्मानवबोध एव । सुखस्य चानागमापायिनोऽपरतन्त्रस्यात्मस्वभावत्वात्तस्यानवबोधः पिधानम् । अतस्तस्यात्यन्तोच्छित्तावशेषपुरुषार्थपरिसमाप्तिः । अज्ञाननिवृत्तेश्च सम्यग्ज्ञानस्वरूपलाभमात्रहेतुत्वात्तदुपादानम् । अशेषानर्थहेत्वात्मानवबोधविषयस्य चानागमिकप्रत्यक्षादिलौकिकप्रमाणाविषयत्वाद्वेदान्तागमवाक्यादेव सम्यग्ज्ञानम् ।
units.iast: ataḥ sarvānarthaheturātmānavabodha eva | sukhasya cānāgamāpāyino'paratantrasyātmasvabhāvatvāttasyānavabodhaḥ pidhānam | atastasyātyantocchittāvaśeṣapuruṣārthaparisamāptiḥ | ajñānanivṛtteśca samyagjñānasvarūpalābhamātrahetutvāttadupādānam | aśeṣānarthahetvātmānavabodhaviṣayasya cānāgamikapratyakṣādilaukikapramāṇāviṣayatvādvedāntāgamavākyādeva samyagjñānam |
units.translation: Therefore ignorance of the Self alone is the cause of every ill. Happiness, which neither comes nor goes and depends on nothing else, is the Self’s own nature; ignorance veils it. When ignorance is wholly destroyed, every human aim is fulfilled. Ignorance is removed only by the attainment of right knowledge. Since the Self, the cause of every ill, is not an object of ordinary means of knowledge such as perception, right knowledge arises only from the words of the Vedānta.

units.label: Text 7
units.translation: Therefore this treatise, which gathers the essence of all Vedānta, is begun.

units.label: Text 8
units.translation: To set out the desired end and state the subject of the treatise in brief, this is the opening verse.

units.label: Verse 1.1
units.deva: खानिलाग्न्यब्धरित्र्यन्तं स्रक्फणीवोद्गतं यतः । ध्वान्तच्छिदे नमस्तस्मै हरये बुद्धिसाक्षिणे ॥ १॥
units.iast: khānilāgnyabdharitryantaṃ srakphaṇīvodgataṃ yataḥ | dhvāntacchide namastasmai haraye buddhisākṣiṇe || 1||
units.translation: From whom the world—from space, wind, fire, and water through earth—arises like a snake imagined in a garland. Salutation to that Hari, the witness of the intellect and destroyer of darkness.

gloss.en: to the witness of the intellect

units.label: Text 11
units.translation: The teacher is saluted after his distinctive qualities are recounted, to show that the authority of our own tradition rests on the authority already taught.

units.label: Verse 1.2
units.translation: From whom water and the other elements turned back, finding no one greater: salutation to that greater one, the breaker of ignorance’s knot.

gloss.en: to the breaker of ignorance’s knot

units.label: Text 14
units.translation: This verse discloses the intention that prompted the salutation.

units.label: Verse 1.3
units.deva: वेदान्तोदरसंगूढं संसारोत्सारि वस्तुगम् । ज्ञानं व्याकृतमप्यन्यैर्वक्ष्ये गुर्वनुशिक्षया ॥ ३॥
units.iast: vedāntodarasaṃgūḍhaṃ saṃsārotsāri vastugam | jñānaṃ vyākṛtamapyanyairvakṣye gurvanuśikṣayā || 3||
units.translation: Though others have explained it, I shall explain under my teacher’s instruction the knowledge hidden in the heart of the Vedānta, which drives away saṃsāra and leads to reality.

gloss.en: hidden in the heart of the Vedānta

units.label: Text 17
units.translation: If it is asked, “What is the subject of this treatise?”, it is now stated:

units.label: Verse 1.4
units.deva: यत्सिद्धाविदमः सिद्धिर्यदसिद्धौ न किंचन । प्रत्यग्धर्मैकनिष्ठस्य याथात्म्यं वक्ष्यते स्फुटम् ॥ ४॥
units.iast: yatsiddhāvidamaḥ siddhiryadasiddhau na kiṃcana | pratyagdharmaikaniṣṭhasya yāthātmyaṃ vakṣyate sphuṭam || 4||
units.translation: When that is realized, this [world] is understood; when it is not realized, nothing [is truly known]. The true nature of one devoted solely to the inward reality will be clearly set forth.

gloss.en: of one devoted solely to the inward reality

units.label: Text 20
units.translation: To encourage attention to the intended subject, the authority of the teacher is described after removing doubts that he is unauthoritative because of omissions, errors, or other defects.

units.label: Verse 1.5
units.deva: गुरूक्तो वेदराद्धान्तस्तत्र नो वच्म्यशक्तितः । सहस्रकिरणव्याप्ते खद्योतः किं प्रकाशयेत् ॥ ५॥
units.iast: gurūkto vedarāddhāntastatra no vacmyaśaktitaḥ | sahasrakiraṇavyāpte khadyotaḥ kiṃ prakāśayet || 5||
units.translation: I cannot set forth the settled teaching of the Veda spoken by my teacher, because of my inability. What could a firefly illumine when the thousand-rayed [sun] shines everywhere?

gloss.en: the settled teaching of the Veda
when [all] is pervaded by a thousand rays

units.label: Text 23
units.translation: If one objects, “Since the teacher has already completed the exposition of the Veda’s meaning, a treatise by you may be suspected of being unauthoritative, prompted by fame and the like,” he replies to dispel that doubt:

units.label: Verse 1.6
units.translation: We do not put forward this treatise for fame, gain, or honor. It is for purifying our own understanding, tested against the touchstones of those who know Brahman.

units.label: Text 26
units.translation: The subject is introduced to summarize the treatise’s subject, the human aim, and its cause.

units.label: Verse 1.7
units.deva: ऐकात्म्याप्रतिपत्तिर्या स्वात्मानुभवसंश्रया । साऽविद्या संसृतेर्बीजं तन्नाशो मुक्तिरात्मनः ॥ ७॥
units.iast: aikātmyāpratipattiryā svātmānubhavasaṃśrayā | sā'vidyā saṃsṛterbījaṃ tannāśo muktirātmanaḥ || 7||
units.translation: Failure to realize oneness, grounded in the experience of one’s own Self, is ignorance, the seed of transmigration; its destruction is liberation for the Self.

gloss.en: is grounded in the experience of one’s own Self

units.label: Text 28
units.translation: Since the human end remains to be stated, it is now expressed.

units.label: Verse 1.8
units.translation: The fire of right knowledge arising from the final words of the Veda burns away delusion about the Self; action does not oppose it.

gloss.en: arising from the final words of the Veda

units.label: Text 31
units.translation: An opponent’s position is stated in order to clarify the thesis.

units.label: Text 32
units.translation: First, the argument proceeds while provisionally admitting knowledge.

units.label: Verse 1.9
units.deva: मुक्तेः क्रियाभिः सिद्धत्वाज्ज्ञानं तत्र करोति किम् । कथं चेच्छृणु तत्सर्वं प्रणिधाय मनो यथा ॥ ९॥
units.iast: mukteḥ kriyābhiḥ siddhatvājjñānaṃ tatra karoti kim | kathaṃ cecchṛṇu tatsarvaṃ praṇidhāya mano yathā || 9||
units.translation: If liberation is accomplished by actions, what does knowledge do there? If you ask how, listen to the whole account with your mind attentively fixed.

units.label: Verse 1.10
units.deva: अकुर्वतः क्रियाः काम्या निषिद्धास्त्यजतस्तथा । नित्यनैमित्तिकं कर्म विधिवच्चानुतिष्ठतः ॥ १०॥
units.iast: akurvataḥ kriyāḥ kāmyā niṣiddhāstyajatastathā | nityanaimittikaṃ karma vidhivaccānutiṣṭhataḥ || 10||
units.translation: One who refrains from desire-motivated actions and abandons prohibited ones, while duly carrying out obligatory and occasion-based duties—

units.label: Text 37
units.translation: what follows from that?

units.label: Verse 1.11
units.deva: काम्यकर्मफलं तस्माद्देवादीमं न ढौकते । निषिद्धस्य निरस्तत्वान्नारकीं नैत्यधोजनिम् ॥ ११॥
units.iast: kāmyakarmaphalaṃ tasmāddevādīmaṃ na ḍhaukate | niṣiddhasya nirastatvānnārakīṃ naityadhojanim || 11||
units.translation: The fruits of desire-motivated action, even those beginning with the gods, do not reach him; because prohibited action has been set aside, he does not enter a hellish lower birth.

gloss.en: beginning with the gods; such as heaven
because it has been set aside

units.label: Text 40
units.deva: देहारम्भकयोश्च धर्माधर्मयोर्ज्ञानिना सह कर्मिणः समानौ चोद्यपरिहारौ ।
units.iast: dehārambhakayośca dharmādharmayorjñāninā saha karmiṇaḥ samānau codyaparihārau |
units.translation: The objection and its answer concerning merit and demerit—which cause the body—are the same for the man of knowledge and for the ritualist.

units.label: Verse 1.12
units.deva: वर्तमानमिदं याभ्यां शरीरं सुखदुःखदम् । आरब्धं पुण्यपापाभ्यां भोगादेव तयोः क्षयः ॥ १२॥
units.iast: vartamānamidaṃ yābhyāṃ śarīraṃ sukhaduḥkhadam | ārabdhaṃ puṇyapāpābhyāṃ bhogādeva tayoḥ kṣayaḥ || 12||
units.translation: This present body, which gives pleasure and pain, was brought about by merit and demerit; those two are exhausted only through experience.

units.label: Text 43
units.deva: काम्यप्रतिषिद्धकर्मफलत्वात्संसारस्य तन्निरासेनैवाशेषानर्थनिरासस्य सिद्धत्वात्किं नित्यानुष्ठानेनेति चेत्तन्न । तदकरणादप्यनर्थप्रसक्तेः ।
units.iast: kāmyapratiṣiddhakarmaphalatvātsaṃsārasya tannirāsenaivāśeṣānarthanirāsasya siddhatvātkiṃ nityānuṣṭhāneneti cettanna | tadakaraṇādapyanarthaprasakteḥ |
units.translation: If one objects, “Since saṃsāra results from desire-driven and forbidden actions, and removing those alone removes every ill, why perform obligatory rites?”, that is wrong: omitting them also leads to harm.

units.label: Verse 1.13
units.deva: नित्यानुष्ठानतश्चैनं प्रत्यवायो न संस्पृशेत् । अनादृत्यात्मविज्ञानमतः कर्माणि संश्रयेत् ॥ १३॥
units.iast: nityānuṣṭhānataścainaṃ pratyavāyo na saṃspṛśet | anādṛtyātmavijñānamataḥ karmāṇi saṃśrayet || 13||
units.translation: No adverse result from omission would touch him through performance of obligatory duties; therefore, disregarding knowledge of the Self, he should rely on actions.

units.label: Text 46
units.deva: अभ्युपेत्यैवमुच्यते न तु यथावस्थितात्मवस्तुविषयं ज्ञानमस्ति । तत्प्रतिपादकप्रमाणाभावात् ।
units.iast: abhyupetyaivamucyate na tu yathāvasthitātmavastuviṣayaṃ jñānamasti | tatpratipādakapramāṇābhāvāt |
units.translation: This is said only for the sake of argument; in truth, there is no knowledge of the Self as it really is, because there is no means of knowledge that teaches it.

units.label: Verse 1.14
units.deva: यावन्त्यश्चेह विद्यन्ते श्रुतयस्स्मृतिभिस्सह । विदधत्युरुयत्नेन कर्मातो भूरिसाधनम् ॥ १४॥
units.iast: yāvantyaśceha vidyante śrutayassmṛtibhissaha | vidadhatyuruyatnena karmāto bhūrisādhanam || 14||
units.translation: All the Vedic texts here, together with traditional texts, prescribe action with great insistence; action, therefore, has many means in its favor.

units.label: Text 49
units.translation: If one says, “Knowledge could be authoritative; the fault may lie with you,” that is not so, because:

units.label: Verse 1.15
units.deva: यत्नतो वीक्षमाणोऽपि विधिं ज्ञानस्य न क्वचित् । श्रुतौ स्मृतौ वा पश्यामि विश्वासो नान्यतोऽस्ति नः ॥ १५॥
units.iast: yatnato vīkṣamāṇo'pi vidhiṃ jñānasya na kvacit | śrutau smṛtau vā paśyāmi viśvāso nānyato'sti naḥ || 15||
units.translation: Even when I search carefully, I find no injunction for knowledge anywhere in the Veda or traditional texts; we place our trust in no other source.

units.label: Text 52
units.translation: If one says that action can arise without an injunction, as it does in ordinary life, that is not so, because:

units.label: Verse 1.16
units.deva: अन्तरेण विधिं मोहाद्यः कुर्यात्साम्परायिकम् । न तत्स्यादुपकाराय भस्मनीव हुतं हविः ॥ १६॥
units.iast: antareṇa vidhiṃ mohādyaḥ kuryātsāmparāyikam | na tatsyādupakārāya bhasmanīva hutaṃ haviḥ || 16||
units.translation: Whoever, through confusion, performs an otherworldly rite without an injunction gains no benefit from it, like an oblation offered into ashes.

units.label: Text 55
units.translation: This also follows from the teaching of Jaimini, who accepts the authority of the Veda.

units.label: Verse 1.17
units.translation: “Because the Veda is intended for action, it would otherwise be purposeless”—thus Jaimini himself, the knower of the Veda, says aloud and emphatically.

units.label: Text 58
units.translation: And from the wording of the mantra:

units.label: Verse 1.18
units.deva: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः । इति मन्त्रोऽपि निश्शेषं कर्मण्यायुरवासृजत् ॥ १८॥
units.iast: kurvanneveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchataṃ samāḥ | iti mantro'pi niśśeṣaṃ karmaṇyāyuravāsṛjat || 18||
units.translation: “By performing actions here alone, one should wish to live a hundred years”—thus the mantra, too, assigned one’s entire life to action.

units.label: Text 61
units.translation: Since the knower accepts the authority of sentences about existing things, while sentences are chiefly governed by action-words, the knowledge intended here does not arise.

units.label: Verse 1.19
units.deva: विरहय्य क्रियां नैव संहन्यन्ते पदान्यपि । न समस्त्यपदं वाक्यं यत्स्याज्ज्ञानविधायकम् ॥ १९॥
units.iast: virahayya kriyāṃ naiva saṃhanyante padānyapi | na samastyapadaṃ vākyaṃ yatsyājjñānavidhāyakam || 19||
units.translation: Without an action-word, words do not form a sentence; there is no verb-less sentence that could prescribe knowledge.

units.label: Text 64
units.translation: Even if knowledge is admitted, there is no defect, because:

units.label: Verse 1.20
units.translation: Whether knowledge is treated as action’s subsidiary or as principal in its own right, their relationship is established here; even when knowledge is present, there is no defect.

gloss.en: in a subsidiary-part and principal-whole relation
as principal in its own right

units.label: Text 67
units.translation: For, whether knowledge is admitted or not, liberation does not arise from knowledge.

units.label: Verse 1.21
units.deva: अतः सर्वाश्रमाणां हि वाङ्मनःकायकर्मभिः । स्वनुष्ठितैर्यथाशक्ति मुक्तिः स्यान्नान्यसाधनात् ॥ २१॥
units.iast: ataḥ sarvāśramāṇāṃ hi vāṅmanaḥkāyakarmabhiḥ | svanuṣṭhitairyathāśakti muktiḥ syānnānyasādhanāt || 21||
units.translation: Therefore, for people in every stage of life, liberation may come through actions of speech, mind, and body performed to the best of their ability; there is no other means.

units.label: Text 70
units.translation: He says this to show that the claim is only foolish talk:

units.label: Verse 1.22
units.deva: इति हृष्टधियां वाचः स्वप्रज्ञाऽऽध्मातचेतसाम् । घुष्यन्ते यज्ञशालासु धूमानद्धधियां किल ॥ २२॥
units.iast: iti hṛṣṭadhiyāṃ vācaḥ svaprajñā''dhmātacetasām | ghuṣyante yajñaśālāsu dhūmānaddhadhiyāṃ kila || 22||
units.translation: So, in sacrificial halls, the words of those pleased with their own opinions and puffed up by their own cleverness are proclaimed by people whose minds are clouded with smoke.

gloss.en: of those whose minds are puffed up by their own cleverness
of those whose minds are covered by smoke

units.label: Text 73
units.translation: He now indicates the scope of the refutation:

units.label: Verse 1.23
units.deva: अत्राभिदध्महे दोषान् क्रमशो न्यायबृंहितैः । वचोभिः पूर्वपक्षोक्तिघातिभिर्नातिसंभ्रमात् ॥ २३॥
units.iast: atrābhidadhmahe doṣān kramaśo nyāyabṛṃhitaiḥ | vacobhiḥ pūrvapakṣoktighātibhirnātisaṃbhramāt || 23||
units.translation: Here we will point out the faults one by one, with arguments strengthened by reasoning and with words that refute the opponent’s claim, without undue confusion.

gloss.en: that refute the stated opposing view

units.label: Text 76
units.translation: Liberation cannot be produced by action, since none of the four kinds of products of action can constitute liberation.

units.label: Verse 1.24
units.deva: अज्ञानहानमात्रत्वान्मुक्तेः कर्म न साधनम् । कर्मापमार्ष्टि नाज्ञानं तमसीवोत्थितं तमः ॥ २४॥
units.iast: ajñānahānamātratvānmukteḥ karma na sādhanam | karmāpamārṣṭi nājñānaṃ tamasīvotthitaṃ tamaḥ || 24||
units.translation: Because liberation is only the removal of ignorance, action is not its means. Action does not remove ignorance, just as darkness cannot remove darkness.

gloss.en: because liberation is only the removal of ignorance

units.label: Text 79
units.translation: Even if liberation were accepted as the product of action, there would still be a defect.

units.label: Verse 1.25
units.deva: एकेन वा भवेन्मुक्तिर्यदि वा सर्वकर्मभिः । प्रत्येकं चेद्वृथान्यानि सर्वेभ्योऽप्येककर्मता ॥ २५॥
units.iast: ekena vā bhavenmuktiryadi vā sarvakarmabhiḥ | pratyekaṃ cedvṛthānyāni sarvebhyo'pyekakarmatā || 25||
units.translation: Liberation would then come either from one action or from all actions. If each action worked separately, the others would be useless; if liberation came from all of them, they would amount to one action.

gloss.en: the state of being one action

units.label: Text 82
units.deva: सर्वप्रकारस्यापि कर्मण उत्पत्तित एव विशिष्टसाध्याभिसंबन्धान्न परिशेष्यन्यायसिद्धिः ।
units.iast: sarvaprakārasyāpi karmaṇa utpattita eva viśiṣṭasādhyābhisaṃbandhānna pariśeṣyanyāyasiddhiḥ |
units.translation: Every action, of every kind, is connected from its very origin with a particular result to be accomplished; therefore it cannot be made to serve an unrelated end by the principle of residue.

units.label: Verse 1.26
units.deva: दुरितक्षपणार्थत्वान्न नित्यं स्याद्विमुक्तये । स्वर्गादिफलसंबन्धात्काम्यं कर्म तथैव न ॥ २६॥
units.iast: duritakṣapaṇārthatvānna nityaṃ syādvimuktaye | svargādiphalasaṃbandhātkāmyaṃ karma tathaiva na || 26||
units.translation: An obligatory rite is not a means to liberation merely because it aims to destroy sin; a desire-driven rite is not a means either, since it is tied to results such as heaven.

gloss.en: because it aims to destroy sin
because it is tied to results such as heaven

units.label: Text 85
units.translation: And there is no valid means of knowledge for this claim.

units.label: Verse 1.27
units.deva: साध्यसाधनभावोऽयं वचनात्पारलौकिकः । नाश्रौषं मोक्षदं कर्म श्रुतेर्वक्त्रात्कथंचन ॥ २७॥
units.iast: sādhyasādhanabhāvo'yaṃ vacanātpāralaukikaḥ | nāśrauṣaṃ mokṣadaṃ karma śrutervaktrātkathaṃcana || 27||
units.translation: The relation between means and result in the other world is known from scripture. Yet I have never heard, from scripture’s mouth, of an action that grants liberation.

gloss.en: the relation between an end and its means

units.label: Text 88
units.translation: Since you merely repeat what has already been admitted, your speech is pointless—like telling a mother-in-law, “Go out!”

units.label: Verse 1.28
units.deva: निषिद्धकाम्ययोस्त्यागस्त्वयापीष्टो यथा मया । नित्यस्याफलवत्त्वाच्च न मोक्षः कर्मसाधनः ॥ २८॥
units.iast: niṣiddhakāmyayostyāgastvayāpīṣṭo yathā mayā | nityasyāphalavattvācca na mokṣaḥ karmasādhanaḥ || 28||
units.translation: You, as I do, approve abandoning prohibited and desire-driven actions. Since obligatory action bears no result, liberation is not accomplished by action.

units.label: Text 91
units.deva: एवं तावत् "मुक्तेः क्रियाभिः सिद्धत्वात् " इति निरस्तोऽयं पक्षः । अथाधुना सर्वकर्मप्रवृत्तिहेतुनिरूपणेन यथावस्थितात्मवस्तुविषयकेवलज्ञानमात्रादेव सकलसंसारानर्थनिवृत्तिरितीमं पक्षं द्रढयितुकाम आह ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvat "mukteḥ kriyābhiḥ siddhatvāt " iti nirasto'yaṃ pakṣaḥ | athādhunā sarvakarmapravṛttihetunirūpaṇena yathāvasthitātmavastuviṣayakevalajñānamātrādeva sakalasaṃsārānarthanivṛttiritīmaṃ pakṣaṃ draḍhayitukāma āha |
units.translation: Thus the view that liberation is accomplished through actions has been refuted. Now, wishing to establish that the cessation of every ill of saṃsāra comes solely from knowledge of the Self as it truly is, through examining the causes that prompt all action, he says:

units.label: Text 92
units.deva: इह चेदं परीक्ष्यते । किं यथा प्रतिषिद्धेषु यादृच्छिकेषु च कर्मसु स्वाभाविकस्वाशयोत्थनिमित्तवशादेवेदं हितमिदमहितमिति विशेषान् परिकल्प्य मृगतृष्णिकोदकपिपासुरिव लौकिकप्रमाणप्रसिद्धान्येव साधनान्युपादाय हितप्राप्तयेऽहितनिरासाय च स्वयमेव प्रवर्तते निवर्तते च तथैवादृष्टार्थेषु काम्येषु नित्येषु च कर्मसु किं वान्यदेव तत्र प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिनिमित्तमिति । किंचातः । यद्येवं श्रुणु । यदि तावद्यथावस्थितवस्तुसम्यग्ज्ञानं प्रमाणभूतं लौकिकमागमिकं वा प्रवृत्तिनिमित्तमिति निश्चीयते निवृत्तिशास्त्रं च नाभ्युपगम्यते तदा हताः कर्मत्यागिनो भ्रान्तिविज्ञानमात्रावष्टम्भादलौकिकप्रमाणोपात्तकर्मानुष्ठानत्यागित्वाच्च । अथ मृगतृष्णिकोदकपिपासुप्रवृत्तिनिमित्तवदयथावस्तुभ्रान्तिविज्ञानमेव सर्वप्रवृत्तिनिमित्तं तदा वर्द्धामहे वयं हताः स्थ यूयमिति ।
units.iast: iha cedaṃ parīkṣyate | kiṃ yathā pratiṣiddheṣu yādṛcchikeṣu ca karmasu svābhāvikasvāśayotthanimittavaśādevedaṃ hitamidamahitamiti viśeṣān parikalpya mṛgatṛṣṇikodakapipāsuriva laukikapramāṇaprasiddhānyeva sādhanānyupādāya hitaprāptaye'hitanirāsāya ca svayameva pravartate nivartate ca tathaivādṛṣṭārtheṣu kāmyeṣu nityeṣu ca karmasu kiṃ vānyadeva tatra pravṛttinivṛttinimittamiti | kiṃcātaḥ | yadyevaṃ śruṇu | yadi tāvadyathāvasthitavastusamyagjñānaṃ pramāṇabhūtaṃ laukikamāgamikaṃ vā pravṛttinimittamiti niścīyate nivṛttiśāstraṃ ca nābhyupagamyate tadā hatāḥ karmatyāgino bhrāntivijñānamātrāvaṣṭambhādalaukikapramāṇopāttakarmānuṣṭhānatyāgitvācca | atha mṛgatṛṣṇikodakapipāsupravṛttinimittavadayathāvastubhrāntivijñānameva sarvapravṛttinimittaṃ tadā varddhāmahe vayaṃ hatāḥ stha yūyamiti |
units.translation: Here this matter is examined: in forbidden and spontaneous actions, does one act or refrain by distinguishing what is beneficial from what is harmful, prompted by one’s natural interests—as a person thirsty for water in a mirage acts on the means known through ordinary experience, seeking good and avoiding harm? Or is some other cause responsible for acting and refraining in rites whose results are unseen, whether desired or obligatory? What follows? Listen. If correct knowledge of things as they are—whether gained by ordinary or scriptural means—is held to prompt action, while the scriptural teaching of renunciation is rejected, then those who abandon action are ruined: they have renounced rites prescribed by a superhuman authority, relying only on a mistaken cognition. But if mistaken cognition of things as they are, like the thirst for water in a mirage, is the cause of all action, then we say: “We are thriving; you are the ones who are lost.”

units.label: Verse 1.29
units.deva: हितं संप्रेप्सतां मोहादहितं च जिहासताम् । उपायान्प्राप्तिहनार्थान् शास्त्रं भासयतेऽर्कवत् ॥ २९॥
units.iast: hitaṃ saṃprepsatāṃ mohādahitaṃ ca jihāsatām | upāyānprāptihanārthān śāstraṃ bhāsayate'rkavat || 29||
units.translation: For those who, through delusion, want to gain what is good and abandon what is harmful, scripture shines like the sun, revealing the means to attain and avoid them.

units.label: Text 95
units.deva: एवं तावत्प्रत्यक्षानुमानागमप्रमाणावष्टम्भादात्मनो निरतिशयसुखहिताव्यतिरेकसिद्धेरहितस्य च षष्ठगोचरवत्स्वत एवानभिसंबन्धादेवंस्वाभाव्यात्मानवबोधमात्रादेव हितं मे स्यादहितं मे मा भूदिति मिथ्याज्ञानं तूषरशुक्तिकानवबोधोत्थमिथ्याज्ञानवत् प्रवृत्तिनिमित्तमिति निर्धारितम् । शास्त्रं च न पदार्थशक्त्याधानकृदिति । अथैतस्यैवोत्तरत्र प्रपञ्च आरभ्यते ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvatpratyakṣānumānāgamapramāṇāvaṣṭambhādātmano niratiśayasukhahitāvyatirekasiddherahitasya ca ṣaṣṭhagocaravatsvata evānabhisaṃbandhādevaṃsvābhāvyātmānavabodhamātrādeva hitaṃ me syādahitaṃ me mā bhūditi mithyājñānaṃ tūṣaraśuktikānavabodhotthamithyājñānavat pravṛttinimittamiti nirdhāritam | śāstraṃ ca na padārthaśaktyādhānakṛditi | athaitasyaivottaratra prapañca ārabhyate |
units.translation: Thus it has been established, relying on perception, inference, and scripture, that the Self is inseparable from unsurpassed happiness and good, while what is harmful is unrelated to it of itself, like a sixth sense-object. Because this is the Self’s nature, the mere ignorance of it gives rise to the false thought, “May good come to me; may harm not come to me,” just as ignorance of a shell gives rise to the false perception of silver in a barren place. Scripture does not implant powers in things. This very point will now be developed.

units.label: Verse 1.30
units.deva: न परीप्सां जिहासां वा पुंसः शास्त्रं करोति हि । निजे एव तु ते यस्मात्पश्वादावपि दर्शनात् ॥ ३०॥
units.iast: na parīpsāṃ jihāsāṃ vā puṃsaḥ śāstraṃ karoti hi | nije eva tu te yasmātpaśvādāvapi darśanāt || 30||
units.translation: Scripture does not create a person’s desire to gain or to avoid; those desires are innate, as seen even in animals.

units.label: Text 98
units.translation: It has already been said that one who does not understand the true nature of things is eligible for the scriptural injunctions and prohibitions.

units.label: Verse 1.31
units.deva: लिप्सतेऽज्ञानतोऽलब्धं कण्ठे चामीकरं यथा । वर्जितं च स्वतो भ्रान्त्या छायायामात्मनो यथा ॥ ३१॥
units.iast: lipsate'jñānato'labdhaṃ kaṇṭhe cāmīkaraṃ yathā | varjitaṃ ca svato bhrāntyā chāyāyāmātmano yathā || 31||
units.translation: Through ignorance one seeks what one has not obtained, like the gold on one’s own neck; through one’s own delusion one rejects what is already present, like one’s own shadow.

units.label: Verse 1.32
units.deva: भयान्मोहावनद्धात्मा रक्षः परिजिहीर्षति । यच्चापरिहृतं वस्तु तथालब्धं च लिप्सते ॥ ३२॥
units.iast: bhayānmohāvanaddhātmā rakṣaḥ parijihīrṣati | yaccāparihṛtaṃ vastu tathālabdhaṃ ca lipsate || 32||
units.translation: Bound by fear and delusion, a person tries to escape a demon; likewise, that person longs to obtain an object not yet gained and not yet set aside.

gloss.en: one whose self is bound by delusion

units.label: Text 103
units.deva: तत्रैतेषु चतुर्षु विषयेषु प्राप्तये परीहाराय च विभज्य न्यायः प्रदर्श्यते ।
units.iast: tatraiteṣu caturṣu viṣayeṣu prāptaye parīhārāya ca vibhajya nyāyaḥ pradarśyate |
units.translation: The reasoning is now shown with respect to these four cases, divided into what is to be gained and what is to be avoided.

units.label: Verse 1.33
units.deva: प्राप्तव्यपरिहार्येषु ज्ञात्वोपायाञ्छृतेः पृथक् । कृत्वाथ प्राप्नुयात्प्राप्यं तथानिष्टं जहात्यपि ॥ ३३॥
units.iast: prāptavyaparihāryeṣu jñātvopāyāñchṛteḥ pṛthak | kṛtvātha prāpnuyātprāpyaṃ tathāniṣṭaṃ jahātyapi || 33||
units.translation: Having separately learned from scripture the means for what should be gained and what should be avoided, one acts, attains what is to be gained, and gives up what is unwanted.

gloss.en: among what is to be attained and avoided

units.label: Text 106
units.translation: But in the remaining two cases, things already present by nature—

units.label: Verse 1.34
units.deva: परिहृतावाप्तयोर्बोधाद्धानप्राप्ती न कर्मणा । मोहमात्रान्तरायत्वात्क्रियया ते न सिध्यतः ॥ ३४॥
units.iast: parihṛtāvāptayorbodhāddhānaprāptī na karmaṇā | mohamātrāntarāyatvātkriyayā te na sidhyataḥ || 34||
units.translation: Abandonment and attainment come through understanding, not action; because delusion alone stands in the way, action cannot accomplish them.

gloss.en: of what is already avoided and attained
because delusion alone is the obstacle

units.label: Text 109
units.translation: Why, then, do the attainment of the unsurpassed happiness one desires and the complete removal of suffering follow solely from knowledge of the Self as it truly is, and not from action? The answer is:

units.label: Verse 1.35
units.translation: Because action arises from ignorance, it cannot remove delusion. Right knowledge, opposed to it, is like sunlight opposed to darkness.

units.label: Text 112
units.deva: नन्वात्मज्ञानमप्यविद्योपादानम् । न हि शास्त्रशिष्याचार्याद्यनुपादायात्मज्ञानमात्मानं लभतः इति । नैष दोषः । यत आत्मज्ञानं हि स्वतस्सिद्धपरमार्थात्मवस्तुस्वरूपमात्राशयादेवाविद्यातदुत्पन्नकारकग्रामप्रध्वंसि स्वात्मोपतावेव शास्त्रादपेक्ष्यते नोत्पन्नमविद्यानिवृत्तौ । कर्म पुनः स्वात्मोत्पत्तावुत्पन्नं च । न हिक्रिया कारकनिस्स्पृहा कल्पकोटिव्यवहितफलदानाय स्वात्मानं बिभर्ति साध्यमानमात्ररूपत्वात्तस्याः । न च क्रियात्मज्ञानवत्स्वात्मप्रतिलम्भकाल एव स्वर्गादिफलेन कर्तारं संबध्नाति । आत्मज्ञानं पुनः पुरुषार्थसिद्धौ नोत्पद्यमानस्वरूपव्यतिरेकेणान्यद्रूपान्तरं साधनान्तरं वापेक्षते । कुत एतत् । यतः ।
units.iast: nanvātmajñānamapyavidyopādānam | na hi śāstraśiṣyācāryādyanupādāyātmajñānamātmānaṃ labhataḥ iti | naiṣa doṣaḥ | yata ātmajñānaṃ hi svatassiddhaparamārthātmavastusvarūpamātrāśayādevāvidyātadutpannakārakagrāmapradhvaṃsi svātmopatāveva śāstrādapekṣyate notpannamavidyānivṛttau | karma punaḥ svātmotpattāvutpannaṃ ca | na hikriyā kārakanisspṛhā kalpakoṭivyavahitaphaladānāya svātmānaṃ bibharti sādhyamānamātrarūpatvāttasyāḥ | na ca kriyātmajñānavatsvātmapratilambhakāla eva svargādiphalena kartāraṃ saṃbadhnāti | ātmajñānaṃ punaḥ puruṣārthasiddhau notpadyamānasvarūpavyatirekeṇānyadrūpāntaraṃ sādhanāntaraṃ vāpekṣate | kuta etat | yataḥ |
units.translation: One may object: “Knowledge of the Self also has ignorance as its basis. No one gains knowledge of the Self without relying on scripture, a student, a teacher, and the like.” This is no defect. Knowledge of the Self destroys ignorance and the entire apparatus of agency that arises from it, because its aim is only the nature of the Self, the supreme reality that is already self-established. It depends on scripture only for the recognition of one’s own Self, not for the production of the Self or the removal of ignorance as a produced effect. Action, however, is undertaken to produce something. An action cannot carry itself forward to yield a result separated from it by countless ages, independently of its instruments and agent, because its very nature is only that of something being accomplished. Nor, unlike knowledge of the Self, does an action connect its agent with a result such as heaven at the very moment the Self is realized. Knowledge of the Self, by contrast, needs no other form or additional means beyond its own arising for the human end to be accomplished. Why is this so? Because:

units.label: Verse 1.36
units.deva: बलवद्धि प्रमाणोत्थं सम्यग्ज्ञानं न बाध्यते । आकाङ्क्षते न चाप्यान्यद्बाधनं प्रति साधनम् ॥ ३६॥
units.iast: balavaddhi pramāṇotthaṃ samyagjñānaṃ na bādhyate | ākāṅkṣate na cāpyānyadbādhanaṃ prati sādhanam || 36||
units.translation: Right knowledge born from a strong means of knowledge is not overturned; nor does it depend on any further means to keep it from being overturned.

gloss.en: arising from a means of knowledge

units.label: Text 115
units.translation: Having established his own position by supporting it with reasons, he concludes without hesitation:

units.label: Verse 1.37
units.translation: Therefore, to remove ignorance, the cause of the ocean of suffering, right knowledge is fully sufficient; action is not, for the reasons already stated.

units.label: Text 118
units.deva: ननु बलवदपि सम्यग्ज्ञानं सदप्रमाणोत्थेन बाध्यमानमुपलभामहे यत उत्पन्नपरमार्थबोधस्यापि कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वरागद्वेषाद्यनवबोधोत्थप्रत्यया आविर्भवन्ति । न ह्यबाधिते सम्यग्ज्ञाने तद्विरुद्धानां प्रत्ययानां सम्भवोऽस्ति । नैतदेवम् । कुतः ।
units.iast: nanu balavadapi samyagjñānaṃ sadapramāṇotthena bādhyamānamupalabhāmahe yata utpannaparamārthabodhasyāpi kartṛtvabhoktṛtvarāgadveṣādyanavabodhotthapratyayā āvirbhavanti | na hyabādhite samyagjñāne tadviruddhānāṃ pratyayānāṃ sambhavo'sti | naitadevam | kutaḥ |
units.translation: One may object: “We observe that even powerful right knowledge is overturned by a cognition that lacks authority, since ideas of agency, enjoyment, attachment, aversion, and the like—arising from ignorance—appear even in one who has gained true understanding. Such contrary cognitions cannot occur while right knowledge remains unopposed.” That is not so. Why?

units.label: Verse 1.38
units.deva: बाधितत्वादविद्याया विद्यां सा नैव बाधते । तद्वासना निमित्तत्वं यान्ति विद्यास्मृतेर्ध्रुवन् ॥ ३८॥
units.iast: bādhitatvādavidyāyā vidyāṃ sā naiva bādhate | tadvāsanā nimittatvaṃ yānti vidyāsmṛterdhruvan || 38||
units.translation: Because ignorance has been sublated, it cannot sublate knowledge. Its residual impression only serves as a cause for the definite recollection of knowledge.

units.label: Text 121
units.deva: "कर्माज्ञानसमुत्थत्वात् " इत्युक्तो हेतुस्तस्य च समर्थनं पूर्वमेवाभिहितं "हितं सम्प्रेप्सताम् " इत्यादिना । तदभ्युच्चयार्थमविद्यान्वयेन च संसारान्वयित्वं प्रदर्शयिष्यामीत्यत आह ।
units.iast: "karmājñānasamutthatvāt " ityukto hetustasya ca samarthanaṃ pūrvamevābhihitaṃ "hitaṃ samprepsatām " ityādinā | tadabhyuccayārthamavidyānvayena ca saṃsārānvayitvaṃ pradarśayiṣyāmītyata āha |
units.translation: The reason already stated—“because action arises from ignorance”—was supported earlier by the passage beginning, “For those who seek to secure what is good.” To reinforce it, he now shows that saṃsāra continues as long as ignorance does:

units.label: Verse 1.39
units.deva: ब्राह्मण्याद्यात्मके देहे लात्वा नात्मेति भावनाम् । श्रुतेः किङ्करतामेति वाङ्मनःकायकर्मसु ॥ ३९॥
units.iast: brāhmaṇyādyātmake dehe lātvā nātmeti bhāvanām | śruteḥ kiṅkaratāmeti vāṅmanaḥkāyakarmasu || 39||
units.translation: Taking the body, marked by being a Brahmin and the like, to be the Self, one becomes a servant of Vedic injunctions concerning actions of speech, mind, and body.

gloss.en: characterized by Brahmin status and the like
in actions of speech, mind, and body

units.label: Text 124
units.translation: Since action arises from ignorance, it ceases when ignorance is removed, as is now explained:

units.label: Verse 1.40
units.deva: दग्धाखिलाधिकारश्चेद्ब्रह्मज्ञानाग्निना मुनिः । वर्तमानः श्रुतेर्मूर्ध्नि नैव स्याद्वेदकिङ्करः ॥ ४०॥
units.iast: dagdhākhilādhikāraścedbrahmajñānāgninā muniḥ | vartamānaḥ śrutermūrdhni naiva syādvedakiṅkaraḥ || 40||
units.translation: If a sage’s entire field of duty has been burned by the fire of knowledge of Brahman, then, standing at the summit of scripture, he is no longer a servant of the Veda.

gloss.en: by the fire of knowledge of Brahman

units.label: Text 127
units.translation: But another person, whose mind is veiled by a dense mass of ignorance and who accepts agency and the rest—the grounds for every kind of ritual duty—acts under the pressure of scriptural injunctions and prohibitions.

units.label: Verse 1.41
units.deva: शुभैः प्राप्नोति देवत्वं निषिद्धैर्नारकीं गतिम् । उभाभ्यां पुण्यपापाभ्यां मानुष्यं लभतेऽवशः ॥ ४१॥
units.iast: śubhaiḥ prāpnoti devatvaṃ niṣiddhairnārakīṃ gatim | ubhābhyāṃ puṇyapāpābhyāṃ mānuṣyaṃ labhate'vaśaḥ || 41||
units.translation: Through good actions he attains divine status; through prohibited actions, a hellish fate. Helplessly, he gains human birth through both merit and demerit.

gloss.en: divine status; the state of a god

units.label: Text 130
units.translation: Propelled by winds of mixed good and bad action, he is tossed through the dreadful ocean of suffering, from Brahmā down to a clump of grass, rising and falling like a water-wheel. Its many births bring sudden flashes of inferior, middling, and superior pleasure, pain, and delusion; he is like a dry gourd beaten by fierce winds in the middle of a roaring sea.

units.label: Verse 1.42
units.deva: एवं चङ्क्रम्यमाणोऽयमविद्याकामकर्मभिः । पाशितो जायते कामी म्रियते चासुखावृतः ॥ ४२॥
units.iast: evaṃ caṅkramyamāṇo'yamavidyākāmakarmabhiḥ | pāśito jāyate kāmī mriyate cāsukhāvṛtaḥ || 42||
units.translation: Thus, driven by ignorance, desire, and action, this person wanders on: bound, he is born desiring and dies enveloped in unhappiness.

units.label: Text 133
units.translation: An authoritative text is now cited to affirm what has been said.

units.label: Verse 1.43
units.deva: श्रुतिश्चेमं जगादार्थं कामस्य विनिवृत्तये । तन्मूला संसृतिर्यस्मात्तन्नाशोऽज्ञानहानतः ॥ ४३॥
units.iast: śrutiścemaṃ jagādārthaṃ kāmasya vinivṛttaye | tanmūlā saṃsṛtiryasmāttannāśo'jñānahānataḥ || 43||
units.translation: Scripture teaches this point to bring desire to an end: transmigration has desire as its root, and that root is destroyed through the removal of ignorance.

units.label: Text 136
units.translation: If one asks, “Which passage of revelation?”

units.label: Verse 1.44
units.deva: यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्त इति नु इति च वाजिनः । कामबन्धनमेवेदं व्यासोऽप्याह पदेपदे ॥ ४४॥
units.iast: yadā sarve pramucyanta iti nu iti ca vājinaḥ | kāmabandhanamevedaṃ vyāso'pyāha padepade || 44||
units.translation: The Vājasaneyins cite “when all [desires] are released” and “indeed”; Vyāsa too says repeatedly that this [saṃsāra] is bondage by desire.

units.label: Text 139
units.deva: एष संसारपन्था व्याख्यातः । अथेदानीं तद्व्यावृत्तये कर्माण्यारादुपकारकत्वेन यथा मोक्षहेतुतां प्रतिपद्यन्ते तथाभिधीयते ।
units.iast: eṣa saṃsārapanthā vyākhyātaḥ | athedānīṃ tadvyāvṛttaye karmāṇyārādupakārakatvena yathā mokṣahetutāṃ pratipadyante tathābhidhīyate |
units.translation: The course of saṃsāra has now been explained. Next it is shown how actions, by serving as indirect aids, come to be regarded as a cause of liberation.

units.label: Verse 1.45
units.deva: तस्यैवं दुःखतप्तस्य कथंचित्पुण्यशीलनात् । नित्येहाक्षालितधियो वैराग्यं जायते हृदि ॥ ४५॥
units.iast: tasyaivaṃ duḥkhataptasya kathaṃcitpuṇyaśīlanāt | nityehākṣālitadhiyo vairāgyaṃ jāyate hṛdi || 45||
units.translation: For one thus scorched by suffering, dispassion arises in the heart through some cultivation of merit, with the mind cleansed by steady practice.

gloss.en: whose mind has been cleansed by steady practice

units.label: Text 142
units.translation: What kind of dispassion arises? The answer is:

units.label: Verse 1.46
units.translation: Just as he came to fear hell, so too he fears the fruits of desire-driven actions. Seeing things as they are, he therefore wishes to perform the obligatory duties regularly.

gloss.en: from the fruits of desire-driven actions
from seeing things as they are

units.label: Text 145
units.translation: By performing obligatory and occasional actions,

units.label: Verse 1.47
units.deva: शुध्यमानं तु तच्चित्तमीश्वरार्पितकर्मभिः । वैराग्यं ब्रह्मलोकादौ व्यनक्त्यथ सुनिर्मलम् ॥ ४७॥
units.iast: śudhyamānaṃ tu taccittamīśvarārpitakarmabhiḥ | vairāgyaṃ brahmalokādau vyanaktyatha sunirmalam || 47||
units.translation: His mind, being purified by actions offered to the Lord, then reveals perfectly pure dispassion toward the world of Brahmā and the rest.

gloss.en: by actions offered to the Lord
toward the world of Brahmā and the rest

units.label: Text 148
units.deva: यस्माद्रजस्तमोमलोपसंसृष्टमेव चित्तं कामबडिशेनाकृष्य विषयदुरन्तसूनास्थानेष निक्षिप्यते तस्मान्नित्यनैमित्तिककर्मानुष्ठानपरिमार्जनेनापविद्धरजस्तमोमलं प्रसन्नमनाकृलं संमार्जितस्फटिकशिलाकल्पं बाह्यविषयहेतुकेन च रागद्वेषात्मकेनातिग्रहबडिशेनानाकृष्यमाणं विधूताशेषकल्मषं प्रत्यङ्मात्रप्रवणं चित्तदर्पणमवतिष्टते । अत इदमभिधीयते ।
units.iast: yasmādrajastamomalopasaṃsṛṣṭameva cittaṃ kāmabaḍiśenākṛṣya viṣayadurantasūnāsthāneṣa nikṣipyate tasmānnityanaimittikakarmānuṣṭhānaparimārjanenāpaviddharajastamomalaṃ prasannamanākṛlaṃ saṃmārjitasphaṭikaśilākalpaṃ bāhyaviṣayahetukena ca rāgadveṣātmakenātigrahabaḍiśenānākṛṣyamāṇaṃ vidhūtāśeṣakalmaṣaṃ pratyaṅmātrapravaṇaṃ cittadarpaṇamavatiṣṭate | ata idamabhidhīyate |
units.translation: When the mind is stained by rajas and tamas, the bait of desire draws it into the perilous snares of sense-objects. But when obligatory and occasional duties have cleansed away those stains, the mind remains clear and undisturbed, like a polished crystal. No longer drawn outward by the strong hooks of attachment and aversion to sense-objects, it is freed of every fault and turned wholly inward. Therefore it is said:

units.label: Verse 1.48
units.deva: व्युत्थिताशेषकामेभ्यो यदा धीरवतिष्ठते । तदैव प्रत्यगात्मानं स्वयमेवाविविक्षति ॥ ४८॥
units.iast: vyutthitāśeṣakāmebhyo yadā dhīravatiṣṭhate | tadaiva pratyagātmānaṃ svayamevāvivikṣati || 48||
units.translation: When the wise person stands firm, having withdrawn from every desire, he then seeks, by himself, to enter the inward Self.

gloss.en: having risen away from all desires
he wishes to enter; seeks to enter

units.label: Text 151
units.deva: अतःपरमवसिताधिकाराणि कर्माणि प्रत्यक्प्रवणवत्वसूनौ कृतसंप्रत्तिकानि चरितार्थानि सन्ति ।
units.iast: ataḥparamavasitādhikārāṇi karmāṇi pratyakpravaṇavatvasūnau kṛtasaṃprattikāni caritārthāni santi |
units.translation: From this point the actions whose scope has ended have served their purpose: they have brought the mind to turn inward.

units.label: Verse 1.49
units.deva: प्रत्यक्प्रवणतां बुद्धेः कर्माण्युत्पाद्य शुद्धितः । कृतार्थान्यस्तमायान्ति प्रावृडन्ते घना इव ॥ ४९॥
units.iast: pratyakpravaṇatāṃ buddheḥ karmāṇyutpādya śuddhitaḥ | kṛtārthānyastamāyānti prāvṛḍante ghanā iva || 49||
units.translation: Through purification, actions bring about the intellect’s inward turn; having fulfilled their purpose, they pass away like clouds at the end of the rainy season.

gloss.en: at the end of the rainy season

units.label: Text 154
units.translation: This, then, is the greatness of performing obligatory duties.

units.label: Verse 1.50
units.deva: तस्मान्मुमुक्षुभिः कार्यमात्मज्ञानाभिलाषिभिः । नित्यं नैमित्तिकं कर्म सदैवात्मविशुद्धये ॥ ५०॥
units.iast: tasmānmumukṣubhiḥ kāryamātmajñānābhilāṣibhiḥ | nityaṃ naimittikaṃ karma sadaivātmaviśuddhaye || 50||
units.translation: Therefore, seekers of liberation who long for knowledge of the Self should always perform obligatory and occasional duties for the purification of the mind.

gloss.en: by those longing for knowledge of the Self
for purification of the inner self; mind

units.label: Text 157
units.translation: The teaching of the all-knowing one is authority for this point:

units.label: Verse 1.51
units.deva: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते । योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शम एवेति च स्मृतिः ॥ ५१॥
units.iast: ārurukṣormuneryogaṃ karma kāraṇamucyate | yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śama eveti ca smṛtiḥ || 51||
units.translation: “For the sage wishing to ascend to yoga, action is said to be the means; for that same person who has attained yoga, quietude alone [is the means],” says the tradition.

gloss.en: of one who has attained yoga

units.label: Text 160
units.deva: नित्यकर्मानुष्ठानाद्धर्मोत्पत्तिर्धर्मोत्पत्तेः पापहानिस्ततश्चित्तशुद्धिस्ततः संसारयाथात्म्यावबोधस्ततो वैराग्यं ततो मुमुक्षुत्वं ततस्तदुपायपर्येषणं ततः सर्वकर्मतत्साधनसंन्यासस्ततो योगाभ्यासस्ततश्चित्तस्य प्रत्यक्प्रवणता ततस्तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यार्थपरिज्ञानं ततोऽविद्योच्छेदस्ततश्च स्वात्मन्ये वावस्थानं "ब्रह्मैव सन् ब्रह्माप्येति " "विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते " इति ।
units.iast: nityakarmānuṣṭhānāddharmotpattirdharmotpatteḥ pāpahānistataścittaśuddhistataḥ saṃsārayāthātmyāvabodhastato vairāgyaṃ tato mumukṣutvaṃ tatastadupāyaparyeṣaṇaṃ tataḥ sarvakarmatatsādhanasaṃnyāsastato yogābhyāsastataścittasya pratyakpravaṇatā tatastattvamasyādivākyārthaparijñānaṃ tato'vidyocchedastataśca svātmanye vāvasthānaṃ "brahmaiva san brahmāpyeti " "vimuktaśca vimucyate " iti |
units.translation: From the performance of obligatory action comes merit; from merit, the removal of sin; then purification of mind; then understanding the true nature of saṃsāra; then dispassion; then the desire for liberation; then the search for its means; then renunciation of all actions and their instruments; then practice of yoga; then the mind’s inward direction; then understanding the meaning of sayings such as “That thou art”; then the destruction of ignorance; and then abiding in one’s own Self alone: “Being Brahman, one reaches Brahman”; “one who has been freed is fully liberated.”

units.label: Verse 1.52
units.translation: Thus, action may contribute indirectly to the removal of ignorance. Unlike knowledge, it does not destroy ignorance directly, because it is not opposed to ignorance.

gloss.en: indirectly; through a series of steps

units.label: Text 163
units.deva: न च कर्मणः कार्यमण्वपि मुक्तौ संभाव्यते नापि मुक्तौ यत्संभवति तत्कर्मापेक्षते । तदुच्यते ।
units.iast: na ca karmaṇaḥ kāryamaṇvapi muktau saṃbhāvyate nāpi muktau yatsaṃbhavati tatkarmāpekṣate | taducyate |
units.translation: No action, even the least, can be involved in liberation, nor does liberation depend on any action. This is explained:

units.label: Verse 1.53
units.deva: उत्पाद्यमाप्यं संस्कार्यं विकार्यं च क्रियाफलम् । नैवं मुक्तिर्यतस्तस्मात्कर्म तस्या न साधनम् ॥ ५३॥
units.iast: utpādyamāpyaṃ saṃskāryaṃ vikāryaṃ ca kriyāphalam | naivaṃ muktiryatastasmātkarma tasyā na sādhanam || 53||
units.translation: The results of action are things produced, attained, prepared, or transformed. Liberation is not of this kind; therefore action is not its means.

gloss.en: what is to be prepared or refined

units.label: Text 166
units.deva: एवं तावत्केवलं कर्म साक्षादविद्यापनुत्तये न पर्याप्तमिति प्रपञ्चितम् । मुक्तौ च मुमुक्षुज्ञानतद्विषयस्वाभाव्यानुरोधेन सर्वप्रकारस्यापि कर्मणोऽसंभव उक्तो "हितं संप्रेप्सताम् " इत्यादिना ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvatkevalaṃ karma sākṣādavidyāpanuttaye na paryāptamiti prapañcitam | muktau ca mumukṣujñānatadviṣayasvābhāvyānurodhena sarvaprakārasyāpi karmaṇo'saṃbhava ukto "hitaṃ saṃprepsatām " ityādinā |
units.translation: It has thus been explained that action alone is not enough to remove ignorance directly. And, as shown by the passage beginning “For those who seek to secure what is good,” no action of any kind can be combined with liberation, which accords with the nature of the knowledge sought by the seeker.

units.label: Text 167
units.deva: यादृशश्चारादुपकारकत्वेन ज्ञानोत्पत्तौ कर्मणां समुच्चयः संभवति तथा प्रतिपादितम् । अविद्योच्छित्तौ तु लब्धात्मस्वभावस्यात्मज्ञानस्यैवासाधारणं साधकतमत्वं नान्यस्य प्रधानभूतस्य गुणभूतस्य चेत्येतदधुनोच्यते ।
units.iast: yādṛśaścārādupakārakatvena jñānotpattau karmaṇāṃ samuccayaḥ saṃbhavati tathā pratipāditam | avidyocchittau tu labdhātmasvabhāvasyātmajñānasyaivāsādhāraṇaṃ sādhakatamatvaṃ nānyasya pradhānabhūtasya guṇabhūtasya cetyetadadhunocyate |
units.translation: It has also been shown how actions may be combined with knowledge as indirect aids to its arising. But when ignorance is to be destroyed, knowledge of the Self—whose nature is already attained—is uniquely the most effective means, and nothing else, whether principal or auxiliary. This is now stated.

units.label: Text 168
units.translation: First he says that knowledge, as a mere auxiliary, is not the cause:

units.label: Verse 1.54
units.deva: संनिपत्य न च ज्ञानं कर्माज्ञानं निरस्यति । साध्यसाधनभावत्वादेककालानवस्थितेः ॥ ५४॥
units.iast: saṃnipatya na ca jñānaṃ karmājñānaṃ nirasyati | sādhyasādhanabhāvatvādekakālānavasthiteḥ || 54||
units.translation: Knowledge does not remove ignorance by joining with action: one is the means and the other its result, so they cannot coexist at the same time.

gloss.en: because of their relation as result and means
because they cannot stand together at one time

units.label: Text 171
units.translation: Nor can they exist together as equally principal means.

units.label: Verse 1.55
units.translation: They cannot be combined: knowledge sublates action, like a lion subduing a sheep, and the two cannot remain in the same place.

gloss.en: because of the relation of what is sublated and what sublates
of a sheep and a lion
because they cannot remain in the same place

units.label: Text 174
units.translation: Why do they oppose one another? Because

units.label: Verse 1.56
units.deva: अयथावस्त्वविद्या स्याद्विद्या तस्या विरोधिनी । समुच्चयस्तयोरेवं रविशार्वरयोरिव ॥ ५६॥
units.iast: ayathāvastvavidyā syādvidyā tasyā virodhinī | samuccayastayorevaṃ raviśārvarayoriva || 56||
units.translation: Ignorance is seeing things otherwise than they are; knowledge opposes it. Their combination is therefore impossible, like the sun and night.

units.label: Text 177
units.translation: Once knowledge is complete in the non-agent Brahman-Self, all injunctions to action lose their force, since action is foreign to the Self’s nature.

units.label: Text 178
units.translation: How so? It is explained:

units.label: Verse 1.57
units.deva: बृहस्पतिसवे यद्वत्क्षत्रियो न प्रवर्तते । ब्राह्मणत्वाद्यहंमानी विप्रो वा क्षत्रकर्मणि ॥ ५७॥
units.iast: bṛhaspatisave yadvatkṣatriyo na pravartate | brāhmaṇatvādyahaṃmānī vipro vā kṣatrakarmaṇi || 57||
units.translation: Just as a Kṣatriya does not undertake the Bṛhaspati rite, a Brahmin who identifies as a Brahmin does not undertake Kṣatriya duties.

gloss.en: one who prides himself on being a Brahmin

units.label: Text 181
units.translation: He says that the illustration corresponds to the point being illustrated:

units.label: Verse 1.58
units.deva: विदेहो वीतसन्देहो नेतिनेत्यवशेषितः । देहाद्यनात्मदृक्तद्वत्क्रियां वीक्षतेऽपि न ॥ ५८॥
units.iast: videho vītasandeho netinetyavaśeṣitaḥ | dehādyanātmadṛktadvatkriyāṃ vīkṣate'pi na || 58||
units.translation: The one free from bodily identification, free from doubt, and established in “not this, not this” sees the body and the rest as not-Self and does not even regard action [as belonging to the Self].

gloss.en: free from the body; disidentified from the body

units.label: Text 184
units.translation: An example is given to make this point clear:

units.label: Verse 1.59
units.deva: मृत्स्नेभके यथेभत्वं शिशुरध्यस्य वल्गति । अध्यस्यात्मानि देहादीन्मूढस्तद्वत्विचेष्टते ॥ ५९॥
units.iast: mṛtsnebhake yathebhatvaṃ śiśuradhyasya valgati | adhyasyātmāni dehādīnmūḍhastadvatviceṣṭate || 59||
units.translation: As a child plays after imagining a clay elephant to be a real elephant, so the ignorant person acts after superimposing the body and the rest upon the Self.

units.label: Text 187
units.deva: न च वयं ज्ञानकर्मणोः सर्वत्रैव प्रत्याचक्ष्महे । यत्र प्रयोज्यप्रयोजकभावो ज्ञानकर्मणोस्तत्र नास्मत्पित्रापि शक्यते निवारयितुम् । तत्र विभागप्रदर्शनायोदाहरणं प्रदर्श्यते ।
units.iast: na ca vayaṃ jñānakarmaṇoḥ sarvatraiva pratyācakṣmahe | yatra prayojyaprayojakabhāvo jñānakarmaṇostatra nāsmatpitrāpi śakyate nivārayitum | tatra vibhāgapradarśanāyodāharaṇaṃ pradarśyate |
units.translation: We do not reject every possible connection between knowledge and action. Where knowledge serves as an instrument that enables an action, no one—not even our father—could prevent that connection. To show how the two are divided, an example is given:

units.label: Verse 1.60
units.deva: स्थाणुं चोरधियालाय भीतो यद्वत्पलायते । बुद्ध्यादिभिस्तथात्मानं भ्रान्तोऽध्यारोप्य चेष्टते ॥ ६०॥
units.iast: sthāṇuṃ coradhiyālāya bhīto yadvatpalāyate | buddhyādibhistathātmānaṃ bhrānto'dhyāropya ceṣṭate || 60||
units.translation: As a frightened person runs away after mistaking a tree stump for a thief, so a deluded person acts after superimposing the intellect and the rest upon the Self.

gloss.en: under the mistaken thought that it is a thief
with the intellect and the rest

units.label: Text 190
units.deva: एवं यत्रयत्र ज्ञानकर्मणोः प्रयोज्यप्रयोजकभावस्तत्र सर्वत्रायं न्यायः । यत्र तु न समकालं नापि क्रमेणोपपद्यते समुच्चयः सविषय उच्यते ।
units.iast: evaṃ yatrayatra jñānakarmaṇoḥ prayojyaprayojakabhāvastatra sarvatrāyaṃ nyāyaḥ | yatra tu na samakālaṃ nāpi krameṇopapadyate samuccayaḥ saviṣaya ucyate |
units.translation: This rule applies wherever knowledge and action stand in a relation of means and end. The case in which they cannot be combined, either at once or in sequence, is now explained.

units.label: Verse 1.61
units.deva: स्थाणोः सतत्त्वविज्ञानं यथा नाङ्गं पलायते । आत्मनस्तत्त्वविज्ञानं तद्वन्नाङ्गं क्रियाविधौ ॥ ६१॥
units.iast: sthāṇoḥ satattvavijñānaṃ yathā nāṅgaṃ palāyate | ātmanastattvavijñānaṃ tadvannāṅgaṃ kriyāvidhau || 61||
units.translation: Just as knowing the true nature of a post is no part of running away, knowledge of the Self’s true nature is no part of an injunction to act.

units.label: Text 193
units.translation: This follows from the nature of an auxiliary:

units.label: Verse 1.62
units.deva: यद्धि यस्यानुरोधेन स्वभावमनुवर्तते । तत्तस्य गुणभूतं स्यान्न प्रधानाद्गुणो यतः ॥ ६२॥
units.iast: yaddhi yasyānurodhena svabhāvamanuvartate | tattasya guṇabhūtaṃ syānna pradhānādguṇo yataḥ || 62||
units.translation: Whatever follows another’s nature in accordance with it is subordinate to that thing, because an attribute is never separate from what is primary.

units.label: Text 196
units.translation: For this reason:

units.label: Verse 1.63
units.deva: कर्मप्रकरणाकाङ्क्षिज्ञानं कर्मगुणो भवेत् । यद्धि प्रकरणे यस्य तत्तदङ्गं प्रचक्षते ॥ ६३॥
units.iast: karmaprakaraṇākāṅkṣijñānaṃ karmaguṇo bhavet | yaddhi prakaraṇe yasya tattadaṅgaṃ pracakṣate || 63||
units.translation: Knowledge that depends on a ritual context becomes an auxiliary of ritual action; whatever belongs to a context is called one of its limbs.

gloss.en: knowledge that depends on a ritual context

units.label: Verse 1.64
units.deva: स्वरूपलाभमात्रेण यत्त्वविद्यां निहन्ति नः । न तदङ्गं प्रधानं वा ज्ञानं स्यात्कर्मणः क्वचित् ॥ ६४॥
units.iast: svarūpalābhamātreṇa yattvavidyāṃ nihanti naḥ | na tadaṅgaṃ pradhānaṃ vā jñānaṃ syātkarmaṇaḥ kvacit || 64||
units.translation: But knowledge, which destroys our ignorance through the mere recognition of the true nature [of the Self], can nowhere be either an auxiliary or the principal part of action.

gloss.en: through the mere recognition of one’s true nature

units.label: Text 201
units.translation: Even the proponent of combining knowledge and action must necessarily accept this;

units.label: Text 202
units.translation: for:

units.label: Verse 1.65
units.deva: अज्ञानमनिराकुर्वज्ज्ञानमेव न सिध्यति । विपन्नकारकग्रामं ज्ञानं कर्म न ढौकते ॥ ६५॥
units.iast: ajñānamanirākurvajjñānameva na sidhyati | vipannakārakagrāmaṃ jñānaṃ karma na ḍhaukate || 65||
units.translation: Knowledge that does not remove ignorance is not established as knowledge at all; action cannot reach knowledge that has dissolved the whole set of agent and instrumental factors.

gloss.en: whose whole set of action-factors has been dissolved

units.label: Text 205
units.translation: Here is another reason why knowledge and action cannot be combined:

units.label: Verse 1.66
units.deva: हेतुस्वरूपकार्याणि प्रकाशतमसोरिव । विरोधीनि ततो नास्ति साङ्गत्यं ज्ञानकर्मणोः ॥ ६६॥
units.iast: hetusvarūpakāryāṇi prakāśatamasoriva | virodhīni tato nāsti sāṅgatyaṃ jñānakarmaṇoḥ || 66||
units.translation: The causes, nature, and effects of knowledge and action are opposed, like light and darkness; therefore, the two cannot be joined.

units.label: Text 208
units.deva: एवमुपसंहृते केचित्स्वसम्प्रदायबलावष्टम्भादाहुर्यदे तद्वेदान्तवाक्यादहं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञानं समुत्पद्यते तन्नैव स्वोत्पत्तिमात्रेणाज्ञानं निरस्यति । किं तर्हि । अहन्यहनि द्राघीयसा कालेनोपासीनस्य सतो भावनोपचयान्निश्शेषम् अज्ञानमपगच्छति "देवो भूत्वा देवानप्येति " इति श्रुतेः । अपरे तु ब्रुवते वेदान्तवाक्यजनितमहं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञानं संसर्गात्मकत्वादात्मवस्तुयाथात्म्यावगाह्येव न भवति । किं तर्हि ।
units.iast: evamupasaṃhṛte kecitsvasampradāyabalāvaṣṭambhādāhuryade tadvedāntavākyādahaṃ brahmeti vijñānaṃ samutpadyate tannaiva svotpattimātreṇājñānaṃ nirasyati | kiṃ tarhi | ahanyahani drāghīyasā kālenopāsīnasya sato bhāvanopacayānniśśeṣam ajñānamapagacchati "devo bhūtvā devānapyeti " iti śruteḥ | apare tu bruvate vedāntavākyajanitamahaṃ brahmeti vijñānaṃ saṃsargātmakatvādātmavastuyāthātmyāvagāhyeva na bhavati | kiṃ tarhi |
units.translation: Having concluded thus, some, relying on the strength of their own tradition, say: “The knowledge ‘I am Brahman’ arises from a Vedānta sentence, but its mere arising does not remove ignorance. What does? After one has meditated for a long time, day after day, the increase of contemplation removes ignorance completely, as scripture says, ‘Having become a god, one reaches the gods.’ Others say that the knowledge ‘I am Brahman’ produced by a Vedānta sentence does not penetrate the true nature of the Self, because it is relational in form. What does?”

units.label: Text 209
units.deva: एतदेव गङ्गास्रोतोवत्सततमभ्यस्यतोऽन्यदेवावाक्यार्थात्मकं विज्ञानान्तरमुत्पद्यते । अस्य पक्षद्वयस्य निवृत्तय इदमभिधीयते ।
units.iast: etadeva gaṅgāsrotovatsatatamabhyasyato'nyadevāvākyārthātmakaṃ vijñānāntaramutpadyate | asya pakṣadvayasya nivṛttaya idamabhidhīyate |
units.translation: “By constantly repeating that very [sentence], like the flow of the Ganges, a different knowledge arises, whose content is no longer merely the sentence.” This is stated to refute both views.

units.label: Verse 1.67
units.deva: सकृत्प्रवृत्त्या मृद्नाति क्रियाकारकरूपभृत् । अज्ञानमागमज्ञानं साङ्गत्यं नास्त्यतोऽनयोः ॥ ६७॥
units.iast: sakṛtpravṛttyā mṛdnāti kriyākārakarūpabhṛt | ajñānamāgamajñānaṃ sāṅgatyaṃ nāstyato'nayoḥ || 67||
units.translation: Scriptural knowledge, though appearing in the form of an act and its factors, crushes ignorance at a single stroke; therefore knowledge and action cannot be joined.

gloss.en: appearing in the form of an act and its factors

units.label: Text 212
units.deva: एवं तावदनानात्वे ब्रह्मणि ज्ञानकर्मणोः समुच्चयो निराकृतः । अथाधुना पक्षान्तराभ्युपगमेनापि प्रत्यवस्थाने पूर्ववदनाश्वासो यथा तथाभिधीयते ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvadanānātve brahmaṇi jñānakarmaṇoḥ samuccayo nirākṛtaḥ | athādhunā pakṣāntarābhyupagamenāpi pratyavasthāne pūrvavadanāśvāso yathā tathābhidhīyate |
units.translation: Thus the combination of knowledge and action has been rejected for Brahman, which is free from multiplicity. Now, even if another position is accepted, it is shown that it remains just as uncertain as before.

units.label: Verse 1.68
units.deva: अनुत्सारितनानात्वं ब्रह्म यस्यापि वादिनः । तन्मतेनापि दुस्साध्यो ज्ञानकर्मसमुच्चयः ॥ ६८॥
units.iast: anutsāritanānātvaṃ brahma yasyāpi vādinaḥ | tanmatenāpi dussādhyo jñānakarmasamuccayaḥ || 68||
units.translation: Even for a proponent whose Brahman has not been freed from multiplicity, the combination of knowledge and action is difficult to establish on that view.

gloss.en: whose multiplicity has not been removed
the combination of knowledge and action

units.label: Text 215
units.translation: The alternatives are stated to lay out the separate objections:

units.label: Verse 1.69
units.deva: ब्रह्मात्मा वा भवेत्तस्य यदि वानात्मरूपकम् । आत्मानाप्तिर्भवेन्मोहादितरस्याप्यनात्मनः ॥ ६९॥
units.iast: brahmātmā vā bhavettasya yadi vānātmarūpakam | ātmānāptirbhavenmohāditarasyāpyanātmanaḥ || 69||
units.translation: For him, Brahman may be either the Self or something of the nature of not-Self. If it is the Self, delusion would explain its seeming non-attainment; if it is other, it remains not-Self.

units.label: Text 218
units.deva: तत्र यदि तावद्वास्तवेनैव वृत्तेन ब्रह्म प्राप्तमात्मस्वाभाव्यात्केवलमासुरमोहापिधानमात्रमेवानाप्तिनिमित्तं तस्मिन्पक्षे ।
units.iast: tatra yadi tāvadvāstavenaiva vṛttena brahma prāptamātmasvābhāvyātkevalamāsuramohāpidhānamātramevānāptinimittaṃ tasminpakṣe |
units.translation: If Brahman is already truly attained because it is the nature of the Self, and its non-attainment is caused only by a demonic delusion that veils it, then, on that view,

units.label: Verse 1.70
units.deva: मोहापिधानभङ्गाय नैव कर्माणि कारणम् । ज्ञानेनैव फलावाप्तेस्तत्र कर्म निरर्थकम् ॥ ७०॥
units.iast: mohāpidhānabhaṅgāya naiva karmāṇi kāraṇam | jñānenaiva phalāvāptestatra karma nirarthakam || 70||
units.translation: Action is not the means for breaking the veil of delusion; since the result is attained through knowledge alone, action is pointless in that case.

gloss.en: for breaking the veil of delusion

units.label: Text 221
units.deva: अनात्मरूपके तु ब्रह्मणि न कर्म साधनभावं प्रतिपद्यते नापि ज्ञानं कर्मसमुच्चितमसमुच्चितं वा यस्मादन्यस्य स्वत एव साधकस्य ब्रह्मणोऽप्यन्यत्वं स्वत एव सिद्धम् ।
units.iast: anātmarūpake tu brahmaṇi na karma sādhanabhāvaṃ pratipadyate nāpi jñānaṃ karmasamuccitamasamuccitaṃ vā yasmādanyasya svata eva sādhakasya brahmaṇo'pyanyatvaṃ svata eva siddham |
units.translation: But if Brahman has the nature of not-Self, action cannot become its means, nor can knowledge—combined with action or without it—be its means, since Brahman is already established as different from the one who independently acts to attain it.

units.label: Text 222
units.translation: In that case,

units.label: Verse 1.71
units.deva: अन्यस्यान्यात्मताप्राप्तौ न क्वचिद्धेतुसम्भवः । तस्मिन् सत्यपि नानष्टः परात्मानं प्रपद्यते ॥ ७१॥
units.iast: anyasyānyātmatāprāptau na kvaciddhetusambhavaḥ | tasmin saty api nānaṣṭaḥ parātmānaṃ prapadyate || 71||
units.translation: There is no possible cause by which one thing can become the Self of another. Even if such a cause were present, one cannot attain the other Self without being destroyed.

gloss.en: in becoming the Self of another

units.label: Text 225
units.translation: On the other alternative, however, an injunction might be possible:

units.label: Verse 1.72
units.deva: परमात्मानुकूलेन ज्ञानाभ्यासेन दुःखिनः । द्वैतिनोऽपि प्रमुच्येरन्न परात्मविरोधिना ॥ ७२॥
units.iast: paramātmānukūlena jñānābhyāsena duḥkhinaḥ | dvaitino'pi pramucyeranna parātmavirodhinā || 72||
units.translation: Even suffering dualists could be liberated through practice of knowledge that accords with the Supreme Self, but not through what opposes it.

gloss.en: in accord with the Supreme Self
by what opposes the Supreme Self

units.label: Text 228
units.translation: On the first alternative, however, there is no room for an injunction at all. How?

units.label: Verse 1.73
units.deva: समस्तव्यस्तभूतस्य ब्रह्मण्येवावतिष्ठतः । ब्रूत कर्मणि को हेतुः सर्वानन्यत्वदर्शिनः ॥ ७३॥
units.iast: samastavyastabhūtasya brahmaṇyevāvatiṣṭhataḥ | brūta karmaṇi ko hetuḥ sarvānanyatvadarśinaḥ || 73||
units.translation: For one who abides in Brahman as the whole and its parts, seeing nothing as other, tell me: what could prompt action?

gloss.en: of one who has become the whole and its separate parts
for one who sees that all is non-other

units.label: Text 231
units.translation: If causes for every action are present or absent in the same way, all actions become confused together. For:

units.label: Verse 1.74
units.deva: सर्वजात्यादिमत्त्वेऽस्य नितरां हेतुसम्भवः । विशेषं ह्यनुपादाय कर्म नैव प्रवर्तते ॥ ७४॥
units.iast: sarvajātyādimattve'sya nitarāṃ hetusambhavaḥ | viśeṣaṃ hyanupādāya karma naiva pravartate || 74||
units.translation: If this Self possessed every distinction, such as caste and the rest, there would be many grounds for action; for action never proceeds without relying on a particular distinction.

gloss.en: if it possessed every caste and the rest

units.label: Text 234
units.translation: If one says that injunction rests on identification with the inner Self, that is not so, because:

units.label: Verse 1.75
units.translation: The knower has no identification with the inner person, since such identification is demonic. If even the knower were demonic, the vision of Brahman would be fruitless.

gloss.en: identification with the inner person; body-mind

units.label: Text 237
units.deva: अज्ञानकार्यत्वान्न समकालं नापि क्रमेण ज्ञानकर्मणोर्वस्त्ववस्तु तन्त्रत्वात्सङ्गतिरस्तीत्येवं निराकृतोऽपि काशं कुशं वावलम्ब्याह ॥
units.iast: ajñānakāryatvānna samakālaṃ nāpi krameṇa jñānakarmaṇorvastvavastu tantratvātsaṅgatirastītyevaṃ nirākṛto'pi kāśaṃ kuśaṃ vāvalambyāha ||
units.translation: Since knowledge and action depend respectively on reality and unreality, they cannot be joined either simultaneously or in sequence; action arises from ignorance. Yet, grasping at a last straw, someone objects:

units.label: Verse 1.76
units.deva: अथाध्यात्मं पुनर्यायादाश्रितो मूढतां भवेत् । स करोत्येव कर्माणि को ह्यज्ञं विनिवारयेत् ॥ ७६॥
units.iast: athādhyātmaṃ punaryāyādāśrito mūḍhatāṃ bhavet | sa karotyeva karmāṇi ko hyajñaṃ vinivārayet || 76||
units.translation: “If he were to turn again toward the inner self, he would become deluded. He would then keep acting; for who can restrain an ignorant person?”

units.label: Text 240
units.translation: And because liberation is already established, it is not something to be accomplished. For:

units.label: Verse 1.77
units.translation: For this yogin, action is the Self in both its general and particular forms; therefore, like breathing in and out, it requires no injunction.

units.label: Text 243
units.deva: अस्तु तर्हि भिन्नाभिन्नात्मकं ब्रह्म । तथा च सति ज्ञानकर्मणो संभवतो भेदाभेदविषयत्वात्तयोः । तत्र तावदयं पक्ष एव न संभवति । किं कारणम् । न हि भिन्नोऽयमित्यभेदबुद्धिमनिराकृत्य भेदबुद्धिः पदार्थमालिङ्गते । एवं ह्यनभ्युपगमे भिन्नाभिन्नपदार्थयोरलौकिकत्वं प्रसज्येत । अथ निष्प्रमाणकमप्याश्रीयते तदप्युभयपक्षाभ्युपगमादभेदपक्षे दुःखिब्रह्म स्यादत आह ।
units.iast: astu tarhi bhinnābhinnātmakaṃ brahma | tathā ca sati jñānakarmaṇo saṃbhavato bhedābhedaviṣayatvāttayoḥ | tatra tāvadayaṃ pakṣa eva na saṃbhavati | kiṃ kāraṇam | na hi bhinno'yamityabhedabuddhimanirākṛtya bhedabuddhiḥ padārthamāliṅgate | evaṃ hyanabhyupagame bhinnābhinnapadārthayoralaukikatvaṃ prasajyeta | atha niṣpramāṇakamapyāśrīyate tadapyubhayapakṣābhyupagamādabhedapakṣe duḥkhibrahma syādata āha |
units.translation: Suppose, then, that Brahman is both different and non-different, so that knowledge and action could occur because they concern difference and non-difference. This view is impossible. Why? Unless the cognition of non-difference is first set aside, the cognition “this is different” cannot grasp its object. If this is not admitted, both difference and non-difference would be impossible to know. Even if one accepts a view unsupported by evidence, Brahman would suffer because non-difference is also part of that view. Thus he says:

units.label: Verse 1.78
units.deva: भिन्नाभिन्नं विशेषैश्चेद्दुःखि स्याद्ब्रह्म ते ध्रुवम् । अशेषदुःखिता च स्यादहो प्रज्ञात्मवादिनाम् ॥ ७८॥
units.iast: bhinnābhinnaṃ viśeṣaiścedduḥkhi syādbrahma te dhruvam | aśeṣaduḥkhitā ca syādaho prajñātmavādinām || 78||
units.translation: If Brahman is both different and non-different in its attributes, your Brahman would surely be subject to suffering; indeed, all suffering would belong to those who claim consciousness as the Self—how astonishing!

gloss.en: for those who hold consciousness to be the Self

units.label: Text 246
units.translation: Therefore the conclusion is correct: knowledge and action are not to be combined.

units.label: Verse 1.79
units.deva: तमोऽङ्गत्वं यथा भानोरग्नेश्शीताङ्गता यथा । वारिणश्चोष्णता यद्वज्ज्ञानस्यैवं क्रियाङ्गता ॥ ७९॥
units.iast: tamo'ṅgatvaṃ yathā bhānoragneśśītāṅgatā yathā | vāriṇaścoṣṇatā yadvajjñānasyaivaṃ kriyāṅgatā || 79||
units.translation: Just as darkness cannot be a part of the sun, coldness a part of fire, or heat a part of water, action cannot be a part of knowledge.

units.label: Text 249
units.deva: यथोक्तोपपत्तिबलेनैव पूर्वपक्षस्योत्सारितत्वाद्वक्तव्यं नावशेषितमित्यतः प्रतिपत्तिकर्मवत्पूर्वपक्षपरिहाराय यत्किञ्चिद्वक्तव्यमित्यत इदमभिधीयते ।
units.iast: yathoktopapattibalenaiva pūrvapakṣasyotsāritatvādvaktavyaṃ nāvaśeṣitamityataḥ pratipattikarmavatpūrvapakṣaparihārāya yatkiñcidvaktavyamityata idamabhidhīyate |
units.translation: Since the foregoing reasoning has already removed the opponent’s position, there is nothing further to state. Yet, to answer any remaining objection as one answers an argument with its own counter-argument, he adds:

units.label: Verse 1.80
units.deva: “मुक्तेः क्रियाभिः सिद्धत्वात्” इत्याद्यनुचितं बहु । यदभाणि तदन्याय्यं यथा तदधुनोच्यते ॥ ८०॥
units.iast: “mukteḥ kriyābhiḥ siddhatvāt” ityādyanucitaṃ bahu | yadabhāṇi tadanyāyyaṃ yathā tadadhunocyate || 80||
units.translation: Much of what you said, beginning with “liberation is accomplished by actions,” was unreasonable; I shall now explain why.

units.label: Text 252
units.deva: योऽयं काम्यानां प्रतिषिद्धानां च त्यागः प्रतिज्ञायते सा प्रतिज्ञा तावन्न शक्यतेऽनुष्ठातुम् । किं कारणम् ।
units.iast: yo'yaṃ kāmyānāṃ pratiṣiddhānāṃ ca tyāgaḥ pratijñāyate sā pratijñā tāvanna śakyate'nuṣṭhātum | kiṃ kāraṇam |
units.translation: First, the promise to abandon desire-driven and prohibited actions cannot be carried out. Why?

units.label: Text 253
units.deva: कर्मणो हि निर्वृत्तात्मनो द्वाभ्यां प्रकाराभ्यां निवृत्तिः संभवत्यारब्धफलस्योपभोगेनानारब्धफलस्याशुभस्य प्रायश्चित्तैरिति । तृतीयोऽपि त्यागप्रकारोऽकर्त्रात्मावबोधात् स त्वात्मज्ञानानभ्युपगमाद्भवता नाभ्युपगम्यते । तत्र यान्यनुपभुक्तफलान्यनारब्धफलानि तानीश्वरेणापि केनचिदपि न शक्यन्ते परित्यक्तुम् ।
units.iast: karmaṇo hi nirvṛttātmano dvābhyāṃ prakārābhyāṃ nivṛttiḥ saṃbhavatyārabdhaphalasyopabhogenānārabdhaphalasyāśubhasya prāyaścittairiti | tṛtīyo'pi tyāgaprakāro'kartrātmāvabodhāt sa tvātmajñānānabhyupagamādbhavatā nābhyupagamyate | tatra yānyanupabhuktaphalānyanārabdhaphalāni tānīśvareṇāpi kenacidapi na śakyante parityaktum |
units.translation: Completed actions can cease in two ways: the fruit of an action whose result has begun is exhausted by experience, while harmful action whose result has not begun is removed by expiation. There is also a third way of relinquishment—knowledge of the Self as non-agent—but you do not accept it, since you reject knowledge of the Self. Of these, no one—not even the Lord—can abandon actions whose results have not begun and have not been experienced.

units.label: Text 254
units.deva: अथारब्धफलानि त्यज्यन्ते तान्यपि न शक्यन्ते त्यक्तुम् ।
units.iast: athārabdhaphalāni tyajyante tānyapi na śakyante tyaktum |
units.translation: If one tries to abandon actions whose results have begun, those too cannot be abandoned.

units.label: Text 255
units.deva: किं कारणम् । अनिवृत्तेः । अनिर्वृत्तं हि चिकीर्षितं कर्म शक्यते त्यक्तुं प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्ती प्रति कर्तुः स्वातन्त्र्यात् । निर्वृत्ते तु कर्मणि तदसंभवाद्दुरनुष्ठेयः प्रतिज्ञानार्थः । अशक्यप्रतिज्ञानाच्च । न च शक्यते प्रतिज्ञातुं यावज्जीवं काम्यानि प्रतिषिद्धानि च कर्माणि न करिष्यामीति सुनिपुणानामपि सूक्ष्मापराधदर्शनात् । प्रमाणाभावाच्च ।
units.iast: kiṃ kāraṇam | anivṛtteḥ | anirvṛttaṃ hi cikīrṣitaṃ karma śakyate tyaktuṃ pravṛttinivṛttī prati kartuḥ svātantryāt | nirvṛtte tu karmaṇi tadasaṃbhavādduranuṣṭheyaḥ pratijñānārthaḥ | aśakyapratijñānācca | na ca śakyate pratijñātuṃ yāvajjīvaṃ kāmyāni pratiṣiddhāni ca karmāṇi na kariṣyāmīti sunipuṇānāmapi sūkṣmāparādhadarśanāt | pramāṇābhāvācca |
units.translation: Why? Because they have already been performed. One can abandon an action not yet performed, since an agent is free to undertake it or refrain; once the action is complete, that choice is no longer possible. Thus the promise is hard to keep. Nor can one promise not to perform any desire-driven or prohibited action for the rest of one’s life: even the most careful people discover subtle faults in themselves. There is no authority for such a promise either.

units.label: Text 256
units.deva: न च प्रमाणमस्ति मोक्षकामो नित्यनैमित्तिके कर्मणी कुर्यात्काम्यप्रतिषिद्धे च वर्जयेदारब्धफले चोपभोगेन क्षपयेदिति । आनन्त्याच्च । न चोपचितानां कर्मणामियत्तास्ति संसारस्यानादित्वात् । न च काम्यैः प्रतिषिधैर्वा तेषां निवृत्तिरस्ति शुद्ध्यशुद्धिसाम्ये सत्यविरोधादित्याह ।
units.iast: na ca pramāṇamasti mokṣakāmo nityanaimittike karmaṇī kuryātkāmyapratiṣiddhe ca varjayedārabdhaphale copabhogena kṣapayediti | ānantyācca | na copacitānāṃ karmaṇāmiyattāsti saṃsārasyānāditvāt | na ca kāmyaiḥ pratiṣidhairvā teṣāṃ nivṛttirasti śuddhyaśuddhisāmye satyavirodhādityāha |
units.translation: Nor is there any authority for saying that one seeking liberation should perform obligatory and occasional rites, avoid desire-driven and prohibited actions, and exhaust the fruits of actions already begun by experiencing them. Moreover, no limit can be assigned to the actions accumulated, since saṃsāra has no beginning. Desire-driven and prohibited actions do not cancel one another, because they are not opposed to one another even when their purity and impurity differ. This is stated:

units.label: Verse 1.81
units.translation: The complete renunciation of desire-driven and prohibited actions accumulated over countless past births is not considered possible, since they are infinite.

units.label: Text 259
units.translation: One might hold that actions accumulated through infinitely many past births

units.label: Verse 1.82
units.deva: क्षयो नित्येन तेषां चेत्प्रायश्चित्तैर्यथैनसः । निष्फलत्वान्न नित्येन काम्यादेर्विनिवारणाम् ॥ ८२॥
units.iast: kṣayo nityena teṣāṃ cetprāyaścittairyathainasaḥ | niṣphalatvānna nityena kāmyādervinivāraṇām || 82||
units.translation: If one says that those actions are exhausted by obligatory rites, as sins are by expiations, [we reply] no: obligatory rites are fruitless for removing desire-driven actions.

gloss.en: of desire-driven actions and the rest

units.label: Text 262
units.translation: There is no authority for that claim either. How?

units.label: Verse 1.83
units.deva: पापापनुत्तये वाक्यात्प्रायश्चित्तं यथा तथा । गम्यते काम्यहानार्थं नित्यं कर्म न वाक्यतः ॥ ८३॥
units.iast: pāpāpanuttaye vākyātprāyaścittaṃ yathā tathā | gamyate kāmyahānārthaṃ nityaṃ karma na vākyataḥ || 83||
units.translation: A Vedic statement makes clear that expiation removes sin. No statement says that obligatory action removes desire-driven action.

units.label: Text 265
units.deva: अथापि स्यात्काम्यैरेव काम्यानां पूर्वजन्मोपचितानां क्षयो भविष्यतीति । तन्न । यतः ।
units.iast: athāpi syātkāmyaireva kāmyānāṃ pūrvajanmopacitānāṃ kṣayo bhaviṣyatīti | tanna | yataḥ |
units.translation: One might further say that desire-driven actions themselves will exhaust those from previous births. That is wrong, because:

units.label: Verse 1.84
units.deva: पाप्मनां पाप्मभिर्नास्ति यथैवेह निराक्रिया । काम्यैरपि तथैवास्तु काम्यानामविरोधतः ॥ ८४॥
units.iast: pāpmanāṃ pāpmabhirnāsti yathaiveha nirākriyā | kāmyairapi tathaivāstu kāmyānāmavirodhataḥ || 84||
units.translation: Just as sins are not removed by other sins, desire-driven actions do not remove other desire-driven actions, since they do not oppose one another.

units.label: Text 268
units.deva: एवं तावत् "मुक्तेः क्रियाभिः सिद्धत्वात् " इति निराकृतम् ॥
units.iast: evaṃ tāvat "mukteḥ kriyābhiḥ siddhatvāt " iti nirākṛtam ||
units.translation: Thus the view that liberation is accomplished through actions has been refuted.

units.label: Text 269
units.translation: He now answers the claim that there is no authority establishing knowledge of the Self.

units.label: Verse 1.85
units.deva: श्रुतयः स्मृतिभिः साकमानन्त्यात्कामिनामिह । विदधत्युरुयत्नेन कर्मातो बहुकामदम् ॥ ८५॥
units.iast: śrutayaḥ smṛtibhiḥ sākam ānantyāt kāminām iha | vidadhaty uru-yatnena karmāto bahu-kāma-dam || 85||
units.translation: Because those who desire rewards are countless, the Vedas and traditional texts prescribe, with great effort, rites that promise many desired fruits.

units.label: Text 272
units.deva: न च बाहुल्यं प्रामाण्ये कारणभावं प्रतिपद्यते । अत आह ।
units.iast: na ca bāhulyaṃ prāmāṇye kāraṇabhāvaṃ pratipadyate | ata āha |
units.translation: Multiplicity does not make a statement authoritative. Therefore he says:

units.label: Verse 1.86
units.deva: प्रामाण्याय न बाहुल्यं न ह्येकत्र प्रमाणताम् । वस्तुन्यटन्ति मानानि त्वेकत्रैकस्य मानता ॥ ८६॥
units.iast: prāmāṇyāya na bāhulyaṃ na hyekatra pramāṇatām | vastunyaṭanti mānāni tvekatraikasya mānatā || 86||
units.translation: Numerical abundance does not establish authority: means of knowledge do not all operate on the same object; each has authority in its own domain.

gloss.en: validity as a means of knowledge

units.label: Text 275
units.deva: यत्तूक्तं "यत्नतो वीक्षमाणोऽपि " इति -- तत्रापि भवत एवापराधः । कस्मात् । यतः ।
units.iast: yattūktaṃ "yatnato vīkṣamāṇo'pi " iti -- tatrāpi bhavata evāparādhaḥ | kasmāt | yataḥ |
units.translation: What you said—“even after searching carefully”—is your own fault. Why? Because:

units.label: Verse 1.87
units.deva: “परीक्ष्य लोकान्” इत्याद्या आत्मज्ञानविधायिनीः । नैष्कर्म्यप्रवणास्साध्वीः श्रुतीः किं न शृणोषि ताः ॥ ८७॥
units.iast: “parīkṣya lokān” ityādyā ātmajñānavidhāyinīḥ | naiṣkarmyapravaṇāssādhvīḥ śrutīḥ kiṃ na śṛṇoṣi tāḥ || 87||
units.translation: Why do you not listen to those excellent Vedic passages, beginning with “Having examined the worlds,” that point to knowledge of the Self and lead toward actionlessness?

gloss.en: pointing to knowledge of the Self

units.label: Text 278
units.deva: ननु " आत्मेत्येवोपासीत " "आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः" इत्यपूर्वविधिश्रुतेः पुरुषस्यात्मदर्शनक्रियायां नियोगोऽवसीयत इति । नैवम् ।
units.iast: nanu " ātmetyevopāsīta " "ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ" ityapūrvavidhiśruteḥ puruṣasyātmadarśanakriyāyāṃ niyogo'vasīyata iti | naivam |
units.translation: One may object that statements such as “One should contemplate the Self as the Self” and “the Self should indeed be seen” are novel injunctions, so a person is enjoined to perform the act of seeing the Self. This is not so.

units.label: Text 279
units.translation: True knowledge of reality is not under a person’s control; it removes ignorance, the seed of every misfortune, and is itself the cause of liberation.

units.label: Text 280
units.translation: Even if an injunction is admitted, this is not a novel injunction. He says:

units.label: Verse 1.88
units.deva: नियमः परिसंख्या वा विध्यर्थोऽपि भवेद्यतः । अनात्मादर्शनेनैव परात्मानमुपास्महे ॥ ८८॥
units.iast: niyamaḥ parisaṃkhyā vā vidhyartho'pi bhavedyataḥ | anātmādarśanenaiva parātmānamupāsmahe || 88||
units.translation: If an injunction is accepted, its force may be restriction or exclusion; we contemplate the Supreme Self precisely by not attending to the not-Self.

units.label: Text 283
units.deva: यच्चोक्तं "विश्वासो नान्यतोऽस्ति नः" इति -- तदपि निद्रातुरचेतसा त्वया स्वप्नायमानेन प्रलपितम् । किं कारणम् । न हि वयं प्रमाणबलेनैकात्म्यं प्रतिपद्यामह ऐकात्म्यस्य स्वत एवानुभवमात्रात्मकत्वात् । अत एव सर्वप्रमाणावतारासंभवं वक्ष्यति ।
units.iast: yaccoktaṃ "viśvāso nānyato'sti naḥ" iti -- tadapi nidrāturacetasā tvayā svapnāyamānena pralapitam | kiṃ kāraṇam | na hi vayaṃ pramāṇabalenaikātmyaṃ pratipadyāmaha aikātmyasya svata evānubhavamātrātmakatvāt | ata eva sarvapramāṇāvatārāsaṃbhavaṃ vakṣyati |
units.translation: What you said—“we trust no other source”—was also a dreamlike utterance from a mind drowsy with ignorance. Why? We do not arrive at non-duality through the force of a means of knowledge; oneness is itself nothing but direct experience. For this very reason he will show that no means of knowledge can operate [on what is already self-evident].

units.label: Text 284
units.translation: For the ordering of the means of knowledge itself rests on direct experience.

units.label: Text 285
units.translation: Therefore he says:

units.label: Verse 1.89
units.deva: वाक्यैकगम्यं यद्वस्तु नान्यस्मात्तत्र विश्वसेत् । नाप्रमेये स्वतस्सिद्धेऽविश्वासः कथमात्मनि ॥ ८९॥
