units.translation: If this method is enjoined for direct realization of the Self, then a person must turn away from all good and evil actions, make the mind one-pointed, and realize the Self through the agreement and exclusion described above.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 16
units.deva: अपरिसमाप्यात्मदर्शनं ततः प्रच्यवमान आरूढपतितो भवति । यदि पुनर्यदृच्छातः प्रवर्तते तदा न कश्चिद्दोष इति । विधिपरिप्रापित इति ब्रूमो यत आह ।
units.iast: aparisamāpyātmadarśanaṃ tataḥ pracyavamāna ārūḍhapatito bhavati | yadi punaryadṛcchātaḥ pravartate tadā na kaściddoṣa iti | vidhipariprāpita iti brūmo yata āha |
units.translation: If he falls away before completing realization of the Self, he becomes one who has fallen from the path. But if he takes it up by chance, there is no fault. We say it is enjoined, because scripture says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 17
units.translation: Using means such as tranquillity, one should clearly see

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.4
units.translation: the Self in the Self, having completely set aside the meaning of “you” through agreement and exclusion.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 19
units.translation: When the meaning of “you” has been abandoned through the reasons already given, scripture

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.5
units.translation: compassionately tells the one who has entered inquiry, “That thou art.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 21
units.deva: अत्रापि चोदयन्ति सांख्याः । शरीरेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिष्वनात्मस्वात्मेति निस्सन्धिबन्धनं मिथ्याज्ञानमज्ञानं तन्निबन्धनो ह्यात्मनोऽनेकानर्थसंबन्धस्तस्य चान्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यामेव निरस्तत्त्वान्निर्विषयं तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यं प्राप्तम् । तस्माद्वाक्यस्य चैष महिमा योऽयमात्मानात्मनोर्विभाग इति । तन्निराकरणायेदमुच्यते ।
units.iast: atrāpi codayanti sāṃkhyāḥ | śarīrendriyamanobuddhiṣvanātmasvātmeti nissandhibandhanaṃ mithyājñānamajñānaṃ tannibandhano hyātmano'nekānarthasaṃbandhastasya cānvayavyatirekābhyāmeva nirastattvānnirviṣayaṃ tattvamasyādivākyaṃ prāptam | tasmādvākyasya caiṣa mahimā yo'yamātmānātmanorvibhāga iti | tannirākaraṇāyedamucyate |
units.translation: The Sāṃkhyas object: “Ignorance is the unbroken false cognition ‘I am’ regarding what is not-Self—the body, senses, mind, and intellect. The Self’s many connections with misery are rooted in this ignorance, which has been removed by agreement and exclusion. Therefore sentences such as ‘That thou art’ have no object; their only function is to distinguish the Self from not-Self.” This is answered:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 22
units.translation: The cognition of difference and the absence of difference in the witness

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.6
units.translation: are both effects of ignorance; a sentence removes them through knowledge of the Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 24
units.translation: On hearing the words “a sentence removes them through knowledge of the Self,” someone asks:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 25
units.deva: मिथ्याज्ञानव्यतिरेकेणात्मानवबोधस्याभावात्किं वाक्येन निवर्तते । अज्ञानं हि नाम ज्ञानाभावस्तस्य चावस्तुस्वाभाव्यात्कुतः संसारकारणत्वं न ह्यसतः सज्जन्मेष्यते "कुतस्तु खलु सोम्यैवं स्यात् " इति "कथमसतः सज्जायेत " इति श्रुतेरिति । अत्रोच्यते ।
units.iast: mithyājñānavyatirekeṇātmānavabodhasyābhāvātkiṃ vākyena nivartate | ajñānaṃ hi nāma jñānābhāvastasya cāvastusvābhāvyātkutaḥ saṃsārakāraṇatvaṃ na hyasataḥ sajjanmeṣyate "kutastu khalu somyaivaṃ syāt " iti "kathamasataḥ sajjāyeta " iti śruteriti | atrocyate |
units.translation: “Apart from false cognition, there is no separate ignorance of the Self; what, then, is removed by the sentence? Ignorance is merely the absence of knowledge, and, being unreal, how could it cause saṃsāra? What is unreal does not give birth to what is real. Scripture says, ‘How could this be so, dear one?’ and ‘How could the real arise from the unreal?’” The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 26
units.translation: Before cognition arises, every object is unknown;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.7
units.translation: yet it exists, and through the one real [Self] the unknown becomes manifest.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 28
units.translation: The previous verse has said that what exists may yet be unknown.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 29
units.translation: When one asks, “What is that existent yet unknown thing?”, its nature is stated:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 30
units.translation: That which shines by itself when one seeks to know,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.8
units.translation: and is established by its own glory, is to be understood as the reality not yet known.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 32
units.deva: अत्र केचिदाहुः । यत्किंचिदिह वाक्यं लौकिकं वैदिकं वा तत्सर्वं संसर्गात्मकमेव वाक्यार्थं गमयति ।
units.iast: atra kecidāhuḥ | yatkiṃcidiha vākyaṃ laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ vā tatsarvaṃ saṃsargātmakameva vākyārthaṃ gamayati |
units.translation: Some say that every sentence, whether worldly or Vedic, conveys a meaning based on relation.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 33
units.deva: अतस्तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्येभ्यः संसर्गात्मकमहं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञाय तावन्निदिध्यासीत यावदवाक्यार्थात्मकः प्रत्यगात्मविषयोऽवबोधोऽहं ब्रह्मेति समभिजायते ।
units.iast: atastattvamasyādivākyebhyaḥ saṃsargātmakamahaṃ brahmeti vijñāya tāvannididhyāsīta yāvadavākyārthātmakaḥ pratyagātmaviṣayo'vabodho'haṃ brahmeti samabhijāyate |
units.translation: Therefore, from sentences such as “That thou art,” one first understands the relational meaning “I am Brahman,” then meditates until direct knowledge of the inward Self arises, beyond the meaning of the sentence.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 34
units.translation: They say liberation is attained from that very knowledge. To refute this, it is said:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 35
units.translation: Just as when “pot” and “not-pot” are distinguished,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.9
units.translation: the meanings of “That” and “thou” are directly understood as beyond relation.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 37
units.translation: If one asks how a meaning beyond relation is understood, the power of qualifier and qualified is explained:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 38
units.translation: The absence of suffering in the meaning of “thou” qualifies the meaning of “That,”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.10
units.translation: and the inwardness of the meaning of “That” is brought near by the word “thou.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 40
units.translation: Apposition and the relation between qualifier and qualified have been stated briefly; he now explains what is indicated and its indication:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 41
units.translation: The changeless awareness and inwardness of the Self are always present;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.11
units.translation: they are the basis for the intellect’s knowing and its sense of “I”; through these the Self is indicated.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 43
units.deva: बुद्धेः कूटस्थबोधप्रत्यक्त्वनिमित्ते बोद्धृताप्रत्यक्त्वे ये त्वसाधारणे तयोर्विशेषवचनम् ।
units.iast: buddheḥ kūṭasthabodhapratyaktvanimitte boddhṛtāpratyaktve ye tvasādhāraṇe tayorviśeṣavacanam |
units.translation: The intellect’s inwardness is due to changeless awareness; its distinctive features—knowing and the sense of “I”—are explained:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 44
units.translation: The intellect’s knowing is its agency; through the “I”-notion it becomes an object;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.12
units.translation: just as those two are joined in the intellect, so they are spoken of as one in the Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 46
units.deva: यथा बुद्धौ पूर्वयोरेवमात्मनीत्यतिदेशेन बुद्धिसाधर्म्य विधानान्नानात्वप्रसक्तौ तदपवादार्थमाह ।
units.iast: yathā buddhau pūrvayorevamātmanītyatideśena buddhisādharmya vidhānānnānātvaprasaktau tadapavādārthamāha |
units.translation: Since the comparison would imply that the Self shares the intellect’s properties and is therefore many, he rejects that implication:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 47
units.translation: Even that distinction between property and its bearer does not belong to the Self;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.13
units.translation: the inward light is therefore undivided, since no cause of division exists.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 49
units.translation: He shows that there is no cause of division:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 50
units.translation: In no state are awareness and inwardness separate;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.14
units.translation: otherwise they would vary, as the sense of “I” and the sense of being a knower always do.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 52
units.translation: Since only the intellect, produced by ignorance, is divided and not the Self, this is established:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 53
units.translation: changeless awareness is non-dual, and the Self is directly inward;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.15
units.translation: the intellect that knows arises from changeless awareness, but by itself is perishable.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 55
units.deva: अथाधुना प्रकृतस्यैव परिणामिनः कूटस्थस्य च लक्षणमुच्यते ।
units.iast: athādhunā prakṛtasyaiva pariṇāminaḥ kūṭasthasya ca lakṣaṇamucyate |
units.translation: The changing and the changeless, which are under discussion, are now defined.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 56
units.translation: That whose nature is understood by depending on some particular feature

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.16
units.translation: is changing, like the body, as established by recognition.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 58
units.translation: That which exists by its own nature, apart from both general and particular features,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.17
units.translation: is changeless even when distinctions fall away, like space within a pot.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 60
units.translation: The inward awareness of both the Self and the intellect has been stated; their distinctive marks are now given:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 61
units.translation: the intellect’s inwardness depends on the body and the rest;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.18
units.translation: but the Self’s nature is its own, like the subtle expanse of space.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 63
units.translation: The intellect is a knower because it gives rise to cognitions;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.19
units.translation: the Self’s own nature remains as it is, like mountains that stand firm.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 65
units.deva: तयोः कूटस्थपरिणामिनोरात्मानवबोध एव संबन्धहेतुर्न पुनर्वास्तवः कश्चिदपि संबन्ध उपपद्यत इत्याह ।
units.iast: tayoḥ kūṭasthapariṇāminorātmānavabodha eva saṃbandhaheturna punarvāstavaḥ kaścidapi saṃbandha upapadyata ityāha |
units.translation: Ignorance alone is the supposed link between the changeless Self and the changing intellect; no real connection between them is possible.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 66
units.translation: The intellect alone is divided into right knowledge, doubt, and error;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.20
units.translation: through delusion, the witness imagines that it accepts and rejects those states.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 68
units.translation: If one asks how the changeless Self is established, it is because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 69
units.translation: It is not a mere cessation, nor is it an arising;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.21
units.translation: it is established apart from those, distinct from both acceptance and rejection.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 71
units.translation: Thus:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 72
units.translation: Having removed every not-Self through causes that arise and pass away,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.22
units.translation: the sentence “That thou art” destroys its own darkness within us.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 74
units.deva: इत्यादि पुनःपुनरुच्यते ग्रन्थलाघवाद्बुद्धिलाघवं प्रयोजकमिति । तत्र यद्यपि तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यादुपादित्सिताद्वितीयात्मार्थवत्पारोक्ष्यसद्वितीयार्थः प्रतीयते ।
units.iast: ityādi punaḥpunarucyate granthalāghavādbuddhilāghavaṃ prayojakamiti | tatra yadyapi tattvamasyādivākyādupāditsitādvitīyātmārthavatpārokṣyasadvitīyārthaḥ pratīyate |
units.translation: This point is repeated again and again because the brevity of the treatise is meant to aid understanding. Although “That thou art” may appear to convey both the intended non-dual Self and a remote, dual meaning,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 75
units.deva: तथापि तु नैवासावर्थः श्रुत्या तात्पर्येण प्रतिपिपादयिषितः प्रागपेतस्य प्रतीतत्वादितीममर्थमाह ।
units.iast: tathāpi tu naivāsāvarthaḥ śrutyā tātparyeṇa pratipipādayiṣitaḥ prāgapetasya pratītatvāditīmamarthamāha |
units.translation: that remote meaning is not what revelation intends, since it has already been understood before the sentence. He says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 76
units.translation: In ordinary usage the word “That” conveys many meanings,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.23
units.translation: yet it does not abandon the remoteness produced by the word;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 78
units.translation: the word “thou,” too, directly expresses its immediate meaning,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.24
units.translation: and if it does not abandon saṃsāric identity, that meaning too is produced by the word.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 80
units.translation: Since remoteness and suffering are contradictory purposes, they are not intended here. He says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 81
units.translation: A meaning stated in a sentence is not thereby endowed with the force of direct denotation.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.25
units.translation: It enters into relation with the meaning required by the sentence.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 83
units.translation: Since this is so, even though the meanings of “that” and “thou” are not directly asserted in their contradictory forms, their relation as qualifier and qualified serves only to reveal the sentence meaning, which is free of a relation between separate things. This is the conclusion.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 84
units.translation: “That” has the force of a qualifier; “thou” has the force of what is qualified.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.26
units.translation: Their relation, as indicated and indicator, is through the innermost Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 86
units.translation: How can the meaning of an indicator be something whose contradictory, unintended sense is being negated?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 87
units.translation: The inner Self is like the rope; the “I” that is taken to be the Self is like the snake.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.27
units.translation: Through the sublation of that mistaken appearance, one understands the sentence meaning; even the sublation depends on the underlying reality.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 89
units.translation: This understanding of the sentence meaning belongs to one who knows agreement and difference through presence and absence.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 90
units.translation: For this reason:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 91
units.translation: As one keeps negating the body and the rest, turning toward the innermost Self,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.28
units.translation: so, in each step, the meaning of “that” enters into the meaning of “thou.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 93
units.deva: कस्मात्पुनः कारणाद्देहाद्यनात्मत्वप्रतिपत्तावेवात्मा तदर्थमात्मत्वेनाभिलिङ्गते न विपर्यय इति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: kasmātpunaḥ kāraṇāddehādyanātmatvapratipattāvevātmā tadarthamātmatvenābhiliṅgate na viparyaya iti | ucyate |
units.translation: Why, when one recognizes the body and the rest as not-Self, is the Self marked out as the meaning of “that” by its very Selfhood, and not the reverse? The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 94
units.deva: प्रत्यगात्मानवबोधस्यनात्मस्वाभाव्यात्तदभिनिर्वृत्तश्चायं बुद्ध्यादिदेहान्तस्तस्मिन्नात्मत्वमविद्याकृतमेवात्मत्वमिवानात्मत्वमपि साविद्यस्यैव । यतो निरविद्यो विद्वानवाक्यार्थरूप एव केवलोऽवशिष्यते तस्मादुच्यते ।
units.iast: pratyagātmānavabodhasyanātmasvābhāvyāttadabhinirvṛttaścāyaṃ buddhyādidehāntastasminnātmatvamavidyākṛtamevātmatvamivānātmatvamapi sāvidyasyaiva | yato niravidyo vidvānavākyārtharūpa eva kevalo'vaśiṣyate tasmāducyate |
units.translation: Because the innermost Self is not recognized, the mind and everything down to the body arise as not-Self; Selfhood attributed to them is created by ignorance. For one still under ignorance, even their apparent not-Selfhood is likewise bound up with ignorance. Once ignorance is gone, the knower remains alone as the very meaning of the sentence, beyond direct designation. Therefore it is said:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 95
units.translation: Because the body and the rest stand between the knower and that meaning, even the Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.29
units.translation: knows it only indirectly; the meaning of “thou,” which is not-Self, is known directly.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 97
units.translation: An example is offered to make the stated point easier to understand.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 98
units.translation: Just as a person whose bile has risen inwardly sees an external white object as yellow,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.30
units.translation: so the consciousness belonging to the innermost Self appears to be outside.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 100
units.translation: Since this is so, understand the point clearly:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 101
units.translation: By drawing out the words from the sentences, through agreement and difference,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.31
units.translation: and learning their meanings from common usage, one readily understands the meaning of the sentence.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 103
units.deva: कुतः पुनः सामान्यमात्रवृत्तेः पदस्य वाक्यार्थप्रतिपत्तिहेतुत्वमिति । बाढम् ।
units.iast: kutaḥ punaḥ sāmānyamātravṛtteḥ padasya vākyārthapratipattihetutvamiti | bāḍham |
units.translation: How can a word, which applies only to a general meaning, serve as a means of understanding the meaning of a sentence? The reply is: Certainly it can.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 104
units.deva: सामान्यं हि पदं ब्रूते विशेषो वाक्यकर्तृकः ।
units.iast: sāmānyaṃ hi padaṃ brūte viśeṣo vākyakartṛkaḥ |
units.translation: A word expresses a general meaning; the sentence-maker supplies the particular.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.32
units.translation: When constrained by scripture and the other sources of context, a word conveys a particular meaning.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 106
units.deva: अन्वयव्यतिरेकपुरस्सरं वाक्यमेव सामानाधिकरण्यादिनाविद्या पटलप्रध्वंसद्वारेण मुमुक्षुं स्वाराज्येऽभिषेचयति न त्वन्वयव्यतिरेकमात्रसाध्योऽयमर्थ इत्याह ।
units.iast: anvayavyatirekapurassaraṃ vākyameva sāmānādhikaraṇyādināvidyā paṭalapradhvaṃsadvāreṇa mumukṣuṃ svārājye'bhiṣecayati na tvanvayavyatirekamātrasādhyo'yamartha ityāha |
units.translation: It is the sentence itself, using co-reference and the like, preceded by reasoning through agreement and difference, that destroys the veil of ignorance and enthrones the seeker in his own sovereignty. This meaning is not established by agreement and difference alone, as the following verse says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 107
units.translation: The not-Selfhood of the mind and the rest can also be established by inference.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.33
units.translation: Yet that alone does not bring ignorance to an end; therefore, through the teaching “not this,” one should take refuge in the sentence of scripture.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 109
units.translation: He says that one who relies on inference alone not only fails to attain the desired meaning but also falls into error:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 110
units.translation: Through delusion, the Buddhists who disregard scripture, shrouded in darkness,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.34
units.translation: with inference as their only eye, have arrived at the doctrine that there is no Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 112
units.deva: न चानादरे कारणमस्ति । यस्मात्सर्वत्रैवानादरनिमित्तं प्रमाणस्य प्रमाणान्तरप्रतिपन्नप्रतिपादनं वा विपरीतप्रतिपादनं वा संशयितप्रतिपादनं वा न वा प्रतिपादनमिति -- न चैतेषामन्यतमदपि कारणमस्ति ।
units.iast: na cānādare kāraṇamasti | yasmātsarvatraivānādaranimittaṃ pramāṇasya pramāṇāntarapratipannapratipādanaṃ vā viparītapratipādanaṃ vā saṃśayitapratipādanaṃ vā na vā pratipādanamiti -- na caiteṣāmanyatamadapi kāraṇamasti |
units.translation: There is no reason to disregard scripture. A means of knowledge may be set aside if it merely repeats what another means has established, teaches the opposite, leaves its result doubtful, or yields no result. None of these is the case here.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 113
units.translation: For scripture says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 114
units.translation: “The scripture that clearly teaches the sorrowless Self, untouched by any other means of knowledge—

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.35
units.translation: by what grounds could it be declared no means of knowledge?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 116
units.translation: Nor does it leave the matter uncertain, because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 117
units.translation: When every cause of doubt has been removed, how could doubt arise about the Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.36
units.translation: from the sentence, when inference concerns what is other than oneself?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 119
units.translation: Moreover:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 120
units.deva: यत्र स्यात्संशयो नासौ ज्ञेय आत्मेति पण्डितैः ।
units.iast: yatra syātsaṃśayo nāsau jñeya ātmeti paṇḍitaiḥ |
units.translation: “That in which doubt could arise is not held by the wise to be the knowable Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.37
units.translation: “—not, because the Self is ever directly known.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 122
units.translation: That scripture is unable to reveal the Self has already been ruled out completely. For it says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 123
units.translation: “For one who has no experience of awareness at all,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.38
units.translation: how could scripture awaken him? He would be like a stone shaped as a human being.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 125
units.deva: अन्वयव्यतिरेकपुरस्सरं वाक्यमेवावाक्यार्थरूपमात्मानं प्रतिपादयतीत्यस्य पक्षस्य द्रढिम्न श्रुत्युदाहरणमुपन्यस्यति ।
units.iast: anvayavyatirekapurassaraṃ vākyamevāvākyārtharūpamātmānaṃ pratipādayatītyasya pakṣasya draḍhimna śrutyudāharaṇamupanyasyati |
units.translation: To strengthen the view that the sentence of scripture, preceded by reasoning through agreement and difference, teaches the Self beyond ordinary sentence meaning, he gives a scriptural example:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 126
units.translation: “I smell this fragrance”—the changeless knower of that experience

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.39
units.deva: स आत्मा तत्परं ज्योतिः शिरसीदं वचः श्रुतेः ॥ ३९॥
units.iast: sa ātmā tatparaṃ jyotiḥ śirasīdaṃ vacaḥ śruteḥ || 39||
units.translation: is the Self, the supreme light. This is the declaration of scripture.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 128
units.deva: यथा "तत्सत्यं स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि " इत्यस्य शेषत्वेनान्वयव्यतिरेकश्रुतिर्यथा "य एषोऽक्षिणिपुरुषो दृश्यते " इत्याद्या "अथ यो वेदेदं जिघ्राणि " इत्यन्ता तथा "अहं ब्रह्मास्मि " इत्यस्य शेषः ।
units.iast: yathā "tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tattvamasi " ityasya śeṣatvenānvayavyatirekaśrutiryathā "ya eṣo'kṣiṇipuruṣo dṛśyate " ityādyā "atha yo vededaṃ jighrāṇi " ityantā tathā "ahaṃ brahmāsmi " ityasya śeṣaḥ |
units.translation: Just as the teaching “That is the real; that is the Self; you are that” is clarified by the passages on agreement and difference beginning “the person seen in the eye” and ending “now, the one who knows ‘I smell this’,” so too those passages explain “I am Brahman.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 129
units.translation: “The meaning of ‘I’ is the innermost Self, with every meaning of ‘you’ negated.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.40
units.translation: Scripture repeatedly teaches this with the words ‘this one’ and the like; this is the fitting interpretation.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 131
units.deva: कथं पुनरयमर्थोऽवसीयते अहंव्याजेनात्रात्मार्थो बुबोधयिषित इति । यतः ।
units.iast: kathaṃ punarayamartho'vasīyate ahaṃvyājenātrātmārtho bubodhayiṣita iti | yataḥ |
units.translation: How is it established that the intended meaning of the word “I” here is the Self? Because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 132
units.translation: “This Self is self-luminous; it is the one present in the sun, moon, fire and speech.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.41
units.translation: When these lights have set, it alone remains as the seer, illuminating the activity of the mind.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 134
units.translation: The sage explains the point in response to a question:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 135
units.translation: “When the reply ‘by the Self alone’ was heard, the question was asked, ‘What is this Self?’

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.42
units.translation: The sage described the Self as beyond the intellect and free in its own nature.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 137
units.deva: यस्माच्चात्मात्राहंव्याजेन प्रत्यङ्मात्रो जिग्राहयिषितस्तस्मादहंवृत्तिः स्वरूपस्य विलयेनैव वाक्यार्थावगमाय कारणत्वं प्रतिपद्यत इतीममर्थमाह ।
units.iast: yasmāccātmātrāhaṃvyājena pratyaṅmātro jigrāhayiṣitastasmādahaṃvṛttiḥ svarūpasya vilayenaiva vākyārthāvagamāya kāraṇatvaṃ pratipadyata itīmamarthamāha |
units.translation: Because the Self meant here by “I” is intended to be understood as the innermost witness alone, the “I”-thought serves to reveal the sentence meaning only by dissolving into its own true nature. This is expressed in the following verse:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 138
units.translation: “Through the ‘I’-thought alone one understands that Brahman;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.43
units.translation: therefore the ego becomes the means by dissolving into its own nature.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 140
units.deva: अत एव च यः प्रतिज्ञातोऽर्थो "नाहंग्राह्ये न तद्धीने "इत्यादिः स युक्तिभिरुपपादित इति कृत्वोपसंह्रियते ।
units.iast: ata eva ca yaḥ pratijñāto'rtho "nāhaṃgrāhye na taddhīne "ityādiḥ sa yuktibhirupapādita iti kṛtvopasaṃhriyate |
units.translation: Thus the point stated earlier—that the Self is not grasped as an object, nor dependent on an object—is established by reasoning. The author concludes:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 141
units.translation: “If the meaning of ‘I’ has been grasped, why does the knower not attain it?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.44
units.translation: If you say it conflicts with perception and the other means of knowledge, the inward teaching concerns no ‘you’ at all.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 143
units.translation: He clarifies the meaning of the preceding verse:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 144
units.translation: “Perception and the other means of knowledge are directed outward; they do not reach the Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.45
units.translation: The statement ‘You are that’ plainly concerns what is inward.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 146
units.translation: Therefore, using agreement and difference, one should separate the Self from the knower, means of knowledge and objects of knowledge that are taken up and discarded, as one draws the pith from a reed. Then, from sentences such as “you are that,” one should know the Self as beyond anything previously established. This is stated here:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 147
units.deva: अहं दुःखी सुखी चेति येनायं प्रत्ययोऽध्रुवः ।
units.iast: ahaṃ duḥkhī sukhī ceti yenāyaṃ pratyayo'dhruvaḥ |
units.translation: “The one by whom this fleeting thought ‘I am unhappy’ or ‘I am happy’

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.46
units.deva: अवगत्यन्त आभाति स म आत्मेति वाक्यधीः ॥ ४६॥
units.iast: avagatyanta ābhāti sa ma ātmeti vākyadhīḥ || 46||
units.translation: is known, and in whom it comes to awareness, is my Self”—such is the understanding born of the sentence.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 149
units.deva: प्रमाणान्तरानवष्टब्धं निरस्ताशेषकार्यकारणात्मकद्वैतप्रपञ्चं सत्यज्ञानानन्दलक्षणमात्मानं तत्त्वमस्यहंब्रह्मास्मीत्यादिवाक्यं संशयितमिथ्याज्ञानाज्ञानप्रध्वंसमुखेन साक्षादपरोक्षात्करतलन्यस्तामलकवत्प्रतिपादयत्येवेत्यसकृदभिहितम् । तत्र केचिदाहुः -- तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यैर्यथावस्थितवस्तुयाथात्म्यान्वाख्याननिष्ठैर्नयथोक्तोऽर्थः प्रतिपत्तुं शक्यतेऽभिधाश्रुतित्वात्तेषाम् ।
units.iast: pramāṇāntarānavaṣṭabdhaṃ nirastāśeṣakāryakāraṇātmakadvaitaprapañcaṃ satyajñānānandalakṣaṇamātmānaṃ tattvamasyahaṃbrahmāsmītyādivākyaṃ saṃśayitamithyājñānājñānapradhvaṃsamukhena sākṣādaparokṣātkaratalanyastāmalakavatpratipādayatyevetyasakṛdabhihitam | tatra kecidāhuḥ -- tattvamasyādivākyairyathāvasthitavastuyāthātmyānvākhyānaniṣṭhairnayathokto'rthaḥ pratipattuṃ śakyate'bhidhāśrutitvātteṣām |
units.translation: It has been said repeatedly that a sentence such as “you are that” or “I am Brahman” does directly reveal the Self—whose nature is reality, awareness and bliss, untouched by any other means of knowledge and free of the entire duality of effects and causes—by removing doubt, false knowledge and ignorance, like a fruit placed in one’s palm. Some object: “Sentences such as ‘you are that,’ which merely describe the nature of an existing thing as it is, cannot reveal the meaning you claim, because they are heard in their literal, declarative sense.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 150
units.deva: न हि लोकेऽभिधाश्रुतेः प्रमाणान्तरनिरपेक्षायानद्यास्तीरे फलानि सन्तीत्यादिकायाः प्रामाण्यमभ्युपगतम् ।
units.iast: na hi loke'bhidhāśruteḥ pramāṇāntaranirapekṣāyānadyāstīre phalāni santītyādikāyāḥ prāmāṇyamabhyupagatam |
units.translation: For in ordinary usage, the authority of a literal statement that needs no other means of knowledge—such as ‘fruit is on the far bank of the river’—is not accepted.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 151
units.deva: अतो नियोगमुखेनैवाभिधाश्रुतेः प्रामाण्यं युक्तं प्रमाणान्तरनिरपेक्षत्वान्नियोगस्य । अस्य परिहारार्थमशेषप्रत्यक्षादिप्रमेयत्वनिराकरणद्वारेणातीन्द्रियार्थविषयत्वादभिधाश्रुतेः प्रामाण्यं सुप्तपुरुषप्रबोधकवाक्यस्येव वक्तव्यमित्ययमारम्भः ।
units.iast: ato niyogamukhenaivābhidhāśruteḥ prāmāṇyaṃ yuktaṃ pramāṇāntaranirapekṣatvānniyogasya | asya parihārārthamaśeṣapratyakṣādiprameyatvanirākaraṇadvāreṇātīndriyārthaviṣayatvādabhidhāśruteḥ prāmāṇyaṃ suptapuruṣaprabodhakavākyasyeva vaktavyamityayamārambhaḥ |
units.translation: They therefore claim that a literal scriptural statement is authoritative only as an injunction, since an injunction does not depend on another means of knowledge. To answer this, the author begins: a literal scriptural statement is authoritative about a supersensible matter, because that matter is not an object of perception and the other means of knowledge—just as a sentence that awakens a sleeping person is authoritative.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 152
units.translation: “Because it is the very nature of constant awareness, it does not depend on another means of knowledge;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.47
units.translation: and because it is free of qualities such as sound, doubt cannot arise about it.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 154
units.translation: “When craving has been cast away, the Self is not known through perception and the other means of knowledge;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.48
units.translation: because it is the innermost Self, it is not an object of knowledge but the very ground of knowing.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 156
units.translation: Scripture states this same point:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 157
units.translation: “Because sight is directed toward limited outward forms, colors and the like,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.49
units.translation: one does not see what is the opposite of them—the Self, already aware by itself.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 159
units.translation: For this reason scripture states what reason establishes: the Self is the seer of seeing.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.50
units.translation: “One should not see the innermost Self as an object; scripture itself is the means of knowledge, and it declares this emphatically.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 161
units.translation: Another reason is given for why the Self is not an object of inference:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 162
units.translation: “Perception is directed outward, and therefore cannot grasp the relation [between knower and known];

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.51
units.translation: so inference, too, can never yield direct experience of the Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 164
units.deva: एवमयं प्रमातृप्रमाणप्रमेयव्यवहारः सर्व एव पराचीनविषय एव न प्रतीचिनमात्मानमवगाहयितुमलम् ।
units.iast: evamayaṃ pramātṛpramāṇaprameyavyavahāraḥ sarva eva parācīnaviṣaya eva na pratīcinamātmānamavagāhayitumalam |
units.translation: Thus the entire transaction of knower, means of knowledge and known objects concerns things outward; it cannot reach the inward Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 165
units.deva: एवं च सत्यनेनैव यथोक्तोऽर्थोऽवसातुं शक्यत इत्याह ।
units.iast: evaṃ ca satyanenaiva yathokto'rtho'vasātuṃ śakyata ityāha |
units.translation: Since this is so, the point already explained can be established by this very reasoning:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 166
units.translation: “Every transaction of knowledge is directed outward;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.52
units.translation: even after careful examination, by this means one seeks only what is other than oneself.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 168
units.translation: Since the sentence meaning “I am Brahman” cannot be reached by ordinary perception and the other means of knowledge:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 169
units.translation: “Having negated what does not breathe and the rest through agreement and difference, the sage turns inward and asks, ‘Who am I?’

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.53
units.translation: To that one who has become discerning, scripture declares: ‘You are that.’”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 171
units.translation: This reasoning through agreement and difference culminates in the sentence meaning becoming clear to one who understands it: “I am Brahman.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 172
units.translation: The distinction between seer and seen, and between the witness and what arises and subsides, is stated here in a concise form accepted by scripture:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 173
units.translation: “Because it is seen, the body is like a pot; the senses, too, are like the body.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.54
units.translation: The mind is known like the senses, and its judgments and other states are known like the mind.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 175
units.translation: The same point follows from the Self’s witnessing all effects and causes as they arise and disappear:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 176
units.translation: “What was absent before comes into being later; what exists may later become absent.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.55
units.translation: What has that nature belongs to the not-Self; the opposite is the seeing Self itself.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 178
units.deva: तत्र घटादीनां दृश्यानामनात्मत्वं द्रष्ट्रात्मपूर्वकं प्रत्यक्षेणैव प्रमाणेनोपलभ्यानात्मनश्चासाधारणान् धर्मानवधार्य तैर्दृश्यत्वागमापायादिभिर्धर्मैः शरीरेन्द्रियमनोनिश्चयादिवृत्तीरनात्मतया व्युदस्याहंवृत्तिमतोऽपि दृश्यत्वाविशेषाद्द्रष्टृपूर्वकत्वमवसीयते । तदेतदाह ।
units.iast: tatra ghaṭādīnāṃ dṛśyānāmanātmatvaṃ draṣṭrātmapūrvakaṃ pratyakṣeṇaiva pramāṇenopalabhyānātmanaścāsādhāraṇān dharmānavadhārya tairdṛśyatvāgamāpāyādibhirdharmaiḥ śarīrendriyamanoniścayādivṛttīranātmatayā vyudasyāhaṃvṛttimato'pi dṛśyatvāviśeṣāddraṣṭṛpūrvakatvamavasīyate | tadetadāha |
units.translation: The not-Selfhood of visible things such as pots is directly evident, with the seer as its ground. Their distinctive properties are recognized; then, by their being seen and by their arising and passing away, the body, senses, mind and its judgments are set aside as not-Self. Since the “I”-thought is also seen, it too is known to depend on a seer. This is expressed as follows:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 179
units.translation: “Just as pots and the like are signs of the ‘I’ by a chain of dependence,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.56
units.translation: so the ‘I’ itself, because it is seen, is a sign of the witnessing Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 181
units.deva: ननु द्रष्टृदर्शनदृश्यानां जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तेष्वागमापायदर्शनाद्यसाक्षिकौ तेषामागमापायौ स आगमापायविभागरहित आत्मा यथा यन्निबन्धनौ जगतः प्रकाशाप्रकाशौ स प्रकाशाप्रकाशविभागरहितः सूर्य इति ।
units.iast: nanu draṣṭṛdarśanadṛśyānāṃ jāgratsvapnasuṣupteṣvāgamāpāyadarśanādyasākṣikau teṣāmāgamāpāyau sa āgamāpāyavibhāgarahita ātmā yathā yannibandhanau jagataḥ prakāśāprakāśau sa prakāśāprakāśavibhāgarahitaḥ sūrya iti |
units.translation: One might object: the seer, seeing and seen are all observed to arise and disappear in waking, dream and deep sleep. Their arising and disappearance are known by a witness; that witness is the Self, free of arising and disappearance. Just as the sun, on which the world’s light and darkness depend, is free of that division—

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 182
units.deva: यदा चैवं तदा वाक्यावगम्यस्यार्थस्यानुदितानस्तमितविज्ञानमात्रस्वभावस्यानुमानेनैव प्रतिपन्नत्वात्पुनरपि वाक्यस्य निर्विषयत्वप्रसङ्गः । नैष दोषः ।
units.iast: yadā caivaṃ tadā vākyāvagamyasyārthasyānuditānastamitavijñānamātrasvabhāvasyānumānenaiva pratipannatvātpunarapi vākyasya nirviṣayatvaprasaṅgaḥ | naiṣa doṣaḥ |
units.translation: if so, the meaning taught by the sentence, whose nature is awareness without beginning or end, has already been established by inference. The scriptural sentence would then have no subject matter. This is no fault:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 183
units.deva: लिङ्गव्यवधानेन तत्प्रतिपत्तेः । ननु साक्षादपरोक्षादात्मस्वभावेनानात्मनो हानोपादानयोः संबन्धग्रहणात्कमतिशयं वाक्यं कुर्यात् । मैवं वोचः ।
units.iast: liṅgavyavadhānena tatpratipatteḥ | nanu sākṣādaparokṣādātmasvabhāvenānātmano hānopādānayoḥ saṃbandhagrahaṇātkamatiśayaṃ vākyaṃ kuryāt | maivaṃ vocaḥ |
units.translation: because that conclusion is reached only through an intervening sign. But if the Self is already directly and immediately experienced as one’s own nature, and one can distinguish what is not-Self in order to give it up or take it up, what further work could the sentence do? Do not say this.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 184
units.translation: The conclusion depends on an inferential sign.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 185
units.deva: न हि लिङ्गव्यवधानेनात्मप्रतिपत्तिः साक्षात्प्रतिपत्तिर्भवति "यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यः " इति श्रुतेः । अत आह ।
units.iast: na hi liṅgavyavadhānenātmapratipattiḥ sākṣātpratipattirbhavati "yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ " iti śruteḥ | ata āha |
units.translation: Knowing the Self through an intervening sign is not direct knowledge. Scripture says, “The Self is attained by the one whom it chooses.” Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 186
units.translation: “A sign that establishes only existence cannot reveal the meaning of the sentence;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.57
units.translation: the Self, beyond the alternatives ‘is’ and ‘is not,’ is understood from the sentence.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 188
units.deva: ननु यदि व्यावृत्तसदसद्विकल्पजालं वस्त्वभीष्टं वाक्याद्भवतस्तथापि तूत्सार्यते वाक्यविषया तृष्णा -- यस्मादन्तरेणापि वाक्यश्रवणं निरस्ताशेषविकल्पमागोपालाविपालपण्डितं सुषुप्ते वस्तु सिद्धमतो नार्थो वाक्यश्रवणेन । नैतदेवम् ।
units.iast: nanu yadi vyāvṛttasadasadvikalpajālaṃ vastvabhīṣṭaṃ vākyādbhavatastathāpi tūtsāryate vākyaviṣayā tṛṣṇā -- yasmādantareṇāpi vākyaśravaṇaṃ nirastāśeṣavikalpamāgopālāvipālapaṇḍitaṃ suṣupte vastu siddhamato nārtho vākyaśravaṇena | naitadevam |
units.translation: Another objection: “If the reality you want is the thing beyond all alternatives of existence and nonexistence, the desire for a scriptural sentence can still be set aside. Even without hearing one, that reality is present in deep sleep, where every distinction is absent, from the cowherd to the learned scholar. So hearing scripture is unnecessary.” This is not so.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 189
units.deva: किं कारणम् । सर्वानर्थबीजस्यात्मानवबोधस्य सुषुप्ते संभवात् । यदि हि सुषुप्तेऽज्ञानं नाभविष्यदन्तरेणापि वेदान्तवाक्यश्रवणमनन निदिध्यासनान्यहं ब्रह्मास्मीत्यध्यवसायात्सर्वप्राणभूतामपि स्वरसत एव सुषुप्तप्रतिपत्तेः सकलसंसारोच्छित्तिप्रसङ्गः । न च कैवल्यात्पुनरुत्थानं न्याय्यमनिर्मोक्षप्रसङ्गात् । न चान्य एव सुषुप्तोऽन्य एवोत्थित इति शक्यं वक्तुं नाद्राक्षमहं सुषुप्तेऽन्यत् किंचिदपीत्युत्तितस्य प्रत्यभिज्ञादर्शनात् । तस्मादवश्यं सुषुप्तेऽज्ञानमभ्युपगन्तव्यम् । ननु यदि तत्राज्ञानमभविष्यद्रागद्वेषघटाज्ञानादिवत्प्रत्यक्षमभविष्यद्यथेह लोके घटं न जानामीत्यज्ञानमव्यवहितं प्रत्यक्षम् । अत्रोच्यते । न । अभिव्यञ्जकाभावात् । कथमभिव्यञ्जकाभाव इति चेच्छृणु ।
units.iast: kiṃ kāraṇam | sarvānarthabījasyātmānavabodhasya suṣupte saṃbhavāt | yadi hi suṣupte'jñānaṃ nābhaviṣyadantareṇāpi vedāntavākyaśravaṇamanana nididhyāsanānyahaṃ brahmāsmītyadhyavasāyātsarvaprāṇabhūtāmapi svarasata eva suṣuptapratipatteḥ sakalasaṃsārocchittiprasaṅgaḥ | na ca kaivalyātpunarutthānaṃ nyāyyamanirmokṣaprasaṅgāt | na cānya eva suṣupto'nya evotthita iti śakyaṃ vaktuṃ nādrākṣamahaṃ suṣupte'nyat kiṃcidapītyuttitasya pratyabhijñādarśanāt | tasmādavaśyaṃ suṣupte'jñānamabhyupagantavyam | nanu yadi tatrājñānamabhaviṣyadrāgadveṣaghaṭājñānādivatpratyakṣamabhaviṣyadyatheha loke ghaṭaṃ na jānāmītyajñānamavyavahitaṃ pratyakṣam | atrocyate | na | abhivyañjakābhāvāt | kathamabhivyañjakābhāva iti cecchṛṇu |
units.translation: Why not? Because ignorance, the seed of every misfortune, persists in deep sleep. If ignorance were absent there, then even without hearing, reflecting on and contemplating the Vedānta sentences, everyone—from the smallest living creature onward—would naturally wake from sleep convinced “I am Brahman”; the whole of worldly bondage would thereby end. Nor would it make sense to rise again after liberation, for that would make liberation impossible. One also cannot say that the sleeper and the one who wakes are different people: the person who wakes recognizes, “I saw nothing else while asleep.” Ignorance must therefore be admitted to persist in deep sleep. An objection follows: if ignorance were present there, it should be directly perceived, as attachment, aversion or ignorance of a pot is perceived here when one says, “I do not know the pot.” The answer is no, because there is no revealer of it. If asked how there can be no revealer, listen:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 190
units.translation: “Just as the ‘I’-thought does not appear without producing an outward mental activity,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.58
units.translation: so darkness is not clearly revealed without the inner instrument, the mind.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 192
units.deva: कश्चिदतिक्रान्तं प्रतिस्मृत्य "दृश्यत्वादहमप्येवं लिङ्गं स्याद्द्रष्टुरात्मनः " इति निर्युक्तिकमभिहितमित्याह । किं कारणम् ।
units.iast: kaścidatikrāntaṃ pratismṛtya "dṛśyatvādahamapyevaṃ liṅgaṃ syāddraṣṭurātmanaḥ " iti niryuktikamabhihitamityāha | kiṃ kāraṇam |
units.translation: Someone recalls the earlier argument and says that the claim ‘because it is seen, the “I” too is a sign of the witnessing Self’ was made without proof. Why?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 193
units.deva: अहंतज्ज्ञात्रोर्विवेकाप्रसिद्धेः । यथेह घटदेवदत्तयोर्ग्राह्यग्राहकत्वेन स्फुटतरो विभागः प्रसिद्धो लोके न तथेहाहंकारतज्ज्ञात्रोर्विभागोऽस्तीति तस्मादसाध्वेतदभिहितमिति । अत्रोच्यते ।
units.iast: ahaṃtajjñātrorvivekāprasiddheḥ | yatheha ghaṭadevadattayorgrāhyagrāhakatvena sphuṭataro vibhāgaḥ prasiddho loke na tathehāhaṃkāratajjñātrorvibhāgo'stīti tasmādasādhvetadabhihitamiti | atrocyate |
units.translation: “Because no distinction between the ‘I’ and the knower is established. In ordinary life the difference between a pot and Devadatta, as object and perceiver, is quite clear; there is no such evident difference between the ego and the one who knows it. So that claim is unsound.” The reply is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 194
units.translation: “Just as fire and wood can stand in the relation of burner and burned within one place,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.59
units.translation: so the ‘I’-thought and the knower can stand in the relation of known and knower.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 196
units.deva: एवं तावदविद्योत्थस्यान्तःकरणस्य बाह्यविषयनिमित्तरूपावच्छेदायाहंवृत्तिर्व्याप्रियते । तयावच्छिन्नं सत्कूटस्थप्रत्यगात्मोपादानावबोधरूपस्याव्यवधानतया विषयभावं प्रतिपद्यत इति । तत्र तयोर्ज्ञात्रहंतारूपयो रवभासकावभास्यसंबन्धव्यतिरेकेण नान्यत्संबन्धान्तरमुपपद्यते । अहंतारूपं त्वात्मसात्कृत्वाऽहंकञ्चुकं परिधायोपकार्यत्वोपकारकत्वक्षमः सन् बाह्यविषयेणोपकारिणापकारिणा वात्मात्मीयं संबन्धं प्रतिपद्यते ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvadavidyotthasyāntaḥkaraṇasya bāhyaviṣayanimittarūpāvacchedāyāhaṃvṛttirvyāpriyate | tayāvacchinnaṃ satkūṭasthapratyagātmopādānāvabodharūpasyāvyavadhānatayā viṣayabhāvaṃ pratipadyata iti | tatra tayorjñātrahaṃtārūpayo ravabhāsakāvabhāsyasaṃbandhavyatirekeṇa nānyatsaṃbandhāntaramupapadyate | ahaṃtārūpaṃ tvātmasātkṛtvā'haṃkañcukaṃ paridhāyopakāryatvopakārakatvakṣamaḥ san bāhyaviṣayeṇopakāriṇāpakāriṇā vātmātmīyaṃ saṃbandhaṃ pratipadyate |
units.translation: The mind, arising from ignorance, takes on a particular form when prompted by an external object; this is the “I”-thought. The changeless innermost Self, its basis and the form of awareness, then becomes its immediate object. Between the knower and the ego there is no relation other than that of illuminator and what is illuminated. By taking the “I”-form as itself and wearing the sheath of ego, the Self appears capable of being helped or harmed and enters into relation with external objects as “mine,” whether they benefit or injure it.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 197
units.translation: This is stated in the following verse:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 198
units.translation: “The knower’s cognition is ‘this’; the ego’s cognition is ‘this is mine.’

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.60
units.translation: This ‘mine’-thought arises through the limiting adjunct of ignorance, from the activity of the ego.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 200
units.deva: एकस्यैव ज्ञातुरन्तर्बाह्यनिमित्तभेदाद्विभिन्नेऽपि विषय इदं ममेति ज्ञानं द्वैरूप्यं जायत इत्युक्तम् ।
units.iast: ekasyaiva jñāturantarbāhyanimittabhedādvibhinne'pi viṣaya idaṃ mameti jñānaṃ dvairūpyaṃ jāyata ityuktam |
units.translation: Thus, even though there is only one knower, differing inner and outer objects give rise to the two forms of cognition, ‘this’ and ‘mine.’

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 201
units.deva: अत्रोपक्रियमाणापक्रियमाणस्यैव ज्ञातुर्विषये ममप्रत्ययो भवति विपर्यये चेदंप्रत्यय इति कथमवगम्यते ।
units.iast: atropakriyamāṇāpakriyamāṇasyaiva jñāturviṣaye mamapratyayo bhavati viparyaye cedaṃpratyaya iti kathamavagamyate |
units.translation: How is it known that the thought “mine” concerns the knower only when the knower is affected, while “this” concerns what is other?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 202
units.translation: It is known through agreement and difference. How? The verse says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 203
units.translation: “Because the knower is not affected, ‘I’ and ‘mine’ cannot belong to the Self;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.61
units.translation: ‘this,’ however, arises like the cognition of a pot, resting only on delusion.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 205
units.deva: मोहतत्कार्याश्रयत्वाज्ज्ञातृत्वविक्रिययोः पूर्वत्रेदंममज्ञान्वयः प्रदर्शितः । अथाधुना तद्व्यतिरेकेण व्यतिरेकप्रदर्शनार्थाह ।
units.iast: mohatatkāryāśrayatvājjñātṛtvavikriyayoḥ pūrvatredaṃmamajñānvayaḥ pradarśitaḥ | athādhunā tadvyatirekeṇa vyatirekapradarśanārthāha |
units.translation: Earlier, the agreement of ‘this’ and ‘mine’ with delusion and with changes in the knower was shown. Now, to show their absence when those conditions are absent, the author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 206
units.translation: “The Self, free of change and ignorance, is neither ‘this’ nor ‘mine’;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.62
units.translation: when one wakes, one says ‘I did not know’—for ignorance belongs to the ego.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 208
units.translation: To show how far the discrimination between Self and not-Self extends, he says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 209
units.translation: “This much is understood through the sentence and through perception:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.63
units.translation: the sentence alone removes the delusion that causes suffering and reveals the ever-present Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 211
units.translation: At the beginning of the second chapter, four kinds of listeners were introduced.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 212
units.deva: तत्र कृत्स्नानात्मनिवृत्तौ सत्यां यः प्रत्यगात्मन्यवाक्यार्थतां प्रतिपद्यते स क्षपिताशेषान्तरायहेतुरिति न तं प्रति वक्तव्यं किंचिदप्यवशिष्यते । योऽपि वाक्यश्रवणमात्रादेव प्रतिपद्यते तस्याप्यतीन्द्रिय शक्तिमत्त्वान्न किंचिदप्यपेक्षितव्यमस्ति । यश्च श्राविततत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यः स्वयमेवान्वयव्यतिरेको कृत्वा तदवसान एव वाक्यार्थं प्रतिपद्यतेऽसावपि यथार्थं प्रतिपन्न इति पूर्ववदेवोपेक्षितव्यः ।
units.iast: tatra kṛtsnānātmanivṛttau satyāṃ yaḥ pratyagātmanyavākyārthatāṃ pratipadyate sa kṣapitāśeṣāntarāyaheturiti na taṃ prati vaktavyaṃ kiṃcidapyavaśiṣyate | yo'pi vākyaśravaṇamātrādeva pratipadyate tasyāpyatīndriya śaktimattvānna kiṃcidapyapekṣitavyamasti | yaśca śrāvitatattvamasyādivākyaḥ svayamevānvayavyatireko kṛtvā tadavasāna eva vākyārthaṃ pratipadyate'sāvapi yathārthaṃ pratipanna iti pūrvavadevopekṣitavyaḥ |
units.translation: Of these, nothing remains to be taught to one who, after all not-Self has been fully set aside, recognizes the Self within as beyond ordinary sentence meaning; every obstacle to that recognition has been destroyed. Nor does one need anything further who understands from merely hearing the sentence, because such a person has extraordinary insight. The person who, after hearing “you are that,” works through agreement and difference independently and understands the sentence meaning at its conclusion has also understood correctly; that person too may be left aside, as before.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 213
units.deva: यः पुनरन्वयव्यतिरेकौ कारयित्वापि पुनःपुनर्वाक्यं श्राव्यते यथाभूतार्थप्रतिपत्तये तस्य कृतान्वयव्यतिरेकस्य सतः कथं वाक्यं श्राव्यत इति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: yaḥ punaranvayavyatirekau kārayitvāpi punaḥpunarvākyaṃ śrāvyate yathābhūtārthapratipattaye tasya kṛtānvayavyatirekasya sataḥ kathaṃ vākyaṃ śrāvyata iti | ucyate |
units.translation: But why should the sentence be repeated for someone who has already worked through agreement and difference, so that this person may understand the truth as it is? The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 214
units.translation: “A man who has lost count of the tenth person, though he has counted nine,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.64
units.translation: does not know ‘I am the tenth,’ even while looking at those nine.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 216
units.translation: The author now applies the meaning of the example to the point at hand:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 217
units.translation: “Even after setting aside duality, one does not know oneself as whole

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.65
units.translation: without a teaching such as ‘you are that’; no further investigation is needed here.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 219
units.deva: नान्वेष्यं चात्र कारणमित्युक्तं तत्कस्मादिति चोदिते प्रत्याहान्वेषणासहिष्णुत्वात् । तत्कथमित्याह ।
units.iast: nānveṣyaṃ cātra kāraṇamityuktaṃ tatkasmāditi codite pratyāhānveṣaṇāsahiṣṇutvāt | tatkathamityāha |
units.translation: When asked why no investigation is needed, he replies: because this delusion cannot withstand inquiry. How?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 220
units.translation: “This delusion has no foundation and conflicts with every sound line of reasoning;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.66
units.deva: सहते न विचारं सा तमो यद्वद्दिवाकरम् ॥ ६६॥
units.iast: sahate na vicāraṃ sā tamo yadvaddivākaram || 66||
units.translation: it cannot endure examination, just as darkness cannot withstand the sun.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 222
units.deva: तस्याः खल्वस्या अविद्याया भ्रान्तेः सम्यग्ज्ञानोत्पत्तिद्वारेण निवृत्तिः ।
units.iast: tasyāḥ khalvasyā avidyāyā bhrānteḥ samyagjñānotpattidvāreṇa nivṛttiḥ |
units.translation: This ignorance, this delusion, is ended by the arising of right knowledge.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 223
units.translation: “The understanding ‘I am that real’ firmly destroys the desire to know more;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.67
units.translation: it arises with regard to the inward Self and does not come from any other means of knowledge.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 225
units.translation: If asked how a sentence can indeed reveal the truth, an example is given:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 226
units.translation: “Just as a man seeking the tenth, distressed after counting only nine,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.68
units.translation: is given true knowledge by the words ‘You yourself are the tenth,’ so too the sentence gives knowledge.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 228
units.translation: The valid knowledge arising from hearing a sentence such as “you are that” is thus produced.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 229
units.deva: न च नैवमिति प्रत्ययान्तर जायते । तदेतद्दृष्टान्तेन प्रतिपादयति ।
units.iast: na ca naivamiti pratyayāntara jāyate | tadetaddṛṣṭāntena pratipādayati |
units.translation: And no contrary cognition arises to dislodge it. The point is explained through the example:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 230
units.translation: “The knowledge born from the sentence ‘You are the tenth’ is not contradicted,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.69
units.translation: nor does he doubt that he is one of the nine at the beginning, middle or end.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 232
units.translation: “In the same way, the sentence ‘You are that,’ which removes duality, gives rise

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.70
units.translation: to firm and correct knowledge of the meaning of the Self within.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 234
units.translation: It has been said that valid knowledge arises regarding the inner Self. An objection is now raised:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 235
units.deva: किं यथा घटादिप्रमेयविषया प्रमा कर्त्रादिकारकभेदानपह्नवेन जायते तथैवोताशेषकारकग्रामोपमर्देन कर्तुः प्रत्यगात्मनीति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: kiṃ yathā ghaṭādiprameyaviṣayā pramā kartrādikārakabhedānapahnavena jāyate tathaivotāśeṣakārakagrāmopamardena kartuḥ pratyagātmanīti | ucyate |
units.translation: “Does this knowledge of the inner Self arise like knowledge of an object such as a pot, without denying the distinctions between agent and the other factors? Or does it arise by dissolving the entire group of factors, with the inward Self as the agent?” The reply is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 236
units.translation: “Inwardness is its own nature: it is inactive, without agent, action or result.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.71
units.translation: Its nondual knowledge is indicated as being the inner Self itself.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 238
units.translation: Because this is so:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 239
units.translation: “Even the wise make the meaning of that sentence their very Self;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.72
units.translation: for as sense objects grow more distant, the senses become weaker in turn.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 241
units.deva: आह । यदि वाक्यमेव यथाभूतार्थवबोधकमथ कस्य हेतोरविद्योत्थापितस्य कर्तृत्वादेरुपदेश इत्युक्ते प्रतिविधीयते ।
units.iast: āha | yadi vākyameva yathābhūtārthavabodhakamatha kasya hetoravidyotthāpitasya kartṛtvāderupadeśa ityukte pratividhīyate |
units.translation: An objection is now raised: “If the sentence itself teaches the truth as it is, why teach agency and the rest, which arise from ignorance?” The reply is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 242
units.translation: “The teaching takes up what is already understood through error, in order to remove that error;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.73
units.translation: it teaches ‘this is that reality’ by negating the mistaken identification.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 244
units.translation: An example is offered to make this clear:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 245
units.translation: “Calling out ‘a post, a post!’ does not dispel the notion that it is a man;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.74
units.translation: mere repetition of the mistaken appearance does not remove a person’s error.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 247
units.translation: Since the word “thou” takes up what the listener already understands, its meanings such as being unhappy, which are merely indicated as its topic, are not intended [as the sentence’s final meaning].

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 248
units.deva: विधीयमानत्वे हि सति विरोधप्रसङ्गो न तु विधीयमाना नूद्यमानयोरिति । स्वप्रधानयोर्हि पदयोर्विरोधाशङ्का सामान्यलिङ्गतत्वात्तयोर्न विपर्यये ।
units.iast: vidhīyamānatve hi sati virodhaprasaṅgo na tu vidhīyamānā nūdyamānayoriti | svapradhānayorhi padayorvirodhāśaṅkā sāmānyaliṅgatatvāttayorna viparyaye |
units.translation: If those attributes were being newly asserted, a contradiction would follow; there is no such contradiction between what is asserted and what is merely restated. The possibility of conflict concerns two words that each primarily assert their own meaning, because the general element they share is understood by inference; it does not apply in the reverse case.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 249
units.translation: “The two words do not carry a shared general meaning that must be retained, nor do they propose to discard their own meanings;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.75
units.translation: ‘that’ and ‘thou’ have distinct starting points, and so must be read in relation to one another.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 251
units.deva: अपास्तसामान्यार्थत्वादनुवादस्थत्वाद्विधीयमानेन च सह विरोधाद्दुःखित्वादेरस्तु कामं जिहासितार्थयो रसंसर्गो यथोपन्यस्तदोषविरहात्तत्त्वमर्थयोः संसर्गोऽस्तु नीलोत्पलवदिति चेन्नैवमप्युपपद्यते । तस्मात् ।
units.iast: apāstasāmānyārthatvādanuvādasthatvādvidhīyamānena ca saha virodhādduḥkhitvāderastu kāmaṃ jihāsitārthayo rasaṃsargo yathopanyastadoṣavirahāttattvamarthayoḥ saṃsargo'stu nīlotpalavaditi cennaivamapyupapadyate | tasmāt |
units.translation: One might argue: “Let the meanings of ‘that’ and ‘thou’ be unrelated, since their shared general meanings have been removed; ‘thou’ merely restates what is known, and it conflicts with what is newly asserted. Then let the two meanings be related, as blue and lotus are related, since that avoids the stated fault.” This too does not work. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 252
units.translation: “The inner Self, which is the final meaning of both, is free of the indirectness found in either meaning;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.76
units.translation: there is no Self without nonduality, nor nonduality apart from the Self that is ever the seer.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 254
units.deva: अत्राह । किमिह जिहासितं किं वोपादित्सितमिति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: atrāha | kimiha jihāsitaṃ kiṃ vopāditsitamiti | ucyate |
units.translation: Someone asks: “What here is to be given up, and what is to be taken up?” The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.77
units.deva: प्रत्यगात्मार्थाभिधायिनस्त्वंपदादुभयं प्रतीयतेऽहं दुःखी प्रत्यगात्मा च । तत्र च प्रत्यगात्मनोऽहं दुःखीत्यनेनाभिसंबन्ध आत्मयाथात्म्यानवबोधहेतुक एव । अतोऽहमर्थोऽपसृष्टत्वादज्ञानोत्थत्वाच्च हेय इति प्रत्यक्षतोवसीयते । तदर्थे किं हेयं किं वोपादेयमिति नावध्रियते । तत इदमभिधीयते । पारोक्ष्यं यत्तदर्थे स्यात्तद्धेयमहमर्थवत् । प्रतीचेवाहमोऽभेदः पारोक्ष्येणात्मनोऽपि मे ॥ ७७॥
units.iast: pratyagātmārthābhidhāyinastvaṃpadādubhayaṃ pratīyate'haṃ duḥkhī pratyagātmā ca | tatra ca pratyagātmano'haṃ duḥkhītyanenābhisaṃbandha ātmayāthātmyānavabodhahetuka eva | ato'hamartho'pasṛṣṭatvādajñānotthatvācca heya iti pratyakṣatovasīyate | tadarthe kiṃ heyaṃ kiṃ vopādeyamiti nāvadhriyate | tata idamabhidhīyate | pārokṣyaṃ yattadarthe syāttaddheyamahamarthavat | pratīcevāhamo'bhedaḥ pārokṣyeṇātmano'pi me || 77||
units.translation: The word “thou,” which expresses the inner Self, conveys both the ordinary “I am unhappy” and the innermost Self. The connection between the innermost Self and “I am unhappy” is caused only by failure to know the Self as it truly is. The ordinary ego is therefore plainly to be relinquished: it is something superimposed and arises from ignorance. What, then, is to be given up or taken up in the meaning of “that”? This is stated in the verse: “Whatever indirectness is in the meaning of ‘that’ is to be set aside, just like the ego; the inward identity of ‘that’ with ‘I’ is the Self, though the Self too appears indirect.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 256
units.deva: कथं पुनस्तदर्थोऽद्वितीयलक्षणः प्रत्यगात्मोपाश्रयं सद्वितीयत्वं दुःखित्वं निरन्वयमपनुदतीति । उच्यते । न चैतयोर्निवर्तकनिवर्त्यभावं वयं ब्रूमः । कथं तर्हि ।
units.iast: kathaṃ punastadartho'dvitīyalakṣaṇaḥ pratyagātmopāśrayaṃ sadvitīyatvaṃ duḥkhitvaṃ niranvayamapanudatīti | ucyate | na caitayornivartakanivartyabhāvaṃ vayaṃ brūmaḥ | kathaṃ tarhi |
units.translation: How does the meaning of “that,” characterized by nonduality and apparently distinct from the inward Self, remove the Self’s apparent duality and suffering? The answer: we do not claim that one directly removes the other. How, then?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 257
units.translation: The sentence reveals the nonduality that was previously unknown in the meaning of “thou,” the inner Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 258
units.deva: अतोऽनवबोधनिरासेन तदुत्थस्य सद्वितीयत्वस्य त्वमर्थत्वस्य परोक्षत्वस्य च तदर्थस्थस्य निरसनान्न वैयधिकरण्यादि चोद्यस्यावसरोऽस्तीति । तदिदमभिधीयते ।
units.iast: ato'navabodhanirāsena tadutthasya sadvitīyatvasya tvamarthatvasya parokṣatvasya ca tadarthasthasya nirasanānna vaiyadhikaraṇyādi codyasyāvasaro'stīti | tadidamabhidhīyate |
units.translation: By removing that ignorance, it removes the resulting duality wrongly attributed to “thou,” and the indirectness wrongly attributed to “that.” Thus the objection that these qualities belong to different subjects has no place. This is stated as follows:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 259
units.translation: “Joined with the meaning of ‘that,’ the meaning of ‘thou’ removes plurality;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.78
units.translation: the meaning of ‘thou,’ without first abandoning its apparent indirectness, cannot reach the meaning of ‘that.’”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 261
units.deva: कस्मात्पुनः कारणात्तदर्थोऽद्वितीयलक्षणस्त्वमर्थेन प्रत्यगात्मना पृथगर्थः सन्नविद्योत्थं सद्वितीयत्वं निहन्तीति । उच्यते । विरोधात् । तदुच्यते ।
units.iast: kasmātpunaḥ kāraṇāttadartho'dvitīyalakṣaṇastvamarthena pratyagātmanā pṛthagarthaḥ sannavidyotthaṃ sadvitīyatvaṃ nihantīti | ucyate | virodhāt | taducyate |
units.translation: Why does the nondual meaning of “that,” though apparently distinct from the inner Self meant by “thou,” destroy the duality born of ignorance? The answer is: because they contradict it. Thus:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 262
units.translation: “The indirectness of the Self conflicts with the apparent secondness of the person in bondage;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.79
units.translation: the two conflicting meanings, ‘that’ and ‘thou,’ remove those appearances.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 264
units.translation: Another reason is given for the power of the meanings of “that” and “thou” to remove one another’s errors:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 265
units.translation: Because the meanings of “that” and “thou” concern an end not previously known and are grounded in scripture,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.80
units.translation: they can each negate their opposed appearance without abandoning their own meaning.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 267
units.deva: एवं तावद्यथोपक्रान्तेन प्रक्रियावर्त्मना न प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणान्तरैर्विरोधगन्धोऽपि संभाव्यते ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvadyathopakrāntena prakriyāvartmanā na pratyakṣādipramāṇāntarairvirodhagandho'pi saṃbhāvyate |
units.translation: Thus, along the line of reasoning begun earlier, no conflict whatever with perception or any other means of knowledge is possible.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 268
units.deva: यदा पुनः सर्वप्रकारेणापि यतमाना नैवेमं वाक्यार्थं संभावयामः प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणान्तरविरोधत एव तस्मिन्नपि पक्ष उच्यते ।
units.iast: yadā punaḥ sarvaprakāreṇāpi yatamānā naivemaṃ vākyārthaṃ saṃbhāvayāmaḥ pratyakṣādipramāṇāntaravirodhata eva tasminnapi pakṣa ucyate |
units.translation: If, despite examining the matter in every way, one still cannot reconcile the sentence meaning with other means of knowledge and assumes a conflict, the author gives an answer to that position too:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 269
units.translation: “If a sentence were to state something contrary to perception or the other means of knowledge,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.81
units.translation: it could certainly be intended as an injunction for a ritual vision, as in the teachings about a woman and fire.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 271
units.deva: यदा तु तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यं सर्वप्रकारेणापि विचार्यमाणं न क्रियां कटाक्षेणापि वीक्षते तदा प्रसंख्यानादिव्यापारो दुस्संभाव्य इति । तदुच्यते ।
units.iast: yadā tu tattvamasyādivākyaṃ sarvaprakāreṇāpi vicāryamāṇaṃ na kriyāṃ kaṭākṣeṇāpi vīkṣate tadā prasaṃkhyānādivyāpāro dussaṃbhāvya iti | taducyate |
units.translation: But when a sentence such as “you are that,” examined in every way, does not even glance toward an action, it is hard to maintain that an activity such as repeated meditation is required. The author therefore says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 272
units.translation: “If a sentence is wholly concerned with an existing reality, it cannot have action as its purpose;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.82
units.translation: for reality has one nature, and therefore no alternative to be chosen among.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 274
units.translation: Nor is there conflict with another means of knowledge, because their subject matters differ. How?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 275
units.translation: The author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 276
units.translation: “A means of knowledge must disclose what was not previously known; if it does not, it is not a means of knowledge.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.83
units.translation: So there can be no reasonable conflict between two means that reveal different things.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 278
units.deva: य एवमपि भिन्नविषयाणां विरोधं वक्ति सोऽत्रापि विरोधं ब्रूयात् ।
units.iast: ya evamapi bhinnaviṣayāṇāṃ virodhaṃ vakti so'trāpi virodhaṃ brūyāt |
units.translation: Someone who nonetheless claims that means of knowledge with different subjects conflict could also claim a conflict in this case:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 279
units.deva: नायं शब्दः कुतो यस्माद्रूपं पश्यामि चक्षुषा ।
units.iast: nāyaṃ śabdaḥ kuto yasmādrūpaṃ paśyāmi cakṣuṣā |
units.translation: “This is not a sound—how could it be? I see a form with my eyes.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.84
units.translation: In the same way, that would be a supposed conflict between a verbal teaching and what is seen by the senses.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 281
units.deva: प्रमाणानां सतां न विरोधः श्रोत्रादीनामिव भिन्नविषयत्वात् ।
units.iast: pramāṇānāṃ satāṃ na virodhaḥ śrotrādīnāmiva bhinnaviṣayatvāt |
units.translation: “Valid means of knowledge do not conflict, since their subjects differ, as do hearing and the other senses.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 282
units.deva: ययोश्चाभिन्नविषयत्वं तयोराखुनकुलयोरिव प्रतिनियत एव बाध्यबाधकभावः स्यात् । अतस्तदुच्यते ।
units.iast: yayoścābhinnaviṣayatvaṃ tayorākhunakulayoriva pratiniyata eva bādhyabādhakabhāvaḥ syāt | atastaducyate |
units.translation: Where two means have the same subject, one has a fixed power to correct the other, as with a mongoose and a snake. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 283
units.deva: प्रत्यक्षं चेन्न शाब्दं स्याच्छाब्दं चेदक्षजं कथम् ।
units.iast: pratyakṣaṃ cenna śābdaṃ syācchābdaṃ cedakṣajaṃ katham |
units.translation: “If it is perceptual, it is not verbal knowledge; if verbal, how can it be perceptual?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.85
units.translation: A false appearance of perception is corrected by perception; a false scriptural appearance by scripture.”
