units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 285
units.deva: न च प्रतिज्ञाहेतुदृष्टान्तन्याय इह संभवति शब्दादीनां प्रत्येकं प्रमाणत्वादत आह ।
units.iast: na ca pratijñāhetudṛṣṭāntanyāya iha saṃbhavati śabdādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ pramāṇatvādata āha |
units.translation: The formal pattern of a thesis, reason and example does not apply here, because words and the other means of knowledge each have authority on their own. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 286
units.translation: “Each means of knowledge reveals its subject by its own power;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.86
units.translation: we do not hold that its authority depends on the help of the others.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 288
units.deva: न च सुखदुःखादिसंबन्धोऽवगत्यात्मनः प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणैर्गृह्यते येन विरोधः प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणैरुद्धाट्यते ।
units.iast: na ca sukhaduḥkhādisaṃbandho'vagatyātmanaḥ pratyakṣādipramāṇairgṛhyate yena virodhaḥ pratyakṣādipramāṇairuddhāṭyate |
units.translation: Nor do perception and the other means of knowledge grasp any relation between awareness and happiness, suffering and the like that could be used to show a conflict with them.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 289
units.translation: “If awareness itself were established as suffering, it would not be established as the Self;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.87
units.deva: कर्मण्येव प्रमा न्याय्या न तु कर्तर्यपि क्वचित् ॥ ८७॥
units.iast: karmaṇyeva pramā nyāyyā na tu kartaryapi kvacit || 87||
units.translation: valid knowledge properly concerns an action or object, never the agent as such.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 291
units.deva: अभ्युपगमेऽपि च प्रसंख्यानशतेनापि नैव त्वं संभावितदोषान्मुच्यते । अत आह ।
units.iast: abhyupagame'pi ca prasaṃkhyānaśatenāpi naiva tvaṃ saṃbhāvitadoṣānmucyate | ata āha |
units.translation: Even if one grants this, a hundred practices of contemplation will not free you from the imagined fault. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 292
units.translation: “If suffering is rooted in a means of knowledge, what can remove it?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.88
units.translation: If it cannot be removed, the Buddhists’ doctrine of no-Self follows, as heat follows from fire.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 294
units.translation: Another view is stated:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 295
units.translation: “If properly undertaken contemplation removes suffering,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.89
units.translation: how could it produce valid knowledge when that knowledge conflicts with perception and the other means?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 297
units.deva: ननु प्रसंख्यानं नाम तत्त्वमस्यादिशब्दार्थान्वयव्यतिरेकयुक्तिविषयबुद्ध्याम्रेडनमभिधीयते तच्चानुष्ठीयमानं प्रमितिवर्धनया परिपूर्णां प्रमितिं जनयति न पुनरैकाग्र्यवर्धनयेति ।
units.iast: nanu prasaṃkhyānaṃ nāma tattvamasyādiśabdārthānvayavyatirekayuktiviṣayabuddhyāmreḍanamabhidhīyate taccānuṣṭhīyamānaṃ pramitivardhanayā paripūrṇāṃ pramitiṃ janayati na punaraikāgryavardhanayeti |
units.translation: One might say that contemplation means repeatedly turning the mind, through reasoning by agreement and difference, toward the meaning of words such as “you are that.” Practised in this way, it produces complete knowledge by increasing the knowledge itself, not by increasing one-pointedness.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 298
units.deva: यथाशेषाशुचिनीडे स्त्रीकृणपे कामिनीति निर्वस्तुकः पुरुषायासमात्रजनितः प्रत्यय इति । तन्न । यतः ।
units.iast: yathāśeṣāśucinīḍe strīkṛṇape kāminīti nirvastukaḥ puruṣāyāsamātrajanitaḥ pratyaya iti | tanna | yataḥ |
units.translation: For example, a man may imagine a woman to be desirable even though she is only a mass of impurity and the notion is produced by his own effort; this objection does not apply, because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 299
units.translation: “What grows through repeated practice of thought

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.90
units.translation: is only one-pointedness of mind; means of knowledge do not reveal their object through repetition.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 301
units.translation: “If a mental exercise strengthened by practice could remove everything,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.91
units.translation: its removal would not be certain, for its result is produced by mental exercise.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 303
units.translation: The author adds:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 304
units.translation: “If the idea ‘I am suffering,’ reinforced for millions of ages, were destroyed,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.92
units.translation: what proof is there that a much weaker, practice-born conviction would remain firm?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 306
units.translation: One might say that scripture will make that conviction firm. No:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 307
units.translation: scripture only produces understanding of the nature of an existing thing as it is.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 308
units.deva: न हि पदार्थशक्त्याधानकृच्छास्त्रम् । प्रसिद्धं च लोके ।
units.iast: na hi padārthaśaktyādhānakṛcchāstram | prasiddhaṃ ca loke |
units.translation: Scripture does not implant new powers in the things it describes. This is well known in ordinary life.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 309
units.translation: “The result produced by mental exercise, and the result produced by action,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.93
units.translation: should not be thought lasting; their connection is like that of things in the Drāviḍa country.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 311
units.translation: Even if suffering in the Self is presented by perception and the other means of knowledge,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 312
units.deva: तथापि तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्योत्थप्रत्यय एव बलीयानिति निश्चयोऽव्यभिचारिप्रामाण्यवाक्योपत्तत्वात्प्रमेयस्य च स्वत एव निर्दुःखित्वसिद्धेः । प्रत्यक्षादेस्तु व्यभिचारित्वात्संभावनायाश्च पुरुषपरिकल्पनामात्रावष्टम्भत्वाच्चेति ।
units.iast: tathāpi tattvamasyādivākyotthapratyaya eva balīyāniti niścayo'vyabhicāriprāmāṇyavākyopattatvātprameyasya ca svata eva nirduḥkhitvasiddheḥ | pratyakṣādestu vyabhicāritvātsaṃbhāvanāyāśca puruṣaparikalpanāmātrāvaṣṭambhatvācceti |
units.translation: the conviction born from “you are that” is stronger: it arises from a sentence whose authority never fails, while the knowable Self is by its own nature free from suffering. Perception can err, and the appearance it supports rests only on a person’s imagination.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 313
units.translation: “Freedom from suffering is established by itself, while perception and the like report suffering;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.94
units.translation: who would trust an outward means of knowledge while disregarding the Self?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 315
units.translation: This is said only to explain the connection [between the passage and its context].

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 316
units.translation: “Even when one proceeds in the face of perception’s obstruction, the turn toward the inward Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.95
units.translation: is understood from scripture’s statement that the sense openings are directed outward.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 318
units.deva: अभ्युपगम्यैवमुच्यते न तु प्रमाणं सत्प्रमाणान्तरेण विरुध्यत इत्यसकृदवोचाम । यत्रापि वाक्यप्रत्यक्षयोर्विरोधाशङ्का तत्रापि पुरुषमोहवशादेव सा जायते न तु परमार्थत इति ।
units.iast: abhyupagamyaivamucyate na tu pramāṇaṃ satpramāṇāntareṇa virudhyata ityasakṛdavocāma | yatrāpi vākyapratyakṣayorvirodhāśaṅkā tatrāpi puruṣamohavaśādeva sā jāyate na tu paramārthata iti |
units.translation: This is said only for the sake of argument; we have repeatedly explained that one valid means of knowledge does not truly conflict with another. Even where a conflict between a scriptural sentence and perception is suspected, it arises only from a person’s delusion, not in reality.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 319
units.translation: Therefore the author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 320
units.translation: “If a sentence should produce knowledge that conflicts with perception and the other means of knowledge…”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.96
units.translation: “The wise would therefore call its directness figurative, since a literal meaning is impossible.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 322
units.translation: An example is given to make this point easier to grasp:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 323
units.translation: “The fire was properly studied, and the bed laughed aloud.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.97
units.translation: In the same way, that Self is indicated by the unsuitable “I”-thought.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 325
units.deva: कस्मात्पुनः कारणात्साक्षादेवात्मा नाभिधीयते किमनया कल्पनयेति तत्राह ।
units.iast: kasmātpunaḥ kāraṇātsākṣādevātmā nābhidhīyate kimanayā kalpanayeti tatrāha |
units.translation: Why is the Self not stated directly, without this imagined device? The author explains:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 326
units.translation: “Apart from the meaning of ‘thou,’ once what is not-Self has been set aside, the Self does not become known;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.98
units.translation: even the meaning of ‘thou’ operates here only through a trace of its attributes.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 328
units.deva: कस्मात्पुनर्हेतोर्ह्यहमित्येतदपि गुणलेशेन वर्तते न पुनः साक्षादेवेति । विधूतसर्वकल्पनाकारणस्वाभाव्यादात्मनः अत आह ।
units.iast: kasmātpunarhetorhyahamityetadapi guṇaleśena vartate na punaḥ sākṣādeveti | vidhūtasarvakalpanākāraṇasvābhāvyādātmanaḥ ata āha |
units.translation: Why does the word “I” also operate only through a trace of attributes, rather than directly? Because the Self is naturally free of every imagined distinction. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 329
units.translation: “Fools imagine, in the sky, stains of smoke, frost and clouds;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.99
units.translation: in the same way they imagine the world of bondage in the innermost Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 331
units.deva: ननु सर्वकल्पनानामप्यात्मन्यत्यन्तासंभवे समानेऽहंवृत्तौ कः पक्षपाते हेतुर्येन वृत्त्यन्तराणि विधूयाहंवृत्त्यैवात्मोपलक्ष्यत इति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: nanu sarvakalpanānāmapyātmanyatyantāsaṃbhave samāne'haṃvṛttau kaḥ pakṣapāte heturyena vṛttyantarāṇi vidhūyāhaṃvṛttyaivātmopalakṣyata iti | ucyate |
units.translation: One might object: “All imagined forms are equally impossible in the Self. Why favor the ‘I’-thought and use it to indicate the Self after setting aside every other thought?” The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 332
units.translation: “This ‘I’-thought reflects awareness and turns inward, unlike the other thoughts;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.100
units.translation: for the reasons already given, the Self is therefore taught through it.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 334
units.translation: “If the supreme Seer were indicated by thoughts whose meanings are ‘you’ and the rest,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.101
units.deva: अनात्मत्वं भवेत्तस्य वितथं च वचः श्रुतेः ॥ १०१॥
units.iast: anātmatvaṃ bhavettasya vitathaṃ ca vacaḥ śruteḥ || 101||
units.translation: the Self would become not-Self, and scripture’s teaching would be false.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 336
units.translation: As explained:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 337
units.translation: “Through this slight trace of attributes, by means of the ‘I’-thought,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.102
units.translation: the Self is indicated, though it is not directly stated here.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 339
units.translation: If asked why it is not stated directly:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 340
units.translation: “Words depend on relation, qualities, action, class and convention;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.103
units.translation: none of these applies to the Self, and so the Self is not directly denoted.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 342
units.deva: यदि शब्दोऽभिधानाभिधेयत्वसंबन्धाङ्गीकारेण नात्मनि वर्तते कथं शब्दादहं ब्रह्मास्मीति सम्यग्बोधोत्पत्तिः ।
units.iast: yadi śabdo'bhidhānābhidheyatvasaṃbandhāṅgīkāreṇa nātmani vartate kathaṃ śabdādahaṃ brahmāsmīti samyagbodhotpattiḥ |
units.translation: If words do not apply to the Self through a relation between word and denoted thing, how can the sentence “I am Brahman” produce correct knowledge?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 343
units.translation: The reply is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 344
units.translation: “One reaches the goal by first taking a path that is not ultimately real;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.104
units.translation: awakened through an indirect attribute, we know the Self by reason of its being our very Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 346
units.deva: कथं पुनरभिधानमभिधेयेनानभिसंबद्धं सदनभिधेयेऽर्थे प्रमां जनयतीति । शृणु यथानभिसंबद्धमप्यनभिधे येऽर्थेऽविद्यानिराकरणमुखेन बोधयतीत्याह ।
units.iast: kathaṃ punarabhidhānamabhidheyenānabhisaṃbaddhaṃ sadanabhidheye'rthe pramāṃ janayatīti | śṛṇu yathānabhisaṃbaddhamapyanabhidhe ye'rthe'vidyānirākaraṇamukhena bodhayatītyāha |
units.translation: How can a word, unconnected with what it denotes, produce knowledge of something that cannot be denoted? Listen: though it is unconnected, it awakens knowledge by removing ignorance, as the following verse says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 347
units.translation: “In ordinary life, people who are asleep are addressed by their names

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.105
units.translation: and at once awaken; in the same way, one awakens to the inward Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 349
units.deva: न हि नाम्नास्ति संबन्धो व्युत्थितस्य शरीरतः ।
units.iast: na hi nāmnāsti saṃbandho vyutthitasya śarīrataḥ |
units.translation: “A name has no relation to the body of the person who wakes;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.106
units.translation: yet through that name the person understands—just so with ‘you are that.’”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 351
units.translation: And again:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 352
units.translation: “Awareness and its absence, though lodged in a darkened mind, do not touch space;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.107
units.translation: in the same way, understand that in the Self they are subject to sublation and what is not sublated.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 354
units.deva: "असत्ये वर्त्मनि स्थित्वा" इत्युपश्रुत्यातिविस्मितो महता संभ्रमेण कश्चिच्चोदयति ।
units.iast: "asatye vartmani sthitvā" ityupaśrutyātivismito mahatā saṃbhrameṇa kaściccodayati |
units.translation: Hearing the words “one reaches the goal by taking an unreal path,” someone, greatly astonished, objects:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 355
units.translation: “There is no unreal means in ordinary life for determining what is ultimately true;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.108
units.translation: no one concludes that there is fire from a false sign such as mist.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 357
units.translation: To anyone who argues this way, one can point to the pot and other familiar examples:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.109
units.translation: “The pot, in turn, is distinct from both [its cause and the absence of the pot]; the alternatives are not the same.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 359
units.translation: Having uprooted this mistaken objection, the author returns to the main point:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 360
units.deva: प्रकृतं चानभिधेये कथमभिधाश्रुतिरविद्याध्वंस्यात्मनि ज्ञानं जनयतीति । तत्रैव कारणान्तरमुच्यते ।
units.iast: prakṛtaṃ cānabhidheye kathamabhidhāśrutiravidyādhvaṃsyātmani jñānaṃ janayatīti | tatraiva kāraṇāntaramucyate |
units.translation: The question at hand is how a scriptural statement can produce knowledge of the Self, which cannot be denoted and which destroys ignorance. Another reason is now given.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 361
units.translation: “Ignorance is difficult to dislodge; the Self’s awakening is simply the recognition of the Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.110
units.translation: It comes from a mere occasion, like a berry resting at the tip of the nose.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 363
units.deva: अनुदितानस्तमितकूटस्थबोधमात्रस्वाभाव्यादात्मनो दुस्संभाव्योऽविद्यासद्भाव इति चेन्न । अविद्याप्रसिद्ध्यैव तत्सद्भावसिद्धेरुलूकनिशावदित्यत इदमुच्यते ।
units.iast: anuditānastamitakūṭasthabodhamātrasvābhāvyādātmano dussaṃbhāvyo'vidyāsadbhāva iti cenna | avidyāprasiddhyaiva tatsadbhāvasiddherulūkaniśāvadityata idamucyate |
units.translation: One might say that ignorance is hard to conceive when the Self is changeless, pure awareness, neither arising nor setting. This is no objection: ignorance is established by ordinary experience, just as an owl’s night is established. Hence the verse:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 364
units.translation: “How bold ignorance is! No one escapes its reach.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.111
units.translation: Ignoring the means of knowledge, it stands there as though it were the Supreme Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 366
units.translation: Since ignorance is established only through ordinary experience, and cannot be supposed in keeping with the reality of the Self, the author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 367
units.translation: “For the one whose own nature is knowledge, free of action and the factors of action,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.112
units.translation: by what reason could ignorance even be conceived?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 369
units.translation: Though the Self is awareness alone, without arising or setting, it is nevertheless seen otherwise, screened by ignorance accepted without examination. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 370
units.translation: “Through inference this reality is excluded from what exists and assigned to nonexistence;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.113
units.translation: for the seeker, its removal too comes only from the sentence.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.114
units.iast: na vyāvṛttiryathā bhāvād bhāvenaivāviśeṣataḥ | abhāvādapyabhāvatvādvyāvṛttirna tatheṣyate || 114||
units.translation: Just as one existent thing is not distinguished from another by existence alone, so an exclusion is not accepted merely because something is non-existent.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 372
units.deva: भाववदभावादपि निवृत्तिरनुमानादेव किमिति न भवतीति चेच्छृणु ।
units.iast: bhāvavadabhāvādapi nivṛttiranumānādeva kimiti na bhavatīti cecchṛṇu |
units.translation: If asked why inference cannot remove nonexistence just as it removes what exists, listen:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 373
units.deva: यतो नानुमानेन व्याविद्धाशेषक्रियाकारकफलात्मनि स्वाराज्येऽभिषेक्तुं शक्यते तस्मात् ।
units.iast: yato nānumānena vyāviddhāśeṣakriyākārakaphalātmani svārājye'bhiṣektuṃ śakyate tasmāt |
units.translation: Inference cannot enthrone one in the sovereignty free from all actions, agents, instruments and results. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 374
units.translation: “This person lies asleep, overcome by the sleep of ignorance, hard to discern;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.115
units.translation: only scripture, which removes both existence and nonexistence, can awaken him.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 376
units.translation: Someone objects: “Ignorance is hard to conceive because the Self is awareness alone, without arising or setting.” This is not so. Why? The verse says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 377
units.translation: “Beforehand, the question ‘Whence did ignorance come?’ cannot arise, because its cause is not available;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.116
units.translation: nor can the question arise afterward, since it is not bounded by any of the three times.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 379
units.translation: Because a sentence such as “you are that” alone removes every trace of ignorance about the Self:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 380
units.translation: “Those who disregard the true means of knowledge and seek to know ‘you are that’ by other means

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.117
units.translation: might as well try to taste flavors with their eyes.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 382
units.deva: एवमप्रतिहतामहं ब्रह्मेति प्रमां तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यं कुर्वदपि न प्रतिपादयतीति चेदभिमतं न कुतश्चनापि प्रतिपत्तिः स्यादत आह ।
units.iast: evamapratihatāmahaṃ brahmeti pramāṃ tattvamasyādivākyaṃ kurvadapi na pratipādayatīti cedabhimataṃ na kutaścanāpi pratipattiḥ syādata āha |
units.translation: If one says that even though the sentence “I am Brahman” produces unobstructed valid knowledge, it does not actually teach it, then nothing could ever be understood. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 383
units.translation: “If this sentence were false, even when awareness is present,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.118
units.translation: there would be no ground for trusting any other sentence either, since they are all alike in yielding awareness.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 385
units.translation: It is not reasonable to invent a different meaning for the sentence than the one intended. For:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 386
units.translation: “If no experience arose even when the word’s meaning was understood,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.119
units.translation: one would have to invent a separate injunction; no other meaning is actually understood.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 388
units.deva: न च यथाभिमतोऽर्थो यथोक्तेन न्यायेन नावसीयते ।
units.iast: na ca yathābhimato'rtho yathoktena nyāyena nāvasīyate |
units.translation: Nor is the intended meaning impossible to determine by the reasoning already explained.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 389
units.translation: The author states that reasoning:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 390
units.translation: “Setting aside names and the rest, one should relinquish the meaning of ‘thou,’

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.120
units.translation: be free of desire for what is other than oneself, and follow the disciplines of calm and the rest.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 392
units.translation: “Breaking through the five sheaths, beginning with the food-made body, as barriers that are not-Self,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.121
units.deva: अहं ब्रह्मेति वाक्यार्थं वेत्ति चेन्नार्थ ईहया ॥ १२१॥
units.iast: ahaṃ brahmeti vākyārthaṃ vetti cennārtha īhayā || 121||
units.translation: one understands the sentence meaning ‘I am Brahman’ without further striving.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 394
units.deva: न चेदेवमुपगम्यते वाक्यस्य प्रमाणस्य सतोऽप्रामाण्यं प्राप्नोति । तदाह ।
units.iast: na cedevamupagamyate vākyasya pramāṇasya sato'prāmāṇyaṃ prāpnoti | tadāha |
units.translation: If this is not accepted, a sentence that is in fact a valid means of knowledge would be declared invalid. The author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 395
units.deva: यदर्थं च प्रवृत्तं यद्वाक्यं तत्र न चेच्छ्रुतम् ।
units.iast: yadarthaṃ ca pravṛttaṃ yadvākyaṃ tatra na cecchrutam |
units.translation: “If the sentence is heard but does not produce valid knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.122
units.translation: of the very matter for which it was spoken, on what grounds is it a valid means of knowledge?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 397
units.translation: Suppose you think:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.123
units.deva: जानीयाच्चेत्प्रसंख्यानाच्छब्दस्सत्यवचाः कथम् । पारोक्ष्यं शब्दो नः प्राह प्रसंख्यानात्त्वसंशयम् ॥ १२३॥
units.iast: jānīyāccetprasaṃkhyānācchabdassatyavacāḥ katham | pārokṣyaṃ śabdo naḥ prāha prasaṃkhyānāttvasaṃśayam || 123||
units.translation: If repeated contemplation gives knowledge, how are the words themselves truthful? The words tell us [the Self is] indirect; through contemplation, [it becomes known] without doubt.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 401
units.translation: We cannot suppose that correct understanding will arise from contemplation consisting of repeatedly turning over the reasoning and the words. For:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 402
units.translation: “If the words and reasoning did not produce valid knowledge before,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.124
units.translation: what new result will come from simply repeating them inwardly?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 404
units.deva: अथैवमपि प्रसंख्यानमन्तरेण प्राणान्धारयितुं न शक्नोषीति चेच्छ्रवणादावेव संपादयिष्यामः । कथम् ।
units.iast: athaivamapi prasaṃkhyānamantareṇa prāṇāndhārayituṃ na śaknoṣīti cecchravaṇādāveva saṃpādayiṣyāmaḥ | katham |
units.translation: If you say that without such contemplation you cannot even sustain life, we will provide for it during listening itself. How?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 405
units.translation: “The same principle of repetition used in contemplation can be applied to hearing:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.125
units.translation: what was heard only faintly or in part is understood when heard properly.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 407
units.deva: ननु प्रसंख्यानविधिमनभ्युपगच्छतः पारमहंसी चर्या बौद्धादिचर्यावदशास्त्रपूर्विका प्राप्नोति ततश्चारूढपतितत्वं न स्यादशेषकर्मणां च निवृत्तिर्न प्राप्नोतीति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: nanu prasaṃkhyānavidhimanabhyupagacchataḥ pāramahaṃsī caryā bauddhādicaryāvadaśāstrapūrvikā prāpnoti tataścārūḍhapatitatvaṃ na syādaśeṣakarmaṇāṃ ca nivṛttirna prāpnotīti | ucyate |
units.translation: An objection: “If you reject an injunction to repeated contemplation, the highest renunciant’s way of life will be unscriptural, like the practices of Buddhists and others. Then there can be no ‘fallen’ person who has attained the path, and the cessation of all action cannot follow.” The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 408
units.translation: “An injunction has also been accepted for understanding the meaning of ‘thou’;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.126
units.translation: without it, those faults would not arise either, since they have no basis.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Chapter colophon
units.translation: [End of the third chapter.]

units.label: Chapter heading
units.translation: Now begins the fourth chapter.

units.label: Text 2
units.translation: “What was explained clearly and at length in the earlier chapters,

units.label: Verse 4.1
units.translation: I will now state in brief, for the understanding of those who seek ease.”

units.label: Text 4
units.translation: “When a subject is taught briefly and at length, people of lesser and greater understanding

units.label: Verse 4.2
units.translation: take it into the mind; for that reason it is taught in both ways.”

units.label: Text 6
units.translation: “In this world, the Self and not-Self are established through perception and other means of knowledge;

units.label: Verse 4.3
units.translation: yet everywhere the not-Self depends on the Self as its ground.”

units.label: Text 8
units.translation: “The not-Selfhood of what is distinct from the body is self-evident;

units.label: Verse 4.4
units.translation: the knower too is taken to be the Self, but doubt arises between them.”

units.label: Text 10
units.translation: “Having learned their distinctive properties, the wise person reasons from them, as from smoke to fire,

units.label: Verse 4.5
units.translation: and thus recognizes the body, intellect and the rest as not-Self.”

units.label: Text 12
units.translation: “For external objects there is the thought ‘this’; for the knower, the thought ‘I.’

units.label: Verse 4.6
units.deva: द्वयं दृष्टं यतो देहे तेनायं मुह्यते जनः ॥ ६॥
units.iast: dvayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yato dehe tenāyaṃ muhyate janaḥ || 6||
units.translation: Since both are seen in the body, people are confused.”

units.label: Text 14
units.deva: केन पुनर्न्यायेनात्मानात्मनोरश्वमहिषयोरिव विभागः क्रियत इति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: kena punarnyāyenātmānātmanoraśvamahiṣayoriva vibhāgaḥ kriyata iti | ucyate |
units.translation: By what reasoning can the Self be distinguished from the not-Self, as a horse from a buffalo? The answer:

units.label: Text 15
units.translation: “We have already explained the reasoning that distinguishes Self from not-Self.

units.label: Verse 4.7
units.translation: Using it, one should set aside the meaning of ‘this’; whatever remains as ‘I’

units.label: Text 17
units.translation: one should know from ‘you are that’ as the ever-present witness of being and nonbeing,

units.label: Verse 4.8
units.translation: immediately inward and not an external object, O sage.”

units.label: Text 19
units.deva: उच्यतां तर्हि कया तु परिपाय्या वाक्यार्थं वेत्तीति ।
units.iast: ucyatāṃ tarhi kayā tu paripāyyā vākyārthaṃ vettīti |
units.translation: Then by what method does one understand the sentence meaning?

units.label: Text 20
units.translation: The answer: through agreement and difference.

units.label: Text 21
units.translation: “Having given up the entire meaning of ‘this,’ one thinks, ‘I too have been given up’,

units.label: Verse 4.9
units.translation: because I do not know my own Self as distinct from the not-Self.”

units.label: Text 23
units.deva: अथ शरीरादिबुद्धिपर्यन्तः स सर्वोऽनात्मैवेति प्रमाणाद्विनिश्चित्य किमिति बुभुत्सातो नोपरमते । शृणु ।
units.iast: atha śarīrādibuddhiparyantaḥ sa sarvo'nātmaiveti pramāṇādviniścitya kimiti bubhutsāto noparamate | śṛṇu |
units.translation: If, on the evidence, one has determined that everything from the body through the intellect is not-Self, why does the desire to know not cease? Listen:

units.label: Text 24
units.translation: “The desire to know remains unended because the cause of inwardness is not yet understood;

units.label: Verse 4.10
units.translation: the person’s mind wavers and is deluded, like one made of the elements.”

units.label: Text 26
units.deva: अविलुप्तविज्ञानात्मन आत्मत्वादेव नित्यसान्निध्याद्बुभुत्सुः किमिति न प्रतिपद्यत इति। यस्मात् ।
units.iast: aviluptavijñānātmana ātmatvādeva nityasānnidhyādbubhutsuḥ kimiti na pratipadyata iti| yasmāt |
units.translation: Why does the seeker not recognize the Self, though awareness remains undiminished and is always present? Because:

units.label: Text 27
units.translation: “By the very means through which one formerly saw the Self, one now regards it as not-Self;

units.label: Verse 4.11
units.translation: one seeks to know, through familiar means of knowledge, the very Seer of seeing.”

units.label: Text 29
units.translation: Why does one not see the Self as one sees not-Self through outward-directed thoughts that savor sound and the rest? The answer:

units.label: Text 30
units.translation: “The eye does not see sound, because sound is not of its nature;

units.label: Verse 4.12
units.translation: in the same way, sight formed of the physical elements cannot fully see the Self.”

units.label: Text 32
units.translation: The reason it is not seen has so far been explained from the nature of perception and the other means of knowledge.

units.label: Text 33
units.translation: Now the denial is explained from the nature of the object of knowledge:

units.label: Text 34
units.translation: “The Self is the constant witness of thousands of changes in the intellect, which are taken up and set aside;

units.label: Verse 4.13
units.translation: because it is inward, the ‘I’-thought does not see it.”

units.label: Text 36
units.translation: Where does this discriminating understanding occur—in the Self or in the not-Self? And what follows from either answer?

units.label: Text 37
units.translation: If it occurs in the Self, seeing not-Self contradicts the Self’s changelessness;

units.label: Text 38
units.translation: if in the not-Self, that too is unconscious, so how could discrimination belong to it? The reply is:

units.label: Text 39
units.translation: As already resolved by the statement “burner and burned can be in one place,”

units.label: Text 40
units.translation: “this discrimination occurs in the intellect: it distinguishes the Self from what is not-Self.”

units.label: Verse 4.14
units.translation: “It acts on the intellect alone, as fruit is said to act on a banana plant.”

units.label: Text 42
units.translation: This is the one who sees truth in what is not true.

units.label: Text 43
units.translation: “Using the lamp of inference, he sets aside all that is not-Self;

units.label: Verse 4.15
units.translation: yet with a mind relying solely on worldly bondage, he seeks the absence of that bondage.”

units.label: Text 45
units.deva: योऽयमन्वयव्यतिरेकजो विवेक आत्मानात्मविभागलक्षणोऽनात्मस्थः स्थाणौ संशयावबोधवत् प्रतिपत्तव्योऽन्यथावस्तुस्वाभाव्यान्मृगतृष्णिकोदकप्रबोधववदित्यत आह ।
units.iast: yo'yamanvayavyatirekajo viveka ātmānātmavibhāgalakṣaṇo'nātmasthaḥ sthāṇau saṃśayāvabodhavat pratipattavyo'nyathāvastusvābhāvyānmṛgatṛṣṇikodakaprabodhavavadityata āha |
units.translation: The discrimination born from agreement and difference, which distinguishes Self from not-Self, occurs in the not-Self, like mistaking a post for a person. It must be understood otherwise, in keeping with the nature of the thing, as one recognizes water in a mirage. Therefore:

units.label: Text 46
units.translation: “Established in the very seed of bondage, this person seeks liberation through a thought born of it;

units.label: Verse 4.16
units.translation: like a hare, he hopes to escape death by closing his eyes.”

units.label: Text 48
units.translation: A scriptural example is offered to strengthen this point:

units.label: Text 49
units.translation: “With this meaning in view, scripture states it clearly,

units.label: Verse 4.17
units.translation: plainly saying ‘that which is before the eye’ and ‘not seen.’”

units.label: Text 51
units.translation: “Having set aside everything down to the intellect, one asks, ‘Who am I?’

units.label: Verse 4.18
units.translation: Scripture replies, ‘You are that,’ which goes beyond every means of knowledge.”

units.label: Text 53
units.translation: This is a brief statement of the meaning of the first three chapters.

units.label: Text 54
units.translation: Although this Vedānta teaching is reasonable and can be gained through the grace of scripture and teacher, some faithful people do not understand it, because its nature is self-established and depends on nothing else.

units.label: Text 55
units.translation: To gather their understanding, an example accepted as authoritative is offered:

units.label: Text 56
units.translation: “The revered teacher, who sought the welfare of all beings, also taught just this;

units.label: Verse 4.19
units.translation: in this way he made the point we have stated perfectly clear.”

units.label: Text 58
units.deva: किं परमात्मन उपदेश उतापरमात्मन इति । किं चातः ।
units.iast: kiṃ paramātmana upadeśa utāparamātmana iti | kiṃ cātaḥ |
units.translation: Is the teaching addressed to the Supreme Self or to the individual self? What follows?

units.label: Text 59
units.deva: यदि परमात्मनस्तस्योपदेशमन्तरेणैव मुक्तत्वान्निरर्थक उपदेशः । अथापरमात्मनस्तस्यापि स्वत एव संसारस्वभावत्वान्निष्फल उपदेशः । एवमुभयत्रापि दोषवत्त्वादत आह ।
units.iast: yadi paramātmanastasyopadeśamantareṇaiva muktatvānnirarthaka upadeśaḥ | athāparamātmanastasyāpi svata eva saṃsārasvabhāvatvānniṣphala upadeśaḥ | evamubhayatrāpi doṣavattvādata āha |
units.translation: If to the Supreme Self, the teaching is pointless because that Self is already free; if to the individual, the teaching is fruitless because that self is by nature bound. Since either view has a fault, the author says:

units.label: Text 60
units.translation: “If scripture spoke of the two without distinguishing them, it would be caught in that same confusion”

units.label: Verse 4.20
units.translation: —this position is taken up and refuted below.

units.label: Text 62
units.translation: In fact, “you are that” is taught to one who, through confusion, fails to distinguish the Self that is already distinct by nature.

units.label: Text 63
units.translation: “This statement is meaningful for one who knows the difference between ‘you’ and ‘I’;

units.label: Verse 4.21
units.translation: to one who does not know it, the words are like singing to the deaf.”

units.label: Text 65
units.deva: तस्य च युष्मदस्मद्विभागविज्ञानस्य का युक्तिरुपायभावं प्रतिपद्यते । शृणु ।
units.iast: tasya ca yuṣmadasmadvibhāgavijñānasya kā yuktirupāyabhāvaṃ pratipadyate | śṛṇu |
units.translation: What reasoning or method establishes knowledge of the distinction between ‘you’ and ‘I’? Listen:

units.label: Text 66
units.translation: “Agreement and difference are the reasoning for the meaning of a thing and of a word;

units.label: Verse 4.22
units.translation: here they alone establish what is meant by ‘I.’”

units.label: Text 68
units.translation: How are these two forms of reasoning applied? The author says:

units.label: Text 69
units.translation: “In deep sleep I did not see even the slightest thing other than this;

units.label: Verse 4.23
units.deva: न वारयति दृष्टिं स्वां प्रत्ययं तु निषेधति " ॥ २३॥
units.iast: na vārayati dṛṣṭiṃ svāṃ pratyayaṃ tu niṣedhati " || 23||
units.translation: this does not deny my own awareness, only the mental cognition.”

units.label: Text 71
units.translation: “When the word’s ordinary meaning has been understood from scripture and common usage,

units.label: Verse 4.24
units.translation: scripture says ‘you are that’ to remove the listener’s delusion.”

units.label: Text 73
units.deva: तत्र त्वमिति पदं यत्र लक्षणया वर्तते सोऽर्थ उच्यते ।
units.iast: tatra tvamiti padaṃ yatra lakṣaṇayā vartate so'rtha ucyate |
units.translation: Here the meaning expressed figuratively by the word “thou” is now stated:

units.label: Text 74
units.translation: “The essential meaning of the word ‘I’ is the light within, the innermost Self;

units.label: Verse 4.25
units.translation: that alone is stated as ‘you are real’; its fruit is liberation.”

units.label: Text 76
units.translation: Here is another example of reasoning by agreement and difference:

units.label: Text 77
units.translation: “A hand, once cut off and discarded, no longer serves to distinguish the person;

units.label: Verse 4.26
units.translation: in the same way, whatever remains after each [attribute] is set aside may be used to distinguish the Self.”

units.label: Text 79
units.translation: “All these attributes are like fine ornaments;

units.label: Verse 4.27
units.translation: once known as superimposed by ignorance, they are seen to be absent in the Self.”

units.label: Text 81
units.translation: “Every attribute is therefore like the discarded hand;

units.label: Verse 4.28
units.translation: knowing this, the wise are free of every attribute, since all are not-Self.”

units.label: Text 83
units.translation: “The knower alone is always to be recognized as the Self; the known is to be set aside.

units.label: Verse 4.29
units.translation: Whatever can be grasped as ‘I’ is like a limb that has been removed.”

units.label: Text 85
units.translation: “Because it is seen, the ‘I’-thought is not a property of the Self, like a pot;

units.label: Verse 4.30
units.translation: the other thoughts are likewise known, and their defects do not stain the Self, which is pure.”

units.label: Text 87
units.translation: This gathers together all the reasoning:

units.label: Text 88
units.translation: “Knowledge of being ever free arises from the sentence, not from anything else.

units.label: Verse 4.31
units.translation: Understanding the sentence meaning, too, is preceded by recalling the meanings of its words.

units.label: Text 90
units.translation: Through agreement and difference the meanings of the words are surely recalled;

units.label: Verse 4.32
units.translation: in this way one recognizes the sorrowless, actionless Self.”

units.label: Text 92
units.translation: “From sentences such as ‘Being alone was this,’ knowledge becomes especially clear,

units.label: Verse 4.33
units.translation: just as the sentence ‘You are the tenth’ does; so too regarding the inward Self.”

units.label: Text 94
units.translation: Here is an example of someone who has fallen into error:

units.label: Text 95
units.translation: “Having lost count by miscounting the nine, a person does not see himself as the tenth,

units.label: Verse 4.34
units.translation: and yet longs to know his own self, which completes the ten.”

units.label: Text 97
units.translation: “With sight blinded by ignorance and understanding stolen by desire,

units.label: Verse 4.35
units.translation: he does not see the distinct witnessing Self, just as the man fails to see that he is the tenth.”

units.label: Text 99
units.translation: How, then, is this person, whose vision is veiled by ignorance, awakened? The author says:

units.label: Text 100
units.translation: “Just as a dreamer is awakened by the cause of waking,

units.label: Verse 4.36
units.deva: करणं कर्म कर्तारं स्वाप्नं नैवेक्षते स्वतः ॥ ३६॥
units.iast: karaṇaṃ karma kartāraṃ svāpnaṃ naivekṣate svataḥ || 36||
units.translation: and then sees none of the dream’s instruments, actions or agents as real,”

units.label: Text 102
units.translation: “so the one who does not know the Self is rightly awakened by scripture;

units.label: Verse 4.37
units.deva: गुरुं शास्त्रं तथा मूढं स्वात्मनोऽन्यं न पश्यति ॥ ३७॥
units.iast: guruṃ śāstraṃ tathā mūḍhaṃ svātmano'nyaṃ na paśyati || 37||
units.translation: the deluded person then sees neither teacher nor scripture as other than his own Self.”

units.label: Text 104
units.deva: स किं सकलसंसारप्रविविक्तमात्मानं वाक्यात्प्रतिपद्यत उत नेतीति । अत्र ब्रूमः । कूटस्थावगतिशेषमात्रत्वात्प्रतिपत्तेरत आह ।
units.iast: sa kiṃ sakalasaṃsārapraviviktamātmānaṃ vākyātpratipadyata uta netīti | atra brūmaḥ | kūṭasthāvagatiśeṣamātratvātpratipatterata āha |
units.translation: Does the person, then, understand from the sentence a Self entirely separate from worldly existence, or not? We answer: recognition leaves only changeless awareness. Therefore:

units.label: Text 105
units.translation: “Just as a snake imagined on a staff resolves into the staff,

units.label: Verse 4.38
units.translation: so, without doubt, the whole world resolves into ever-present awareness through the sentence.”

units.label: Text 107
units.translation: Why is this so? Because:

units.label: Text 108
units.translation: “The scripture that speaks clearly of seeing, of what is inward, unborn and undecaying,

units.label: Verse 4.39
units.translation: indicates you as without beginning, without end and boundless.”

units.label: Text 110
units.translation: Only the knowledge arising from a sentence such as “you are that” sublates the error. For:

units.label: Text 111
units.translation: “It teaches that no form other than this Self exists;

units.label: Verse 4.40
units.translation: misapprehension is the seed of both dream and waking.”

units.label: Text 113
units.translation: An example is given to strengthen this point:

units.label: Text 114
units.translation: “The waking person and the dreamer are held to effects and causes;

units.label: Verse 4.41
units.deva: प्राज्ञः कारणबद्धस्तु द्वौ तौ तुर्ये न सिध्यतः " ॥ ४१॥
units.iast: prājñaḥ kāraṇabaddhastu dvau tau turye na sidhyataḥ " || 41||
units.translation: the sleeper is held to causes, but neither is established in the Fourth.”

units.label: Text 116
units.translation: “Dream arises from misapprehension; sleep from not knowing reality.

units.label: Verse 4.42
units.translation: When both errors are ended, one attains the state called the Fourth.”

units.label: Text 118
units.translation: Here is another example from the revered teacher:

units.label: Verse 4.43
units.deva: सुषुप्ताख्यं तमोऽज्ञानं बीजं स्वप्नप्रबोधयोः । आत्मबोधप्रदग्धं स्याद्बीजं दग्धं यथाभवम् ॥ ४३॥
units.iast: suṣuptākhyaṃ tamo'jñānaṃ bījaṃ svapnaprabodhayoḥ | ātmabodhapradagdhaṃ syādbījaṃ dagdhaṃ yathābhavam || 43||
units.translation: The ignorance called deep sleep is the seed of dream and waking; burned by knowledge of the Self, it becomes like a scorched seed.

gloss.en: burned by knowledge of the Self
as it becomes; in that state

units.label: Text 122
units.translation: “In this way our revered teachers of Gauḍa and Drāviḍa have explained the point:

units.label: Verse 4.44
units.translation: the Lord, the Seer of ‘I’ and the rest, is conditioned only by ignorance.”

units.label: Text 124
units.translation: Just as the mistaken appearance has ignorance as its seed, so the failure to recognize the Self that seeds it belongs to the not-Self. The verse says:

units.label: Text 125
units.translation: “The triad ‘this is knowledge, I am the knower, this is what is known’—

units.label: Verse 4.45
units.translation: the changeless one who knows it is beyond that darkness.”

units.label: Text 127
units.deva: यत एतदेवमतस्तस्यैव बीजात्मनस्तमसश्चित्तधर्मविशिष्टस्य स्वकार्यद्वितीयाभिसंबन्धो न त्वविकारिण आत्मन इत्याह दृष्टान्तेन ।
units.iast: yata etadevamatastasyaiva bījātmanastamasaścittadharmaviśiṣṭasya svakāryadvitīyābhisaṃbandho na tvavikāriṇa ātmana ityāha dṛṣṭāntena |
units.translation: The seed-like darkness, which belongs to the mind, is connected with its changing effects and with what is other than the Self, not with the changeless Self. An example is given:

units.label: Text 128
units.translation: “As form is joined to the changing light that reveals it,

units.label: Verse 4.46
units.translation: so happiness, sorrow and the rest are joined to the changing mind.”

units.label: Text 130
units.translation: The author now shows this through agreement and difference:

units.label: Text 131
units.translation: “In deep repose, when what changes has subsided, because the Self is changeless,

units.label: Verse 4.47
units.translation: not even the slightest second thing touches the Seer.”

units.label: Text 133
units.translation: This is the Self, whose very nature is changeless awareness.

units.label: Text 134
units.translation: “As in deep sleep, so too at the ends of dream and waking:

units.label: Verse 4.48
units.translation: though it seems to see, because it is changeless it sees no second thing.”

units.label: Text 136
units.translation: “For one who knows, there is no foothold for the thoughts ‘mine’ and ‘I’,

units.label: Verse 4.49
units.translation: just as darkness cannot remain before someone holding a shining lamp.”

units.label: Text 138
units.translation: Here is an example:

units.label: Text 139
units.translation: “Before waking, the existence of any object other than the dream is established only within that dream;

units.label: Verse 4.50
units.translation: with awakening, the intellect and the rest are likewise not established apart from the Self within.”

units.label: Text 141
units.translation: The wise person, seeing within the Self the Self that is free of taking up and laying down,

units.label: Text 142
units.translation: “accepts everything and denies everything;

units.label: Verse 4.51
units.translation: acceptance is the appearance of a separate form, while denial is knowing that it is not the Self’s nature.”

units.label: Text 144
units.translation: Everything has now been explained; the author concludes:

units.label: Text 145
units.translation: “I have set out the knowledge established by all Vedānta, resting on the highest truth,

units.label: Verse 4.52
units.translation: which removes the darkness from the understanding.”

units.label: Text 147
units.translation: This much has been taught here:

units.label: Text 148
units.translation: “There is no knower of the Self other than me, and no one ignorant apart from me.

units.label: Verse 4.53
units.translation: Whoever knows this without distinction is the highest knower of Brahman.”

units.label: Text 150
units.deva: एवमात्मानं ज्ञात्वा किं प्रवर्तितव्यमुत निवर्तितव्यमाहोस्विन्मुक्तप्रग्रहतेति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: evamātmānaṃ jñātvā kiṃ pravartitavyamuta nivartitavyamāhosvinmuktapragrahateti | ucyate |
units.translation: After knowing the Self in this way, should one act, refrain from acting, or have complete freedom to act? The answer is:

units.label: Text 151
units.translation: “Because this is not different from what is to be known, and follows the nature of the knowable,

units.label: Verse 4.54
units.deva: न प्रवृत्तिं निवृत्तिं वा कटाक्षेणापि वीक्षते ॥ ५४॥
units.iast: na pravṛttiṃ nivṛttiṃ vā kaṭākṣeṇāpi vīkṣate || 54||
units.translation: it does not even glance toward action or the cessation of action.”

units.label: Text 153
units.translation: Why is it not different from what is to be known? Because:

units.label: Text 154
units.translation: “Before knowing the Self, awareness takes external things as secondary;

units.label: Verse 4.55
units.translation: when all worldly bondage is destroyed, scriptural knowledge rests on the Self alone.”

units.label: Text 156
units.translation: One who has understood ultimate reality has no relation of dependent means to an end, since the cause of that relation has been removed. The verse says:

units.label: Text 157
units.translation: “Because true knowledge ends worldly becoming as it actually is,

units.label: Verse 4.56
units.translation: it does not undergo cessation any more than it undergoes action.”

units.label: Text 159
units.translation: “The very arising of knowledge of the Self, by itself, puts an end to all worldly becoming;

units.label: Verse 4.57
units.translation: by removing darkness alone, it leaves no further mistaken notion.”

units.label: Text 161
units.translation: “Because the Self is unrelated to place, time and the rest, which are effects of delusion,

units.label: Verse 4.58
units.translation: ignorance cannot be some separate thing that must first arise and then be burned away.”

units.label: Text 163
units.translation: “When the fire of right knowledge has once burned up delusion and all its effects,

units.label: Verse 4.59
units.translation: what further task remains for what has been sublated?”

units.label: Text 165
units.deva: वास्तवेनैव वृत्तेनाविद्यायाः प्रध्वस्तत्वान्न किंचिदवशिष्यत इत्युक्तः परिहारः । अथापरस्सांप्रदायिकः परिहारः ।
units.iast: vāstavenaiva vṛttenāvidyāyāḥ pradhvastatvānna kiṃcidavaśiṣyata ityuktaḥ parihāraḥ | athāparassāṃpradāyikaḥ parihāraḥ |
units.translation: This was the first reply: ignorance is destroyed as a real fact. Now comes another traditional reply:

units.label: Text 166
units.translation: “Even after the snake has disappeared, a person may still tremble from the snake he saw;

units.label: Verse 4.60
units.translation: so the knower of the Self may retain an effect of delusion, though all delusion is destroyed.”

units.label: Text 168
units.translation: Since the seed of action has been cut off:

units.label: Text 169
units.translation: “A tree whose root is torn out perishes by drying up;

units.label: Verse 4.61
units.translation: in the same way, for one who knows the truth of the Self, the body ends through withdrawal.”

units.label: Text 171
units.translation: The author now rejects the view that realization permits any conduct:

units.label: Text 172
units.translation: “If one who knows that duality is real may act as he pleases,

units.label: Verse 4.62
units.translation: what difference is there between the wise and dogs when they eat what is impure?”

units.label: Text 174
units.translation: Why should this not be allowed? Because:

units.label: Text 175
units.translation: “From unrighteousness comes ignorance, and from it comes heedless conduct;

units.label: Verse 4.63
units.translation: how could that be the result of virtue, when even virtue is not accepted?”

units.label: Text 177
units.translation: Rejecting heedless conduct, the Lord says:

units.label: Verse 4.64
units.translation: “The one whose every undertaking…” and “the one who sees the light…”—the all-seeing Lord [teaches this discipline].”

units.label: Text 179
units.deva: तिष्ठतु तावत्सर्वप्रवृत्तिबीजघस्मरं ज्ञानं मुमुक्ष्ववस्थायामपि न संभवति यथेष्टाचरणम् ।
units.iast: tiṣṭhatu tāvatsarvapravṛttibījaghasmaraṃ jñānaṃ mumukṣvavasthāyāmapi na saṃbhavati yatheṣṭācaraṇam |
units.translation: Set aside for now the liberated knower, whose knowledge consumes the seed of every action: even while one is still seeking liberation, heedless conduct is impossible.

units.label: Text 180
units.translation: The text says:

units.label: Text 181
units.deva: " यो हि यत्र विरक्तः स्यान्नासौ तस्मै प्रवर्तते ।
units.iast: " yo hi yatra viraktaḥ syānnāsau tasmai pravartate |
units.translation: “One who is dispassionate toward a thing does not pursue it;

units.label: Verse 4.65
units.translation: being dispassionate toward all three worlds, what would a seeker of liberation strive for here?”

units.label: Text 183
units.translation: An example is given:

units.label: Text 184
units.translation: “Even when tormented by hunger, a person does not wish to eat poison;

units.label: Verse 4.66
units.translation: one who knows that sweet food ends thirst, and is not deluded, longs for that.”

units.label: Text 186
units.deva: यतोऽवगतपरमार्थतत्त्वस्य यथेष्टाचरणं न मनागपि घटते मुमुक्षुत्वेऽपि च तस्मात् ।
units.iast: yato'vagataparamārthatattvasya yatheṣṭācaraṇaṃ na manāgapi ghaṭate mumukṣutve'pi ca tasmāt |
units.translation: Because heedless conduct cannot occur even slightly for one who knows ultimate reality, or even for one seeking liberation:

units.label: Text 187
units.translation: “Attachment is a sign of ignorance in the fields where the mind ranges;

units.label: Verse 4.67
units.deva: कुतः शाड्वलता तस्य यस्याग्निः कोटरे तरोः ॥ ६७॥
units.iast: kutaḥ śāḍvalatā tasya yasyāgniḥ koṭare taroḥ || 67||
units.translation: how could grass grow on a tree whose hollow is filled with fire?”

units.label: Text 189
units.translation: How does this knowledge of the Self, which fulfills every human aim, arise? The answer:

units.label: Text 190
units.translation: “Knowledge arises in one established in humility and the other virtues, and equipped with means such as freedom from hatred;

units.label: Verse 4.68
units.translation: it does not arise in a mind turned outward.”

units.label: Text 192
units.deva: उत्पन्न आत्मविज्ञाने किमविद्याकार्यत्वात्प्रवृत्तिवन्निवृत्त्यात्मकामानित्वदयो निवर्तन्त उत नेति । नेति ब्रूमः । किं कारणम् । निवृत्तिशास्त्राविरुद्धस्वाभाव्यात्परमात्मनो न तु नियोगवशात् । कथं तर्हि । शृणु ।
units.iast: utpanna ātmavijñāne kimavidyākāryatvātpravṛttivannivṛttyātmakāmānitvadayo nivartanta uta neti | neti brūmaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam | nivṛttiśāstrāviruddhasvābhāvyātparamātmano na tu niyogavaśāt | kathaṃ tarhi | śṛṇu |
units.translation: When knowledge of the Self has arisen, do humility and the other qualities, which take the form of withdrawal, cease as effects of ignorance, like activity? We say no. Why? The Supreme Self naturally accords with the teaching of renunciation; these qualities do not arise from an injunction. How, then? Listen:

units.label: Text 193
units.translation: “For one awakened to the Self, qualities such as freedom from hatred

units.label: Verse 4.69
units.translation: arise effortlessly; they are not practices to be cultivated as means.”

units.label: Text 195
units.translation: Because this is so:

units.label: Text 196
units.translation: “One who wishes to study this treatise should diligently cultivate humility and the other means;

units.label: Verse 4.70
units.translation: one should not behave badly, for this teaching accords with the nature of the inward Self.”

units.label: Text 198
units.translation: This treatise must not be given to:

units.label: Text 199
units.translation: “One who is not dispassionate toward worldly existence, or who has not cast aside desire,

units.label: Verse 4.71
units.translation: or to one unfit to enter into the meaning of Vedānta.”

units.label: Text 201
units.translation: “One who has properly known what was taught has nothing further left to know;

units.label: Verse 4.72
units.translation: one should therefore not imagine this knowledge while action still remains unremoved.”

units.label: Text 203
units.translation: “Renunciants who have laid aside all action, whose minds are turned inward,

units.label: Verse 4.73
units.translation: desireless and peaceful, know this teaching as it has been set out.”

units.label: Text 205
units.deva: श्रीमच्छङ्करपादपद्मयुगलं संसेव्य लब्ध्वोचिवान् ज्ञानं पारमहंस्यमेतदमलं स्वान्तान्धकारापनुत् ।
units.iast: śrīmacchaṅkarapādapadmayugalaṃ saṃsevya labdhvocivān jñānaṃ pāramahaṃsyametadamalaṃ svāntāndhakārāpanut |
units.translation: “Having served the twin lotus feet of the blessed Śaṅkara, I received this pure knowledge of the highest renunciation, which removes the darkness of the heart.

units.label: Verse 4.74
units.deva: मा भूदत्र विरोधिनी मतिरतः सद्भिः परीक्ष्यं बुधैः सर्वत्रैव विशुद्धये मतमिदं सन्तः परं कारणम् ॥७४॥
units.iast: mā bhūdatra virodhinī matirataḥ sadbhiḥ parīkṣyaṃ budhaiḥ sarvatraiva viśuddhaye matamidaṃ santaḥ paraṃ kāraṇam ||74||
units.translation: Let no contrary view arise here; let wise and good people examine this teaching for the sake of purity everywhere. The good are its highest cause.”

units.label: Text 207
units.translation: “The sound teaching of great souls shines pure, like the sun to those who see by night;

units.label: Verse 4.75
units.translation: for minds made clear, it shines like a great treasure to one whose thirst has been quenched.”

units.label: Text 209
units.deva: विष्णोः पादानुगां यां निखिलभवनुदं शंकरोऽवापयोगात् सर्वज्ञं ब्रह्मसंस्थं मुनिगणसहितं सम्यगभ्यर्च्यभक्तया ।
units.iast: viṣṇoḥ pādānugāṃ yāṃ nikhilabhavanudaṃ śaṃkaro'vāpayogāt sarvajñaṃ brahmasaṃsthaṃ munigaṇasahitaṃ samyagabhyarcyabhaktayā |
units.translation: “Śaṅkara attained through yoga the knowledge that follows Viṣṇu’s path and removes all worldly becoming. I worshipped with devotion the all-knowing sage, established in Brahman, together with the company of sages.

units.label: Verse 4.76
units.deva: विद्यां गङ्गामिवाहं प्रवरगुणनिधेः प्राप्य वेदान्तदीप्तां कारुण्यात्तामवोचं जनिमृतिनिवहध्वस्तये दुःखितेभ्यः ॥ ७६॥
units.iast: vidyāṃ gaṅgāmivāhaṃ pravaraguṇanidheḥ prāpya vedāntadīptāṃ kāruṇyāttāmavocaṃ janimṛtinivahadhvastaye duḥkhitebhyaḥ || 76||
units.translation: Receiving from that treasure of excellent qualities the knowledge that flows like the Gaṅgā and illumines Vedānta, I have spoken it out of compassion for the suffering, to end the multitude of births and deaths.”

units.label: Text 211
units.deva: वेदान्तोदरवर्ति भास्वदमलं ध्वान्तच्छिदस्मद्धियो दिव्यं ज्ञानमतीद्रियेऽपिविषये व्याहन्यते न क्वचित् ।
units.iast: vedāntodaravarti bhāsvadamalaṃ dhvāntacchidasmaddhiyo divyaṃ jñānamatīdriye'piviṣaye vyāhanyate na kvacit |
units.translation: “This pure, radiant knowledge, dwelling in the heart of Vedānta and removing the darkness of our understanding, concerns a supersensible truth, yet is never obstructed.

units.label: Verse 4.77
units.deva: यो नो न्यायशलाकयैव निखिलं संसारबीजं तमः प्रोत्सार्याविरकार्षीद्गुरुगुरुः पूज्याय तस्मै नमः ॥ ७७॥
units.iast: yo no nyāyaśalākayaiva nikhilaṃ saṃsārabījaṃ tamaḥ protsāryāvirakārṣīdguruguruḥ pūjyāya tasmai namaḥ || 77||
units.translation: We bow to that revered teacher of teachers, who, solely through the rod of reasoning, drove away the darkness that is the seed of all worldly bondage and revealed the truth.”

units.label: Text 213
units.translation: “This account of the connections between the verses is skillfully given for each verse;

units.label: Verse 4.78
units.translation: one who knows it will surely have explained the Naiṣkarmyasiddhi correctly.”

units.label: Chapter colophon
units.translation: [End of the fourth chapter.]

wordGlossCoverage.note: All 100 verses of Adhyāya 1 and verses 2.1–2.20, plus verses 3.114, 3.123, and 4.43, have complete glosses. The remaining 300 numbered verses and prose commentary passages still need separate glosses.

translationCredit: Original English translation for the complete text; original literal readings and token-by-token glosses for texts 1.2–1.4.
